__label__MELVILLE and how nobly it raises our conceit of the mighty misty monster to behold him solemnly sailing through a calm tropical sea his vast mild head overhung by a canopy of vapour engendered by his incommunicable contemplations and that vapour as you will sometimes see it glorified by a rainbow as if heaven itself had put its seal upon his thoughts
__label__MELVILLE for dye see rainbows do not visit the clear air they only irradiate vapour

__label__MELVILLE doubts of all things earthly and intuitions of some things heavenly this combination makes neither believer nor infidel but makes a man who regards them both with equal eye
__label__MELVILLE other poets have warbled the praises of the soft eye of the antelope and the lovely plumage of the bird that never alights less celestial i celebrate a tail
__label__MELVILLE reckoning the largest sized sperm whales tail to begin at that point of the trunk where it tapers to about the girth of a man it comprises upon its upper surface alone an area of at least fifty square feet
__label__MELVILLE the compact round body of its root expands into two broad firm flat palms or flukes gradually shoaling away to less than an inch in thickness

__label__MELVILLE the fibres in the upper and lower layers are long and horizontal those of the middle one very short and running crosswise between the outside layers
__label__MELVILLE this triune structure as much as anything else imparts power to the tail

__label__MELVILLE such is the subtle elasticity of the organ i treat of that whether wielded in sport or in earnest or in anger whatever be the mood it be in its flexions are invariably marked by exceeding grace

__label__MELVILLE in man or fish wriggling is a sign of inferiority

__label__MELVILLE but still driving on in the wake of the whales at length they seemed abating their speed gradually the ship neared them and the wind now dying away word was passed to spring to the boats
__label__MELVILLE but no sooner did the herd by some presumed wonderful instinct of the sperm whale become notified of the three keels that were after them though as yet a mile in their rear than they rallied again and forming in close ranks and battalions so that their spouts all looked like flashing lines of stacked bayonets moved on with redoubled velocity
__label__MELVILLE stripped to our shirts and drawers we sprang to the white ash and after several hours pulling were almost disposed to renounce the chase when a general pausing commotion among the whales gave animating token that they were now at last under the influence of that strange perplexity of inert irresolution which when the fishermen perceive it in the whale they say he is gallied
__label__MELVILLE the compact martial columns in which they had been hitherto rapidly and steadily swimming were now broken up in one measureless rout and like king porus elephants in the indian battle with alexander they seemed going mad with consternation
__label__MELVILLE in all directions expanding in vast irregular circles and aimlessly swimming hither and thither by their short thick spoutings they plainly betrayed their distraction of panic
__label__MELVILLE this was still more strangely evinced by those of their number who completely paralysed as it were helplessly floated like water logged dismantled ships on the sea
__label__MELVILLE had these leviathans been but a flock of simple sheep pursued over the pasture by three fierce wolves they could not possibly have evinced such excessive dismay
__label__MELVILLE but this occasional timidity is characteristic of almost all herding creatures
__label__MELVILLE though banding together in tens of thousands the lion maned buffaloes of the west have fled before a solitary horseman
__label__MELVILLE witness too all human beings how when herded together in the sheepfold of a theatres pit they will at the slightest alarm of fire rush helter skelter for the outlets crowding trampling jamming and remorselessly dashing each other to death
__label__MELVILLE best therefore withhold any amazement at the strangely gallied whales before us for there is no folly of the beasts of the earth which is not infinitely outdone by the madness of men
__label__MELVILLE though many of the whales as has been said were in violent motion yet it is to be observed that as a whole the herd neither advanced nor retreated but collectively remained in one place
__label__MELVILLE as is customary in those cases the boats at once separated each making for some one lone whale on the outskirts of the shoal
__label__MELVILLE in about three minutes time queequegs harpoon was flung the stricken fish darted blinding spray in our faces and then running away with us like light steered straight for the heart of the herd
__label__MELVILLE though such a movement on the part of the whale struck under such circumstances is in no wise unprecedented and indeed is almost always more or less anticipated yet does it present one of the more perilous vicissitudes of the fishery
__label__MELVILLE for as the swift monster drags you deeper and deeper into the frantic shoal you bid adieu to circumspect life and only exist in a delirious throb

__label__MELVILLE but not a bit daunted queequeg steered us manfully now sheering off from this monster directly across our route in advance now edging away from that whose colossal flukes were suspended overhead while all the time starbuck stood up in the bows lance in hand pricking out of our way whatever whales he could reach by short darts for there was no time to make long ones
__label__MELVILLE nor were the oarsmen quite idle though their wonted duty was now altogether dispensed with

__label__MELVILLE cried a second to another which close to our gunwale seemed calmly cooling himself with his own fan like extremity
__label__MELVILLE all whaleboats carry certain curious contrivances originally invented by the nantucket indians called druggs
__label__MELVILLE two thick squares of wood of equal size are stoutly clenched together so that they cross each others grain at right angles a line of considerable length is then attached to the middle of this block and the other end of the line being looped it can in a moment be fastened to a harpoon
__label__MELVILLE it is chiefly among gallied whales that this drugg is used
__label__MELVILLE for then more whales are close round you than you can possibly chase at one time

__label__MELVILLE so that when at last the jerking harpoon drew out and the towing whale sideways vanished then with the tapering force of his parting momentum we glided between two whales into the innermost heart of the shoal as if from some mountain torrent we had slid into a serene valley lake
__label__MELVILLE here the storms in the roaring glens between the outermost whales were heard but not felt

__label__MELVILLE and still in the distracted distance we beheld the tumults of the outer concentric circles and saw successive pods of whales eight or ten in each swiftly going round and round like multiplied spans of horses in a ring and so closely shoulder to shoulder that a titanic circus rider might easily have over arched the middle ones and so have gone round on their backs
__label__MELVILLE owing to the density of the crowd of reposing whales more immediately surrounding the embayed axis of the herd no possible chance of escape was at present afforded us

__label__MELVILLE at any rate though indeed such a test at such a time might be deceptive spoutings might be discovered from our low boat that seemed playing up almost from the rim of the horizon

__label__MELVILLE floating on their sides the mothers also seemed quietly eyeing us

__label__MELVILLE the waif is a pennoned pole two or three of which are carried by every boat and which when additional game is at hand are inserted upright into the floating body of a dead whale both to mark its place on the sea and also as token of prior possession should the boats of any other ship draw near
__label__MELVILLE the result of this lowering was somewhat illustrative of that sagacious saying in the fishery the more whales the less fish

__label__MELVILLE the previous chapter gave account of an immense body or herd of sperm whales and there was also then given the probable cause inducing those vast aggregations
__label__MELVILLE now though such great bodies are at times encountered yet as must have been seen even at the present day small detached bands are occasionally observed embracing from twenty to fifty individuals each
__label__MELVILLE such bands are known as schools
__label__MELVILLE they generally are of two sorts those composed almost entirely of females and those mustering none but young vigorous males or bulls as they are familiarly designated

__label__MELVILLE the contrast between this ottoman and his concubines is striking because while he is always of the largest leviathanic proportions the ladies even at full growth are not more than one third of the bulk of an average sized male

__label__MELVILLE it is very curious to watch this harem and its lord in their indolent ramblings

__label__MELVILLE you meet them on the line in time for the full flower of the equatorial feeding season having just returned perhaps from spending the summer in the northern seas and so cheating summer of all unpleasant weariness and warmth
__label__MELVILLE by the time they have lounged up and down the promenade of the equator awhile they start for the oriental waters in anticipation of the cool season there and so evade the other excessive temperature of the year
__label__MELVILLE when serenely advancing on one of these journeys if any strange suspicious sights are seen my lord whale keeps a wary eye on his interesting family
__label__MELVILLE should any unwarrantably pert young leviathan coming that way presume to draw confidentially close to one of the ladies with what prodigious fury the bashaw assails him and chases him away
__label__MELVILLE high times indeed if unprincipled young rakes like him are to be permitted to invade the sanctity of domestic bliss though do what the bashaw will he cannot keep the most notorious lothario out of his bed for alas
__label__MELVILLE all fish bed in common

__label__MELVILLE but supposing the invader of domestic bliss to betake himself away at the first rush of the harems lord then is it very diverting to watch that lord

__label__MELVILLE for like certain other omnivorous roving lovers that might be named my lord whale has no taste for the nursery however much for the bower and so being a great traveller he leaves his anonymous babies all over the world every baby an exotic
__label__MELVILLE in good time nevertheless as the ardour of youth declines as years and dumps increase as reflection lends her solemn pauses in short as a general lassitude overtakes the sated turk then a love of ease and virtue supplants the love for maidens our ottoman enters upon the impotent repentant admonitory stage of life forswears disbands the harem and grown to an exemplary sulky old soul goes about all alone among the meridians and parallels saying his prayers and warning each young leviathan from his amorous errors
__label__MELVILLE now as the harem of whales is called by the fishermen a school so is the lord and master of that school technically known as the schoolmaster
__label__MELVILLE it is therefore not in strict character however admirably satirical that after going to school himself he should then go abroad inculcating not what he learned there but the folly of it
__label__MELVILLE his title schoolmaster would very naturally seem derived from the name bestowed upon the harem itself but some have surmised that the man who first thus entitled this sort of ottoman whale must have read the memoirs of vidocq and informed himself what sort of a country schoolmaster that famous frenchman was in his younger days and what was the nature of those occult lessons he inculcated into some of his pupils
__label__MELVILLE the same secludedness and isolation to which the schoolmaster whale betakes himself in his advancing years is true of all aged sperm whales
__label__MELVILLE almost universally a lone whale as a solitary leviathan is called proves an ancient one
__label__MELVILLE like venerable moss bearded daniel boone he will have no one near him but nature herself and her he takes to wife in the wilderness of waters and the best of wives she is though she keeps so many moody secrets
__label__MELVILLE the schools composing none but young and vigorous males previously mentioned offer a strong contrast to the harem schools
__label__MELVILLE for while those female whales are characteristically timid the young males or forty barrel bulls as they call them are by far the most pugnacious of all leviathans and proverbially the most dangerous to encounter excepting those wondrous grey headed grizzled whales sometimes met and these will fight you like grim fiends exasperated by a penal gout
__label__MELVILLE the forty barrel bull schools are larger than the harem schools
__label__MELVILLE like a mob of young collegians they are full of fight fun and wickedness tumbling round the world at such a reckless rollicking rate that no prudent underwriter would insure them any more than he would a riotous lad at yale or harvard
__label__MELVILLE they soon relinquish this turbulence though and when about three fourths grown break up and separately go about in quest of settlements that is harems

__label__MELVILLE say you strike a forty barrel bull poor devil
__label__MELVILLE all his comrades quit him
__label__MELVILLE but strike a member of the harem school and her companions swim around her with every token of concern sometimes lingering so near her and so long as themselves to fall a prey
__label__MELVILLE the allusion to the waif and waif poles in the last chapter but one necessitates some account of the laws and regulations of the whale fishery of which the waif may be deemed the grand symbol and badge
__label__MELVILLE it frequently happens that when several ships are cruising in company a whale may be struck by one vessel then escape and be finally killed and captured by another vessel and herein are indirectly comprised many minor contingencies all partaking of this one grand feature
__label__MELVILLE for example after a weary and perilous chase and capture of a whale the body may get loose from the ship by reason of a violent storm and drifting far away to leeward be retaken by a second whaler who in a calm snugly tows it alongside without risk of life or line
__label__MELVILLE thus the most vexatious and violent disputes would often arise between the fishermen were there not some written or unwritten universal undisputed law applicable to all cases
__label__MELVILLE perhaps the only formal whaling code authorized by legislative enactment was that of holland
__label__MELVILLE it was decreed by the states general in ad 1695
__label__MELVILLE but though no other nation has ever had any written whaling law yet the american fishermen have been their own legislators and lawyers in this matter
__label__MELVILLE they have provided a system which for terse comprehensiveness surpasses justinians pandects and the by laws of the chinese society for the suppression of meddling with other peoples business
__label__MELVILLE yes these laws might be engraven on a queen annes farthing or the barb of a harpoon and worn round the neck so small are they
__label__MELVILLE i
__label__MELVILLE a fast fish belongs to the party fast to it
__label__MELVILLE ii
__label__MELVILLE a loose fish is fair game for anybody who can soonest catch it
__label__MELVILLE but what plays the mischief with this masterly code is the admirable brevity of it which necessitates a vast volume of commentaries to expound it
__label__MELVILLE first what is a fast fish
__label__MELVILLE alive or dead a fish is technically fast when it is connected with an occupied ship or boat by any medium at all controllable by the occupant or occupants a mast an oar a nine inch cable a telegraph wire or a strand of cobweb it is all the same
__label__MELVILLE likewise a fish is technically fast when it bears a waif or any other recognised symbol of possession so long as the party waifing it plainly evince their ability at any time to take it alongside as well as their intention so to do
__label__MELVILLE these are scientific commentaries but the commentaries of the whalemen themselves sometimes consist in hard words and harder knocks the coke upon littleton of the fist
__label__MELVILLE true among the more upright and honourable whalemen allowances are always made for peculiar cases where it would be an outrageous moral injustice for one party to claim possession of a whale previously chased or killed by another party
__label__MELVILLE but others are by no means so scrupulous
__label__MELVILLE some fifty years ago there was a curious case of whale trover litigated in england wherein the plaintiffs set forth that after a hard chase of a whale in the northern seas and when indeed they the plaintiffs had succeeded in harpooning the fish they were at last through peril of their lives obliged to forsake not only their lines but their boat itself
__label__MELVILLE ultimately the defendants the crew of another ship came up with the whale struck killed seized and finally appropriated it before the very eyes of the plaintiffs
__label__MELVILLE and when those defendants were remonstrated with their captain snapped his fingers in the plaintiffs teeth and assured them that by way of doxology to the deed he had done he would now retain their line harpoons and boat which had remained attached to the whale at the time of the seizure
__label__MELVILLE wherefore the plaintiffs now sued for the recovery of the value of their whale line harpoons and boat
__label__MELVILLE mr erskine was counsel for the defendants lord ellenborough was the judge
__label__MELVILLE in the course of the defence the witty erskine went on to illustrate his position by alluding to a recent crim
__label__MELVILLE con
__label__MELVILLE case wherein a gentleman after in vain trying to bridle his wifes viciousness had at last abandoned her upon the seas of life but in the course of years repenting of that step he instituted an action to recover possession of her
__label__MELVILLE erskine was on the other side and he then supported it by saying that though the gentleman had originally harpooned the lady and had once had her fast and only by reason of the great stress of her plunging viciousness had at last abandoned her yet abandon her he did so that she became a loose fish and therefore when a subsequent gentleman re harpooned her the lady then became that subsequent gentlemans property along with whatever harpoon might have been found sticking in her
__label__MELVILLE now in the present case erskine contended that the examples of the whale and the lady were reciprocally illustrative of each other
__label__MELVILLE these pleadings and the counter pleadings being duly heard the very learned judge in set terms decided to wit that as for the boat he awarded it to the plaintiffs because they had merely abandoned it to save their lives but that with regard to the controverted whale harpoons and line they belonged to the defendants the whale because it was a loose fish at the time of the final capture and the harpoons and line because when the fish made off with them it the fish acquired a property in those articles and hence anybody who afterwards took the fish had a right to them
__label__MELVILLE now the defendants afterwards took the fish ergo the aforesaid articles were theirs
__label__MELVILLE a common man looking at this decision of the very learned judge might possibly object to it
__label__MELVILLE but ploughed up to the primary rock of the matter the two great principles laid down in the twin whaling laws previously quoted and applied and elucidated by lord ellenborough in the above cited case these two laws touching fast fish and loose fish i say will on reflection be found the fundamentals of all human jurisprudence for notwithstanding its complicated tracery of sculpture the temple of the law like the temple of the philistines has but two props to stand on

__label__MELVILLE after this i was asked whether i desired to ship of course i said yes that is if he would allow me to enter for one cruise engaging to discharge me if i so desired at the next port
__label__MELVILLE in this way men are frequently shipped on board whalemen in the south seas
__label__MELVILLE my stipulation was acceded to and the ships articles handed me to sign
__label__MELVILLE the mate was now called below and charged to make a well man of me not let it be borne in mind that the captain felt any great compassion for me he only desired to have the benefit of my services as soon as possible
__label__MELVILLE helping me on deck the mate stretched me out on the windlass and commenced examining my limb and then doctoring it after a fashion with something from the medicine chest rolled it up in a piece of an old sail making so big a bundle that with my feet resting on the windlass i might have been taken for a sailor with the gout
__label__MELVILLE while this was going on someone removing my tappa cloak slipped on a blue frock in its place and another actuated by the same desire to make a civilized mortal of me flourished about my head a great pair lie imminent jeopardy of both ears and the certain destruction of hair and beard
__label__MELVILLE the day was now drawing to a close and as the land faded from my sight i was all alive to the change in my condition
__label__MELVILLE but how far short of our expectations is oftentimes the fulfilment of the most ardent hopes
__label__MELVILLE safe aboard of a ship so long my earnest prayer with home and friends once more in prospect i nevertheless felt weighed down by a melancholy that could not be shaken off
__label__MELVILLE it was the thought of never more seeing those who notwithstanding their desire to retain me a captive had upon the whole treated me so kindly
__label__MELVILLE i was leaving them for ever
__label__MELVILLE so unforeseen and sudden had been my escape so excited had i been through it all and so great the contrast between the luxurious repose of the valley and the wild noise and motion of a ship at sea that at times my recent adventures had all the strangeness of a dream and i could scarcely believe that the same sun now setting over a waste of waters had that very morning risen above the mountains and peered in upon me as i lay on my mat in typee
__label__MELVILLE going below into the forecastle just after dark i was inducted into a wretched bunk or sleeping box built over another
__label__MELVILLE the rickety bottoms of both were spread with several pieces of a blanket
__label__MELVILLE a battered tin can was then handed me containing about half a pint of tea so called by courtesy though whether the juice of such stalks as one finds floating therein deserves that title is a matter all shipowners must settle with their consciences
__label__MELVILLE a cube of salt beef on a hard round biscuit by way of platter was also handed up and without more ado i made a meal the salt flavour of which after the nebuchadnezzar fare of the valley was positively delicious
__label__MELVILLE while thus engaged an old sailor on a chest just under me was puffing out volumes of tobacco smoke
__label__MELVILLE my supper finished he brushed the stem of his sooty pipe against the sleeve of his frock and politely waved it toward me
__label__MELVILLE the attention was sailor like as for the nicety of the thing no man who has lived in forecastles is at all fastidious and so after a few vigorous whiffs to induce repose i turned over and tried my best to forget myself
__label__MELVILLE but in vain
__label__MELVILLE my crib instead of extending fore and aft as it should have done was placed athwart ships that is at right angles to the keel and the vessel going before the wind rolled to such a degree that every time my heels went up and my head went down i thought i was on the point of turning a somerset
__label__MELVILLE beside this there were still more annoying causes of inquietude and every once in a while a splash of water came down the open scuttle and flung the spray in my face
__label__MELVILLE at last after a sleepless night broken twice by the merciless call of the watch a peep of daylight struggled into view from above and someone came below
__label__MELVILLE it was my old friend with the pipe
__label__MELVILLE here shipmate said i help me out of this place and let me go on deck
__label__MELVILLE halloa whos that croaking
__label__MELVILLE was the rejoinder as he peered into the obscurity where i lay
__label__MELVILLE ay typee my king of the cannibals is it you i but i say my lad hows that spar of yourn
__label__MELVILLE the mate says its in a devil of a way and last night set the steward to sharpening the handsaw hope he wont have the carving of ye
__label__MELVILLE long before daylight we arrived off the bay of nukuheva and making short tacks until morning we then ran in and sent a boat ashore with the natives who had brought me to the ship
__label__MELVILLE upon its return we made sail again and stood off from the land
__label__MELVILLE there was a fine breeze and notwithstanding my bad nights rest the cool fresh air of a morning at sea was so bracing mat as soon as i breathed it my spirits rose at once
__label__MELVILLE seated upon the windlass the greater portion of the day and chatting freely with the men i learned the history of the voyage thus far and everything respecting the ship and its present condition
__label__MELVILLE these matters i will now throw together in the next chapter
__label__MELVILLE some account of the ship
__label__MELVILLE first and foremost i must give some account of the julia herself or little jule as the sailors familiarly styled her
__label__MELVILLE she was a small barque of a beautiful model something more than two hundred tons yankee built and very old
__label__MELVILLE fitted for a privateer out of a new england port during the war of 1812 she had been captured at sea by a british cruiser and after seeing all sorts of service was at last employed as a government packet in the australian seas
__label__MELVILLE being condemned however about two years previous she was purchased at auction by a house in sydney who after some slight repairs dispatched her on the present voyage
__label__MELVILLE notwithstanding the repairs she was still in a miserable plight
__label__MELVILLE the lower masts were said to be unsound the standing rigging was much worn and in some places even the bulwarks were quite rotten
__label__MELVILLE still she was tolerably tight and but little more than the ordinary pumping of a morning served to keep her free
__label__MELVILLE but all this had nothing to do with her sailing at that brave little jule plump little jule was a witch
__label__MELVILLE blow high or blow low she was always ready for the breeze and when she dashed the waves from her prow and pranced and pawed the sea you never thought of her patched sails and blistered hull
__label__MELVILLE how the fleet creature would fly before the wind
__label__MELVILLE rolling now and then to be sure but in very playfulness
__label__MELVILLE sailing to windward no gale could bow her over with spars erect she looked right up into the winds eye and so she went
__label__MELVILLE but after all little jule was not to be confided in
__label__MELVILLE lively enough and playful she was but on that very account the more to be distrusted
__label__MELVILLE who knew but that like some vivacious old mortal all at once sinking into a decline she might some dark night spring a leak and carry us all to the bottom
__label__MELVILLE however she played us no such ugly trick and therefore i wrong little jule in supposing it
__label__MELVILLE she had a free roving commission
__label__MELVILLE according to her papers she might go whither she pleased whaling sealing or anything else
__label__MELVILLE sperm whaling however was what she relied upon though as yet only two fish had been brought alongside
__label__MELVILLE the day they sailed out of sydney heads the ships company all told numbered some thirty two souls now they mustered about twenty the rest had deserted
__label__MELVILLE even the three junior mates who had headed the whaleboats were gone and of the four harpooners only one was left a wild new zealander or mowree as his countrymen are more commonly called in the pacific
__label__MELVILLE but this was not all
__label__MELVILLE more than half the seamen remaining were more or less unwell from a long sojourn in a dissipated port some of them wholly unfit for duty one or two dangerously ill and the rest managing to stand their watch though they could do but little
__label__MELVILLE the captain was a young cockney who a few years before had emigrated to australia and by some favouritism or other had procured the command of the vessel though in no wise competent
__label__MELVILLE he was essentially a landsman and though a man of education no more meant for the sea than a hairdresser
__label__MELVILLE hence everybody made fun of him
__label__MELVILLE they called him the cabin boy paper jack and half a dozen other undignified names
__label__MELVILLE in truth the men made no secret of the derision in which they held him and as for the slender gentleman himself he knew it all very well and bore himself with becoming meekness
__label__MELVILLE holding as little intercourse with them as possible he left everything to the chief mate who as the story went had been given his captain in charge
__label__MELVILLE yet despite his apparent unobtrusiveness the silent captain had more to do with the men than they thought
__label__MELVILLE in short although one of your sheepish looking fellows he had a sort of still timid cunning which no one would have suspected and which for that very reason was all the more active
__label__MELVILLE so the bluff mate who always thought he did what he pleased was occasionally made a fool of and some obnoxious measures which he carried out in spite of all growlings were little thought to originate with the dapper little fellow in nankeen jacket and white canvas pumps
__label__MELVILLE but to all appearance at least the mate had everything his own way indeed in most things this was actually the case and it was quite plain that the captain stood in awe of him
__label__MELVILLE so far as courage seamanship and a natural aptitude for keeping riotous spirits in subjection were concerned no man was better qualified for his vocation than john jermin
__label__MELVILLE he was the very beau ideal of the efficient race of short thick set men
__label__MELVILLE his hair curled in little rings of iron gray all over his round bullet head
__label__MELVILLE as for his countenance it was strongly marked deeply pitted with the small pox
__label__MELVILLE for the rest there was a fierce little squint out of one eye the nose had a rakish twist to one side while his large mouth and great white teeth looked absolutely sharkish when he laughed
__label__MELVILLE in a word no one after getting a fair look at him would ever think of improving the shape of his nose wanting in symmetry as it was
__label__MELVILLE notwithstanding his pugnacious looks however jermin had a heart as big as a bullocks that you saw at a glance
__label__MELVILLE such was our mate but he had one failing he abhorred all weak infusions and cleaved manfully to strong drink at all times he was more or less under the influence of it
__label__MELVILLE taken in moderate quantities i believe in my soul it did a man like him good brightened his eyes swept the cobwebs out of his brain and regulated his pulse
__label__MELVILLE but the worst of it was that sometimes he drank too much and a more obstreperous fellow than jermin in his cups you seldom came across
__label__MELVILLE he was always for having a fight but the very men he flogged loved him as a brother for he had such an irresistibly good natured way of knocking them down that no one could find it in his heart to bear malice against him
__label__MELVILLE so much for stout little jermin
__label__MELVILLE all english whalemen are bound by law to carry a physician who of course is rated a gentleman and lives in the cabin with nothing but his professional duties to attend to but incidentally he drinks flip and plays cards with the captain
__label__MELVILLE there was such a worthy aboard of the julia but curious to tell he lived in the forecastle with the men
__label__MELVILLE and this was the way it happened
__label__MELVILLE in the early part of the voyage the doctor and the captain lived together as pleasantly as could be
__label__MELVILLE to say nothing of many a can they drank over the cabin transom both of them had read books and one of them had travelled so their stories never flagged
__label__MELVILLE but once on a time they got into a dispute about politics and the doctor moreover getting into a rage drove home an argument with his fist and left the captain on the floor literally silenced
__label__MELVILLE this was carrying it with a high hand so he was shut up in his state room for ten days and left to meditate on bread and water and the impropriety of flying into a passion
__label__MELVILLE smarting under his disgrace he undertook a short time after his liberation to leave the vessel clandestinely at one of the islands but was brought back ignominiously and again shut up
__label__MELVILLE being set at large for the second time he vowed he would not live any longer with the captain and went forward with his chests among the sailors where he was received with open arms as a good fellow and an injured man
__label__MELVILLE i must give some further account of him for he figures largely in the narrative
__label__MELVILLE his early history like that of many other heroes was enveloped in the profoundest obscurity though he threw out hints of a patrimonial estate a nabob uncle and an unfortunate affair which sent him a roving
__label__MELVILLE all that was known however was this
__label__MELVILLE he had gone out to sydney as assistant surgeon of an emigrant ship
__label__MELVILLE on his arrival there he went back into the country and after a few months wanderings returned to sydney penniless and entered as doctor aboard of the julia
__label__MELVILLE his personal appearance was remarkable
__label__MELVILLE he was over six feet high a tower of bones with a complexion absolutely colourless fair hair and a light unscrupulous gray eye twinkling occasionally at the very devil of mischief
__label__MELVILLE among the crew he went by the name of the long doctor or more frequently still doctor long ghost
__label__MELVILLE and from whatever high estate doctor long ghost might have fallen he had certainly at some time or other spent money drunk burgundy and associated with gentlemen
__label__MELVILLE as for his learning he quoted virgil and talked of hobbs of malmsbury beside repeating poetry by the canto especially hudibras
__label__MELVILLE he was moreover a man who had seen the world
__label__MELVILLE in the easiest way imaginable he could refer to an amour he had in palermo his lion hunting before breakfast among the caffres and the quality of the coffee to be drunk in muscat and about these places and a hundred others he had more anecdotes than i can tell of
__label__MELVILLE then such mellow old songs as he sang in a voice so round and racy the real juice of sound
__label__MELVILLE how such notes came forth from his lank body was a constant marvel
__label__MELVILLE upon the whole long ghost was as entertaining a companion as one could wish and to me in the julia an absolute godsend
__label__MELVILLE further account of the julia
__label__MELVILLE owing to the absence of anything like regular discipline the vessel was in a state of the greatest uproar
__label__MELVILLE the captain having for some time past been more or less confined to the cabin from sickness was seldom seen
__label__MELVILLE the mate however was as hearty as a young lion and ran about the decks making himself heard at all hours
__label__MELVILLE bembo the new zealand harpooner held little intercourse with anybody but the mate who could talk to him freely in his own lingo
__label__MELVILLE part of his time he spent out on the bowsprit fishing for albicores with a bone hook and occasionally he waked all hands up of a dark night dancing some cannibal fandango all by himself on the forecastle
__label__MELVILLE but upon the whole he was remarkably quiet though something in his eye showed he was far from being harmless
__label__MELVILLE doctor long ghost having sent in a written resignation as the ships doctor gave himself out as a passenger for sydney and took the world quite easy
__label__MELVILLE as for the crew those who were sick seemed marvellously contented for men in their condition and the rest not displeased with the general licence gave themselves little thought of the morrow
__label__MELVILLE the julias provisions were very poor
__label__MELVILLE when opened the barrels of pork looked as if preserved in iron rust and diffused an odour like a stale ragout
__label__MELVILLE the beef was worse yet a mahogany coloured fibrous substance so tough and tasteless that i almost believed the cooks story of a horses hoof with the shoe on having been fished up out of the pickle of one of the casks
__label__MELVILLE nor was the biscuit much better nearly all of it was broken into hard little gunflints honeycombed through and through as if the worms usually infesting this article in long tropical voyages had in boring after nutriment come out at the antipodes without finding anything
__label__MELVILLE of what sailors call small stores we had but little
__label__MELVILLE tea however we had in abundance though i dare say the hong merchants never had the shipping of it
__label__MELVILLE beside this every other day we had what english seamen call shot soup great round peas polishing themselves like pebbles by rolling about in tepid water
__label__MELVILLE it was afterward told me that all our provisions had been purchased by the owners at an auction sale of condemned navy stores in sydney
__label__MELVILLE but notwithstanding the wateriness of the first course of soup and the saline flavour of the beef and pork a sailor might have made a satisfactory meal aboard of the julia had there been any side dishes a potato or two a yam or a plantain
__label__MELVILLE but there was nothing of the kind
__label__MELVILLE still there was something else which in the estimation of the men made up for all deficiencies and that was the regular allowance of pisco
__label__MELVILLE it may seem strange that in such a state of affairs the captain should be willing to keep the sea with his ship
__label__MELVILLE but the truth was that by lying in harbour he ran the risk of losing the remainder of his men by desertion and as it was he still feared that in some outlandish bay or other he might one day find his anchor down and no crew to weigh it
__label__MELVILLE with judicious officers the most unruly seamen can at sea be kept in some sort of subjection but once get them within a cables length of the land and it is hard restraining them
__label__MELVILLE it is for this reason that many south sea whalemen do not come to anchor for eighteen or twenty months on a stretch
__label__MELVILLE when fresh provisions are needed they run for the nearest land heave to eight or ten miles off and send a boat ashore to trade
__label__MELVILLE the crews manning vessels like these are for the most part villains of all nations and dyes picked up in the lawless ports of the spanish main and among the savages of the islands
__label__MELVILLE like galley slaves they are only to be governed by scourges and chains
__label__MELVILLE their officers go among them with dirk and pistol concealed but ready at a grasp
__label__MELVILLE not a few of our own crew were men of this stamp but riotous at times as they were the bluff drunken energies of jennin were just the thing to hold them in some sort of noisy subjection
__label__MELVILLE upon an emergency he flew in among them showering his kicks and cuffs right and left and creating a sensation in every direction
__label__MELVILLE and as hinted before they bore this knock down authority with great good humour
__label__MELVILLE a sober discreet dignified officer could have done nothing with them such a set would have thrown him and his dignity overboard
__label__MELVILLE matters being thus there was nothing for the ship but to keep the sea
__label__MELVILLE nor was the captain without hope that the invalid portion of his crew as well as himself would soon recover and then there was no telling what luck in the fishery might yet be in store for us
__label__MELVILLE at any rate at the time of my coming aboard the report was that captain guy was resolved upon retrieving the past and filling the vessel with oil in the shortest space possible
__label__MELVILLE with this intention we were now shaping our course for hytyhoo a village on the island of st christina one of the marquesas and so named by mendanna for the purpose of obtaining eight seamen who some weeks before had stepped ashore there from the julia
__label__MELVILLE it was supposed that by this time they must have recreated themselves sufficiently and would be glad to return to their duty
__label__MELVILLE so to hytyhoo with all our canvas spread and coquetting with the warm breezy trades we bowled along gliding up and down the long slow swells the bonettas and albicores frolicking round us
__label__MELVILLE a scene in the forecastle
__label__MELVILLE i had scarcely been aboard of the ship twenty four hours when a circumstance occurred which although noways picturesque is so significant of the state of affairs that i cannot forbear relating it
__label__MELVILLE in the first place however it must be known that among the crew was a man so excessively ugly that he went by the ironical appellation of beauty
__label__MELVILLE he was the ships carpenter and for that reason was sometimes known by his nautical cognomen of chips
__label__MELVILLE there was no absolute deformity about the man he was symmetrically ugly
__label__MELVILLE but ill favoured as he was in person beauty was none the less ugly in temper but no one could blame him his countenance had soured his heart
__label__MELVILLE now jermin and beauty were always at swords points
__label__MELVILLE the truth was the latter was the only man in the ship whom the mate had never decidedly got the better of and hence the grudge he bore him
__label__MELVILLE as for beauty he prided himself upon talking up to the mate as we shall soon see
__label__MELVILLE toward evening there was something to be done on deck and the carpenter who belonged to the watch was missing
__label__MELVILLE wheres that skulk chips
__label__MELVILLE shouted jermin down the forecastle scuttle
__label__MELVILLE taking his ease dye see down here on a chest if you want to know replied that worthy himself quietly withdrawing his pipe from his mouth
__label__MELVILLE this insolence flung the fiery little mate into a mighty rage but beauty said nothing puffing away with all the tranquillity imaginable
__label__MELVILLE here it must be remembered that never mind what may be the provocation no prudent officer ever dreams of entering a ships forecastle on a hostile visit
__label__MELVILLE if he wants to see anybody who happens to be there and refuses to come up why he must wait patiently until the sailor is willing
__label__MELVILLE the reason is this
__label__MELVILLE the place is very dark and nothing is easier than to knock one descending on the head before he knows where he is and a very long while before he ever finds out who did it
__label__MELVILLE nobody knew this better than jermin and so he contented himself with looking down the scuttle and storming
__label__MELVILLE at last beauty made some cool observation which set him half wild
__label__MELVILLE tumble on deck he then bellowed come up with you or ill jump down and make you
__label__MELVILLE the carpenter begged him to go about it at once
__label__MELVILLE no sooner said than done prudence forgotten jermin was there and by a sort of instinct had his man by the throat before he could well see him
__label__MELVILLE one of the men now made a rush at him but the rest dragged him off protesting that they should have fair play
__label__MELVILLE now come on deck shouted the mate struggling like a good fellow to hold the carpenter fast
__label__MELVILLE take me there was the dogged answer and beauty wriggled about in the nervous grasp of the other like a couple of yards of boa constrictor

__label__MELVILLE while thus occupied beauty got his arms loose and threw him over backward

__label__MELVILLE unfortunately jermin at last slipped and fell his foe seating himself on his chest and keeping him down
__label__MELVILLE now this was one of those situations in which the voice of counsel or reproof comes with peculiar unction

__label__MELVILLE but the mate said nothing in reply only foaming at the mouth and struggling to rise
__label__MELVILLE just then a thin tremor of a voice was heard from above
__label__MELVILLE it was the captain who happening to ascend to the quarter deck at the commencement of the scuffle would gladly have returned to the cabin but was prevented by the fear of ridicule
__label__MELVILLE as the din increased and it became evident that his officer was in serious trouble he thought it would never do to stand leaning over the bulwarks so he made his appearance on the forecastle resolved as his best policy to treat the matter lightly

__label__MELVILLE jermin mr jermin carpenter carpenter what are you doing down there

__label__MELVILLE cried the mate furiously

__label__MELVILLE oh

__label__MELVILLE the doctor was not far off just then

__label__MELVILLE a few moments more and jermin forced to a compromise followed after in his torn frock and scarred face looking for all the world as if he had just disentangled himself from some intricate piece of machinery
__label__MELVILLE for about half an hour both remained in the cabin where the mates rough tones were heard high above the low smooth voice of the captain
__label__MELVILLE of all his conflicts with the men this was the first in which jermin had been worsted and he was proportionably enraged
__label__MELVILLE upon going below as the steward afterward told us he bluntly informed guy that for the future he might look out for his ship himself for his part he had done with her if that was the way he allowed his officers to be treated
__label__MELVILLE after many high words the captain finally assured him that the first fitting opportunity the carpenter should be cordially flogged though as matters stood the experiment would be a hazardous one
__label__MELVILLE upon this jermin reluctantly consented to drop the matter for the present and he soon drowned all thoughts of it in a can of flip which guy had previously instructed the steward to prepare as a sop to allay his wrath
__label__MELVILLE nothing more ever came of this
__label__MELVILLE what happened at hytyhoo
__label__MELVILLE less than forty eight hours after leaving nukuheva the blue looming island of st christina greeted us from afar
__label__MELVILLE drawing near the shore the grim black spars and waspish hull of a small man of war craft crept into view the masts and yards lined distinctly against the sky
__label__MELVILLE she was riding to her anchor in the bay and proved to be a french corvette
__label__MELVILLE this pleased our captain exceedingly and coming on deck he examined her from the mizzen rigging with his glass
__label__MELVILLE his original intention was not to let go an anchor but counting upon the assistance of the corvette in case of any difficulty he now changed his mind and anchored alongside of her
__label__MELVILLE as soon as a boat could be lowered he then went off to pay his respects to the commander and moreover as we supposed to concert measures for the apprehension of the runaways
__label__MELVILLE returning in the course of twenty minutes he brought along with him two officers in undress and whiskers and three or four drunken obstreperous old chiefs one with his legs thrust into the armholes of a scarlet vest another with a pair of spurs on his heels and a third in a cocked hat and feather
__label__MELVILLE in addition to these articles they merely wore the ordinary costume of their race a slip of native cloth about the loins
__label__MELVILLE indecorous as their behaviour was these worthies turned out to be a deputation from the reverend the clergy of the island and the object of their visit was to put our ship under a rigorous taboo to prevent the disorderly scenes and facilities for desertion which would ensue were the natives men and women allowed to come off to us freely
__label__MELVILLE there was little ceremony about the matter
__label__MELVILLE the priests went aside for a moment laid their shaven old crowns together and went over a little mummery
__label__MELVILLE whereupon their leader tore a long strip from his girdle of white tappa and handed it to one of the french officers who after explaining what was to be done gave it to jermin
__label__MELVILLE the mate at once went out to the end of the flying jib boom and fastened there the mystic symbol of the ban
__label__MELVILLE this put to flight a party of girls who had been observed swimming toward us
__label__MELVILLE tossing their arms about and splashing the water like porpoises with loud cries of taboo
__label__MELVILLE taboo
__label__MELVILLE they turned about and made for the shore
__label__MELVILLE the night of our arrival the mate and the mowree were to stand watch and watch relieving each other every four hours the crew as is sometimes customary when lying at an anchor being allowed to remain all night below
__label__MELVILLE a distrust of the men however was in the present instance the principal reason for this proceeding

__label__MELVILLE jermin was frantic

__label__MELVILLE how conducive to the restoration of their shattered health would have been those delicious groves

__label__MELVILLE toward sunset a crowd was seen coming down to the water

__label__MELVILLE following them up was a shouting rabble of islanders pricking them with the points of their long spears the party from the corvette menacing them in flank with their naked cutlasses
__label__MELVILLE the bonus of a musket to the king of the bay and the promise of a tumblerful of powder for every man caught had set the whole population on their track and so successful was the hunt that not only were that mornings deserters brought back but five of those left behind on a former visit
__label__MELVILLE the natives however were the mere hounds of the chase raising the game in their coverts but leaving the securing of it to the frenchmen
__label__MELVILLE here as elsewhere the islanders have no idea of taking part in such a scuffle as ensues upon the capture of a party of desperate seamen
__label__MELVILLE the runaways were at once brought aboard and though they looked rather sulky soon came round and treated the whole affair as a frolicsome adventure
__label__MELVILLE we touch at la dominica
__label__MELVILLE fearful of spending another night at hytyhoo captain guy caused the ship to be got under way shortly after dark

__label__MELVILLE the object of this as we learned was to procure if possible several english sailors who according to the commander of the corvette had recently gone ashore there from an american whaler and were desirous of shipping aboard one of their own country vessels
__label__MELVILLE we made the land in the afternoon coming abreast of a shady glen opening from a deep bay and winding by green denies far out of sight

__label__MELVILLE roared the mate jumping up on the bulwarks and in a moment the prancing julia suddenly arrested in her course bridled her head like a steed reined in while the foam flaked under her bows
__label__MELVILLE this was the place where we expected to obtain the men so a boat was at once got in readiness to go ashore
__label__MELVILLE now it was necessary to provide a picked crew men the least likely to abscond
__label__MELVILLE after considerable deliberation on the part of the captain and mate four of the seamen were pitched upon as the most trustworthy or rather they were selected from a choice assortment of suspicious characters as being of an inferior order of rascality
__label__MELVILLE armed with cutlasses all round the natives were said to be an ugly set they were followed over the side by the invalid captain who on this occasion it seems was determined to signalize himself
__label__MELVILLE accordingly in addition to his cutlass he wore an old boarding belt in which was thrust a brace of pistols

__label__MELVILLE in a few moments they embarked again and were soon riding pertly over the waves of the bay
__label__MELVILLE all of a sudden the captain started to his feet the boat spun round and again made for the shore
__label__MELVILLE some twenty or thirty natives armed with spears which through the glass looked like reeds had just come out of the grove and were apparently shouting to the strangers not to be in such a hurry but return and be sociable
__label__MELVILLE but they were somewhat distrusted for the boat paused about its length from the beach when the captain standing up in its head delivered an address in pantomime the object of which seemed to be that the islanders should draw near
__label__MELVILLE one of them stepped forward and made answer seemingly again urging the strangers not to be diffident but beach their boat
__label__MELVILLE the captain declined tossing his arms about in another pantomime
__label__MELVILLE in the end he said something which made them shake their spears whereupon he fired a pistol among them which set the whole party running while one poor little fellow dropping his spear and clapping his hand behind him limped away in a manner which almost made me itch to get a shot at his assailant
__label__MELVILLE wanton acts of cruelty like this are not unusual on the part of sea captains landing at islands comparatively unknown
__label__MELVILLE even at the pomotu group but a days sail from tahiti the islanders coming down to the shore have several times been fired at by trading schooners passing through their narrow channels and this too as a mere amusement on the part of the ruffians
__label__MELVILLE indeed it is almost incredible the light in which many sailors regard these naked heathens
__label__MELVILLE they hardly consider them human
__label__MELVILLE but it is a curious fact that the more ignorant and degraded men are the more contemptuously they look upon those whom they deem their inferiors
__label__MELVILLE all powers of persuasion being thus lost upon these foolish savages and no hope left of holding further intercourse the boat returned to the ship
__label__MELVILLE what happened at hannamanoo
__label__MELVILLE on the other side of the island was the large and populous bay of hannamanoo where the men sought might yet be found
__label__MELVILLE but as the sun was setting by the time the boat came alongside we got our offshore tacks aboard and stood away for an offing
__label__MELVILLE about daybreak we wore and ran in and by the time the sun was well up entered the long narrow channel dividing the islands of la dominica and st christina
__label__MELVILLE on one hand was a range of steep green bluffs hundreds of feet high the white huts of the natives here and there nestling like birds nests in deep clefts gushing with verdure
__label__MELVILLE across the water the land rolled away in bright hillsides so warm and undulating that they seemed almost to palpitate in the sun
__label__MELVILLE on we swept past bluff and grove wooded glen and valley and dark ravines lighted up far inland with wild falls of water
__label__MELVILLE a fresh land breeze filled our sails the embayed waters were gentle as a lake and every wave broke with a tinkle against our coppered prow
__label__MELVILLE on gaining the end of the channel we rounded a point and came full upon the bay of hannamanoo
__label__MELVILLE this is the only harbour of any note about the island though as far as a safe anchorage is concerned it hardly deserves the title
__label__MELVILLE before we held any communication with the shore an incident occurred which may convey some further idea of the character of our crew
__label__MELVILLE having approached as near the land as we could prudently our headway was stopped and we awaited the arrival of a canoe which was coming out of the bay
__label__MELVILLE all at once we got into a strong current which swept us rapidly toward a rocky promontory forming one side of the harbour
__label__MELVILLE the wind had died away so two boats were at once lowered for the purpose of pulling the ships head round
__label__MELVILLE before this could be done the eddies were whirling upon all sides and the rock so near that it seemed as if one might leap upon it from the masthead
__label__MELVILLE notwithstanding the speechless fright of the captain and the hoarse shouts of the unappalled jennin the men handled the ropes as deliberately as possible some of them chuckling at the prospect of going ashore and others so eager for the vessel to strike that they could hardly contain themselves
__label__MELVILLE unexpectedly a countercurrent befriended us and assisted by the boats we were soon out of danger
__label__MELVILLE what a disappointment for our crew
__label__MELVILLE all their little plans for swimming ashore from the wreck and having a fine time of it for the rest of their days thus cruelly nipped in the bud
__label__MELVILLE soon after the canoe came alongside
__label__MELVILLE in it were eight or ten natives comely vivacious looking youths all gesture and exclamation the red feathers in their head bands perpetually nodding
__label__MELVILLE with them also came a stranger a renegade from christendom and humanity a white man in the south sea girdle and tattooed in the face
__label__MELVILLE a broad blue band stretched across his face from ear to ear and on his forehead was the taper figure of a blue shark nothing but fins from head to tail
__label__MELVILLE some of us gazed upon this man with a feeling akin to horror no ways abated when informed that he had voluntarily submitted to this embellishment of his countenance
__label__MELVILLE what an impress
__label__MELVILLE far worse than cains his was perhaps a wrinkle or a freckle which some of our modern cosmetics might have effaced but the blue shark was a mark indelible which all the waters of abana and pharpar rivers of damascus could never wash out
__label__MELVILLE he was an englishman lem hardy he called himself who had deserted from a trading brig touching at the island for wood and water some ten years previous
__label__MELVILLE he had gone ashore as a sovereign power armed with a musket and a bag of ammunition and ready if need were to prosecute war on his own account
__label__MELVILLE the country was divided by the hostile kings of several large valleys
__label__MELVILLE with one of them from whom he first received overtures he formed an alliance and became what he now was the military leader of the tribe and war god of the entire island
__label__MELVILLE his campaigns beat napoleons
__label__MELVILLE in one night attack his invincible musket backed by the light infantry of spears and javelins vanquished two clans and the next morning brought all the others to the feet of his royal ally
__label__MELVILLE nor was the rise of his domestic fortunes at all behind the corsicans three days after landing the exquisitely tattooed hand of a princess was his receiving along with the damsel as her portion one thousand fathoms of fine tappa fifty double braided mats of split grass four hundred hogs ten houses in different parts of her native valley and the sacred protection of an express edict of the taboo declaring his person inviolable for ever
__label__MELVILLE now this man was settled for life perfectly satisfied with his circumstances and feeling no desire to return to his friends
__label__MELVILLE friends indeed he had none
__label__MELVILLE he told me his history
__label__MELVILLE thrown upon the world a foundling his paternal origin was as much a mystery to him as the genealogy of odin and scorned by everybody he fled the parish workhouse when a boy and launched upon the sea
__label__MELVILLE he had followed it for several years a dog before the mast and now he had thrown it up for ever
__label__MELVILLE and for the most part it is just this sort of men so many of whom are found among sailors uncared for by a single soul without ties reckless and impatient of the restraints of civilization who are occasionally found quite at home upon the savage islands of the pacific
__label__MELVILLE and glancing at their hard lot in their own country what marvel at their choice
__label__MELVILLE according to the renegado there was no other white man on the island and as the captain could have no reason to suppose that hardy intended to deceive us he concluded that the frenchmen were in some way or other mistaken in what they had told us
__label__MELVILLE however when our errand was made known to the rest of our visitors one of them a fine stalwart fellow his face all eyes and expression volunteered for a cruise
__label__MELVILLE all the wages he asked was a red shirt a pair of trousers and a hat which were to be put on there and then besides a plug of tobacco and a pipe
__label__MELVILLE the bargain was struck directly but wymontoo afterward came in with a codicil to the effect that a friend of his who had come along with him should be given ten whole sea biscuits without crack or flaw twenty perfectly new and symmetrically straight nails and one jack knife
__label__MELVILLE this being agreed to the articles were at once handed over the native receiving them with great avidity and in the absence of clothing using his mouth as a pocket to put the nails in
__label__MELVILLE two of them however were first made to take the place of a pair of ear ornaments curiously fashioned out of bits of whitened wood
__label__MELVILLE it now began breezing strongly from seaward and no time was to be lost in getting away from the land so after an affecting rubbing of noses between our new shipmate and his countrymen we sailed away with him
__label__MELVILLE to our surprise the farewell shouts from the canoe as we dashed along under bellied royals were heard unmoved by our islander but it was not long thus
__label__MELVILLE that very evening when the dark blue of his native hills sunk in the horizon the poor savage leaned over the bulwarks dropped his head upon his chest and gave way to irrepressible emotions
__label__MELVILLE the ship was plunging hard and wymontoo sad to tell in addition to his other pangs was terribly sea sick
__label__MELVILLE the tattooers of la dominica
__label__MELVILLE for a while leaving little jule to sail away by herself i will here put down some curious information obtained from hardy
__label__MELVILLE the renegado had lived so long on the island that its customs were quite familiar and i much lamented that from the shortness of our stay he could not tell us more than he did
__label__MELVILLE from the little intelligence gathered however i learned to my surprise that in some things the people of hivarhoo though of the same group of islands differed considerably from my tropical friends in the valley of typee
__label__MELVILLE as his tattooing attracted so much remark hardy had a good deal to say concerning the manner in which that art was practised upon the island
__label__MELVILLE throughout the entire cluster the tattooers of hivarhoo enjoyed no small reputation
__label__MELVILLE they had carried their art to the highest perfection and the profession was esteemed most honourable
__label__MELVILLE no wonder then that like genteel tailors they rated their services very high so much so that none but those belonging to the higher classes could afford to employ them
__label__MELVILLE so true was this that the elegance of ones tattooing was in most cases a sure indication of birth and riches
__label__MELVILLE professors in large practice lived in spacious houses divided by screens of tappa into numerous little apartments where subjects were waited upon in private
__label__MELVILLE the arrangement chiefly grew out of a singular ordinance of the taboo which enjoined the strictest privacy upon all men high and low while under the hands of a tattooer
__label__MELVILLE for the time the slightest intercourse with others is prohibited and the small portion of food allowed is pushed under the curtain by an unseen hand
__label__MELVILLE the restriction with regard to food is intended to reduce the blood so as to diminish the inflammation consequent upon puncturing the skin
__label__MELVILLE as it is this comes on very soon and takes some time to heal so that the period of seclusion generally embraces many days sometimes several weeks
__label__MELVILLE all traces of soreness vanished the subject goes abroad but only again to return for on account of the pain only a small surface can be operated upon at once and as the whole body is to be more or less embellished by a process so slow the studios alluded to are constantly filled
__label__MELVILLE indeed with a vanity elsewhere unheard of many spend no small portion of their days thus sitting to an artist
__label__MELVILLE to begin the work the period of adolescence is esteemed the most suitable
__label__MELVILLE after casting about for some eminent tattooer the friends of the youth take him to his house to have the outlines of the general plan laid out
__label__MELVILLE it behoves the professor to have a nice eye for a suit to be worn for life should be well cut
__label__MELVILLE some tattooers yearning after perfection employ at large wages one or two men of the commonest order vile fellows utterly regardless of appearances upon whom they first try their patterns and practise generally
__label__MELVILLE their backs remorselessly scrawled over and no more canvas remaining they are dismissed and ever after go about the scorn of their countrymen
__label__MELVILLE hapless wights
__label__MELVILLE thus martyred in the cause of the fine arts
__label__MELVILLE beside the regular practitioners there are a parcel of shabby itinerant tattooers who by virtue of their calling stroll unmolested from one hostile bay to another doing their work dog cheap for the multitude
__label__MELVILLE they always repair to the various religious festivals which gather great crowds
__label__MELVILLE when these are concluded and the places where they are held vacated even by the tattooers scores of little tents of coarse tappa are left standing each with a solitary inmate who forbidden to talk to his unseen neighbours is obliged to stay there till completely healed
__label__MELVILLE the itinerants are a reproach to their profession mere cobblers dealing in nothing but jagged lines and clumsy patches and utterly incapable of soaring to those heights of fancy attained by the gentlemen of the faculty
__label__MELVILLE all professors of the arts love to fraternize and so in hannamanoo the tattooers came together in the chapters of their worshipful order
__label__MELVILLE in this society duly organized and conferring degrees hardy from his influence as a white was a sort of honorary grand master
__label__MELVILLE the blue shark and a sort of urim and thummim engraven upon his chest were the seal of his initiation
__label__MELVILLE all over hivarhoo are established these orders of tattooers
__label__MELVILLE the way in which the renegados came to be founded is this
__label__MELVILLE a year or two after his landing there happened to be a season of scarcity owing to the partial failure of the breadfruit harvest for several consecutive seasons
__label__MELVILLE this brought about such a falling off in the number of subjects for tattooing that the profession became quite needy
__label__MELVILLE the royal ally of hardy however hit upon a benevolent expedient to provide for their wants at the same time conferring a boon upon many of his subjects
__label__MELVILLE by sound of conch shell it was proclaimed before the palace on the beach and at the head of the valley that noomai king of hannamanoo and friend of hardee hardee the white kept open heart and table for all tattooers whatsoever but to entitle themselves to this hospitality they were commanded to practise without fee upon the meanest native soliciting their services
__label__MELVILLE numbers at once flocked to the royal abode both artists and sitters
__label__MELVILLE it was a famous time and the buildings of the palace being taboo to all but the tattooers and chiefs the sitters bivouacked on the common and formed an extensive encampment
__label__MELVILLE the lora tattoo or the time of tattooing will be long remembered
__label__MELVILLE an enthusiastic sitter celebrated the event in verse
__label__MELVILLE several lines were repeated to us by hardy some of which in a sort of colloquial chant he translated nearly thus
__label__MELVILLE where is that sound
__label__MELVILLE in hannamanoo
__label__MELVILLE and wherefore that sound
__label__MELVILLE the sound of a hundred hammers tapping tapping tapping the shark teeth
__label__MELVILLE where is that light
__label__MELVILLE round about the kings house and the small laughter
__label__MELVILLE the small merry laughter it is of the sons and daughters of the tattooed
__label__MELVILLE we steer to the westward state of affairs
__label__MELVILLE the night we left hannamanoo was bright and starry and so warm that when the watches were relieved most of the men instead of going below flung themselves around the foremast
__label__MELVILLE toward morning finding the heat of the forecastle unpleasant i ascended to the deck where everything was noiseless
__label__MELVILLE the trades were blowing with a mild steady strain upon the canvas and the ship heading right out into the immense blank of the western pacific
__label__MELVILLE the watch were asleep
__label__MELVILLE with one foot resting on the rudder even the man at the helm nodded and the mate himself with arms folded was leaning against the capstan
__label__MELVILLE on such a night and all alone reverie was inevitable
__label__MELVILLE i leaned over the side and could not help thinking of the strange objects we might be sailing over
__label__MELVILLE but my meditations were soon interrupted by a gray spectral shadow cast over the heaving billows
__label__MELVILLE it was the dawn soon followed by the first rays of the morning
__label__MELVILLE they flashed into view at one end of the arched night like to compare great things with small the gleamings of guy fawkess lantern in the vaults of the parliament house
__label__MELVILLE before long what seemed a live ember rested for a moment on the rim of the ocean and at last the blood red sun stood full and round in the level east and the long sea day began
__label__MELVILLE breakfast over the first thing attended to was the formal baptism of wymontoo who after thinking over his affairs during the night looked dismal enough
__label__MELVILLE there were various opinions as to a suitable appellation
__label__MELVILLE some maintained that we ought to call him sunday that being the day we caught him others eighteen forty two the then year of our lord while doctor long ghost remarked that he ought by all means to retain his original name wymontoo hee meaning as he maintained in the figurative language of the island something analogous to one who had got himself into a scrape
__label__MELVILLE the mate put an end to the discussion by sousing the poor fellow with a bucket of salt water and bestowing upon him the nautical appellation of luff
__label__MELVILLE though a certain mirthfulness succeeded his first pangs at leaving home wymontoo we will call him thus gradually relapsed into his former mood and became very melancholy
__label__MELVILLE often i noticed him crouching apart in the forecastle his strange eyes gleaming restlessly and watching the slightest movement of the men
__label__MELVILLE many a time he must have been thinking of his bamboo hut when they were talking of sydney and its dance houses
__label__MELVILLE we were now fairly at sea though to what particular cruising ground we were going no one knew and to all appearances few cared
__label__MELVILLE the men after a fashion of their own began to settle down into the routine of sea life as if everything was going on prosperously
__label__MELVILLE blown along over a smooth sea there was nothing to do but steer the ship and relieve the look outs at the mast heads
__label__MELVILLE as for the sick they had two or three more added to their number the air of the island having disagreed with the constitutions of several of the runaways
__label__MELVILLE to crown all the captain again relapsed and became quite ill
__label__MELVILLE the men fit for duty were divided into two small watches headed respectively by the mate and the mowree the latter by virtue of his being a harpooner succeeding to the place of the second mate who had absconded
__label__MELVILLE in this state of things whaling was out of the question but in the face of everything jermin maintained that the invalids would soon be well
__label__MELVILLE however that might be with the same pale hue sky overhead we kept running steadily to the westward
__label__MELVILLE forever advancing we seemed always in the same place and every day was the former lived over again
__label__MELVILLE we saw no ships expected to see none
__label__MELVILLE no sign of life was perceptible but the porpoises and other fish sporting under the bows like pups ashore
__label__MELVILLE but at intervals the gray albatross peculiar to these seas came flapping his immense wings over us and then skimmed away silently as if from a plague ship
__label__MELVILLE or flights of the tropic bird known among seamen as the boatswain wheeled round and round us whistling shrilly as they flew
__label__MELVILLE the uncertainty hanging over our destination at this time and the fact that we were abroad upon waters comparatively little traversed lent an interest to this portion of the cruise which i shall never forget
__label__MELVILLE from obvious prudential considerations the pacific has been principally sailed over in known tracts and this is the reason why new islands are still occasionally discovered by exploring ships and adventurous whalers notwithstanding the great number of vessels of all kinds of late navigating this vast ocean
__label__MELVILLE indeed considerable portions still remain wholly unexplored and there is doubt as to the actual existence of certain shoals and reefs and small clusters of islands vaguely laid down in the charts
__label__MELVILLE the mere circumstance therefore of a ship like ours penetrating into these regions was sufficient to cause any reflecting mind to feel at least a little uneasy
__label__MELVILLE for my own part the many stories i had heard of ships striking at midnight upon unknown rocks with all sail set and a slumbering crew often recurred to me especially as from the absence of discipline and our being so shorthanded the watches at night were careless in the extreme
__label__MELVILLE but no thoughts like these were entertained by my reckless shipmates and along we went the sun every evening setting right ahead of our jib boom
__label__MELVILLE for what reason the mate was so reserved with regard to our precise destination was never made known
__label__MELVILLE the stories he told us i for one did not believe deeming them all a mere device to lull the crew
__label__MELVILLE he said we were bound to a fine cruising ground scarcely known to other whalemen which he had himself discovered when commanding a small brig upon a former voyage
__label__MELVILLE here the sea was alive with large whales so tame that all you had to do was to go up and kill them they were too frightened to resist
__label__MELVILLE a little to leeward of this was a small cluster of islands where we were going to refit abounding with delicious fruits and peopled by a race almost wholly unsophisticated by intercourse with strangers
__label__MELVILLE in order perhaps to guard against the possibility of anyone finding out the precise latitude and longitude of the spot we were going to jermin never revealed to us the ships place at noon though such is the custom aboard of most vessels
__label__MELVILLE meanwhile he was very assiduous in his attention to the invalids
__label__MELVILLE doctor long ghost having given up the keys of the medicine chest they were handed over to him and as physician he discharged his duties to the satisfaction of all
__label__MELVILLE pills and powders in most cases were thrown to the fish and in place thereof the contents of a mysterious little quarter cask were produced diluted with water from the butt
__label__MELVILLE his draughts were mixed on the capstan in cocoa nut shells marked with the patients names
__label__MELVILLE like shore doctors he did not eschew his own medicines for his professional calls in the forecastle were sometimes made when he was comfortably tipsy nor did he omit keeping his invalids in good humour spinning his yarns to them by the hour whenever he went to see them

__label__MELVILLE but poor ropey proved quite as clumsy among the crockery as in the rigging and one day when the ship was pitching having stumbled into the cabin with a wooden tureen of soup he scalded the officers so that they didnt get over it in a week
__label__MELVILLE upon which he was dismissed and returned to the forecastle
__label__MELVILLE now nobody is so heartily despised as a pusillanimous lazy good for nothing land lubber a sailor has no bowels of compassion for him
__label__MELVILLE yet useless as such a character may be in many respects a ships company is by no means disposed to let him reap any benefit from his deficiencies
__label__MELVILLE regarded in the light of a mechanical power whenever there is any plain hard work to be done he is put to it like a lever everyone giving him a pry
__label__MELVILLE then again he is set about all the vilest work
__label__MELVILLE is there a heavy job at tarring to be done he is pitched neck and shoulders into a tar barrel and set to work at it

__label__MELVILLE like as not if the mate sends him after his quadrant on the way he is met by the captain who orders him to pick some oakum and while he is hunting up a bit of rope a sailor comes along and wants to know what the deuce hes after and bids him be off to the forecastle
__label__MELVILLE obey the last order is a precept inviolable at sea
__label__MELVILLE so the land lubber afraid to refuse to do anything rushes about distracted and does nothing in the end receiving a shower of kicks and cuffs from all quarters
__label__MELVILLE added to his other hardships he is seldom permitted to open his mouth unless spoken to and then he might better keep silent
__label__MELVILLE alas for him
__label__MELVILLE if he should happen to be anything of a droll for in an evil hour should he perpetrate a joke he would never know the last of it
__label__MELVILLE the witticisms of others however upon himself must be received in the greatest good humour
__label__MELVILLE woe be unto him if at meal times he so much as look sideways at the beef kid before the rest are helped
