__label__MELVILLE alas
__label__MELVILLE i say again for the land lubber at sea
__label__MELVILLE he is the veriest wretch the watery world over
__label__MELVILLE and such was bope tarn of all landlubbers the most lubberly and most miserable
__label__MELVILLE a forlorn stunted hook visaged mortal he was too one of those whom you know at a glance to have been tried hard and long in the furnace of affliction
__label__MELVILLE his face was an absolute puzzle though sharp and sallow it had neither the wrinkles of age nor the smoothness of youth so that for the soul of me i could hardly tell whether he was twenty five or fifty
__label__MELVILLE but to his history
__label__MELVILLE in his better days it seems he had been a journeyman baker in london somewhere about holborn and on sundays wore a hue coat and metal buttons and spent his afternoons in a tavern smoking his pipe and drinking his ale like a free and easy journeyman baker that he was

__label__MELVILLE a kind word made a fool of him and hence most of the scrapes he got into

__label__MELVILLE the dane was a mule of a man and understanding but little english seldom made anything of a reply so the cooper generally dropped his leg and marched off with the air of a man who despised saying anything further
__label__MELVILLE we encounter a gale
__label__MELVILLE the mild blue weather we enjoyed after leaving the marquesas gradually changed as we ran farther south and approached tahiti
__label__MELVILLE in these generally tranquil seas the wind sometimes blows with great violence though as every sailor knows a spicy gale in the tropic latitudes of the pacific is far different from a tempest in the howling north atlantic
__label__MELVILLE we soon found ourselves battling with the waves while the before mild trades like a woman roused blew fiercely but still warmly in our face
__label__MELVILLE for all this the mate carried sail without stint and as for brave little jule she stood up to it well and though once in a while floored in the trough of a sea sprang to her keel again and showed play

__label__MELVILLE hurrah

__label__MELVILLE it was the main t gallant mast
__label__MELVILLE crash
__label__MELVILLE it broke off just above the cap and held there by the rigging dashed with every roll from side to side with all the hamper that belonged to it

__label__MELVILLE the yard with a snap and a plunge went hissing into the sea disappeared and shot its full length out again

__label__MELVILLE while this lively breeze continued baltimore our old black cook was in great tribulation
__label__MELVILLE like most south seamen the julias caboose or cook house was planted on the larboard side of the forecastle
__label__MELVILLE under such a press of canvas and with the heavy sea running the barque diving her bows under now and then shipped green glassy waves which breaking over the head rails fairly deluged that part of the ship and washed clean aft
__label__MELVILLE the caboose house thought to be fairly lashed down to its place served as a sort of breakwater to the inundation

__label__MELVILLE thus equipped for a ducking or a drowning as the case might be our culinary high priest drew to the slides of his temple and performed his sooty rites in secret
__label__MELVILLE so afraid was the old man of being washed overboard that he actually fastened one end of a small line to his waistbands and coiling the rest about him made use of it as occasion required
__label__MELVILLE when engaged outside he unwound the cord and secured one end to a ringbolt in the deck so that if a chance sea washed him off his feet it could do nothing more
__label__MELVILLE one evening just as he was getting supper the julia reared up on her stern like a vicious colt and when she settled again forward fairly dished a tremendous sea
__label__MELVILLE nothing could withstand it

__label__MELVILLE the water then poured along the deck like a flood rolling over and over pots pans and kettles and even old baltimore himself who went breaching along like a porpoise

__label__MELVILLE the few men on deck having sprung into the main rigging sailor like did nothing but roar at his calamity
__label__MELVILLE the same night our flying jib boom snapped off like a pipe stem and our spanker gaff came down by the run
__label__MELVILLE by the following morning the wind in a great measure had gone down the sea with it and by noon we had repaired our damages as well as we could and were sailing along as pleasantly as ever
__label__MELVILLE but there was no help for the demolished bulwarks we had nothing to replace them and so whenever it breezed again our dauntless craft went along with her splintered prow dripping but kicking up her fleet heels just as high as before
__label__MELVILLE the coral islands
__label__MELVILLE how far we sailed to the westward after leaving the marquesas or what might have been our latitude and longitude at any particular time or how many leagues we voyaged on our passage to tahiti are matters about which i am sorry to say i cannot with any accuracy enlighten the reader
__label__MELVILLE jermin as navigator kept our reckoning and as hinted before kept it all to himself
__label__MELVILLE at noon he brought out his quadrant a rusty old thing so odd looking that it might have belonged to an astrologer
__label__MELVILLE sometimes when rather flustered from his potations he went staggering about deck instrument to eye looking all over for the sun a phenomenon which any sober observer might have seen right overhead
__label__MELVILLE how upon earth he contrived on some occasions to settle his latitude is more than i can tell
__label__MELVILLE the longitude he must either have obtained by the rule of three or else by special revelation
__label__MELVILLE not that the chronometer in the cabin was seldom to be relied on or was any ways fidgety quite the contrary it stood stock still and by that means no doubt the true greenwich time at the period of stopping at least was preserved to a second
__label__MELVILLE the mate however in addition to his dead reckoning pretended to ascertain his meridian distance from bow bells by an occasional lunar observation
__label__MELVILLE this i believe consists in obtaining with the proper instruments the angular distance between the moon and some one of the stars
__label__MELVILLE the operation generally requires two observers to take sights and at one and the same time
__label__MELVILLE now though the mate alone might have been thought well calculated for this inasmuch as he generally saw things double the doctor was usually called upon to play a sort of second quadrant to jermins first and what with the capers of both they used to furnish a good deal of diversion
__label__MELVILLE the mates tremulous attempts to level his instrument at the star he was after were comical enough
__label__MELVILLE for my own part when he did catch sight of it i hardly knew how he managed to separate it from the astral host revolving in his own brain
__label__MELVILLE however by hook or by crook he piloted us along and before many days a fellow sent aloft to darn a rent in the fore top sail threw his hat into the air and bawled out land ho
__label__MELVILLE land it was but in what part of the south seas jermin alone knew and some doubted whether even he did
__label__MELVILLE but no sooner was the announcement made than he came running on deck spy glass in hand and clapping it to his eye turned round with the air of a man receiving indubitable assurance of something he was quite certain of before
__label__MELVILLE the land was precisely that for which he had been steering and with a wind in less than twenty four hours we would sight tahiti
__label__MELVILLE what he said was verified
__label__MELVILLE the island turned out to be one of the pomotu or low group sometimes called the coral islands perhaps the most remarkable and interesting in the pacific
__label__MELVILLE lying to the east of tahiti the nearest are within a days sail of that place
__label__MELVILLE they are very numerous mostly small low and level sometimes wooded but always covered with verdure
__label__MELVILLE many are crescent shaped others resemble a horse shoe in figure
__label__MELVILLE these last are nothing more than narrow circles of land surrounding a smooth lagoon connected by a single opening with the sea
__label__MELVILLE some of the lagoons said to have subterranean outlets have no visible ones the inclosing island in such cases being a complete zone of emerald
__label__MELVILLE other lagoons still are girdled by numbers of small green islets very near to each other
__label__MELVILLE the origin of the entire group is generally ascribed to the coral insect
__label__MELVILLE according to some naturalists this wonderful little creature commencing its erections at the bottom of the sea after the lapse of centuries carries them up to the surface where its labours cease
__label__MELVILLE here the inequalities of the coral collect all floating bodies forming after a time a soil in which the seeds carried thither by birds germinate and cover the whole with vegetation
__label__MELVILLE here and there all over this archipelago numberless naked detached coral formations are seen just emerging as it were from the ocean
__label__MELVILLE these would appear to be islands in the very process of creation at any rate one involuntarily concludes so on beholding them
__label__MELVILLE as far as i know there are but few bread fruit trees in any part of the pomotu group
__label__MELVILLE in many places the cocoa nut even does not grow though in others it largely flourishes
__label__MELVILLE consequently some of the islands are altogether uninhabited others support but a single family and in no place is the population very large
__label__MELVILLE in some respects the natives resemble the tahitians their language too is very similar
__label__MELVILLE the people of the southeasterly clusters concerning whom however but little is known have a bad name as cannibals and for that reason their hospitality is seldom taxed by the mariner
__label__MELVILLE within a few years past missionaries from the society group have settled among the leeward islands where the natives have treated them kindly
__label__MELVILLE indeed nominally many of these people are now christians and through the political influence of their instructors no doubt a short time since came tinder the allegiance of pomaree the queen of tahiti with which island they always carried on considerable intercourse
__label__MELVILLE the coral islands are principally visited by the pearl shell fishermen who arrive in small schooners carrying not more than five or six men
__label__MELVILLE for a long while the business was engrossed by merenhout the french consul at tahiti but a dutchman by birth who in one year is said to have sent to france fifty thousand dollars worth of shells
__label__MELVILLE the oysters are found in the lagoons and about the reefs and for half a dozen nails a day or a compensation still less the natives are hired to dive after them
__label__MELVILLE a great deal of cocoa nut oil is also obtained in various places
__label__MELVILLE some of the uninhabited islands are covered with dense groves and the ungathered nuts which have fallen year after year lie upon the ground in incredible quantities
__label__MELVILLE two or three men provided with the necessary apparatus for trying out the oil will in the course of a week or two obtain enough to load one of the large sea canoes
__label__MELVILLE cocoa nut oil is now manufactured in different parts of the south seas and forms no small part of the traffic carried on with trading vessels
__label__MELVILLE a considerable quantity is annually exported from the society islands to sydney
__label__MELVILLE it is used in lamps and for machinery being much cheaper than the sperm and for both purposes better than the right whale oil
__label__MELVILLE they bottle it up in large bamboos six or eight feet long and these form part of the circulating medium of tahiti
__label__MELVILLE to return to the ship
__label__MELVILLE the wind dying away evening came on before we drew near the island
__label__MELVILLE but we had it in view during the whole afternoon
__label__MELVILLE it was small and round presenting one enamelled level free from trees and did not seem four feet above the water

__label__MELVILLE tahiti
__label__MELVILLE at early dawn of the following morning we saw the peaks of tahiti
__label__MELVILLE in clear weather they may be seen at the distance of ninety miles
__label__MELVILLE hivarhoo
__label__MELVILLE shouted wymontoo overjoyed and running out upon the bowsprit when the land was first faintly descried in the distance
__label__MELVILLE but when the clouds floated away and showed the three peaks standing like obelisks against the sky and the bold shore undulating along the horizon the tears gushed from his eyes
__label__MELVILLE poor fellow
__label__MELVILLE it was not hivarhoo
__label__MELVILLE green hivarhoo was many a long league off
__label__MELVILLE tahiti is by far the most famous island in the south seas indeed a variety of causes has made it almost classic
__label__MELVILLE its natural features alone distinguish it from the surrounding groups
__label__MELVILLE two round and lofty promontories whose mountains rise nine thousand feet above the level of the ocean are connected by a low narrow isthmus the whole being some one hundred miles in circuit
__label__MELVILLE from the great central peaks of the larger peninsula orohena aorai and pirohitee the land radiates on all sides to the sea in sloping green ridges
__label__MELVILLE between these are broad and shadowy valleys in aspect each a tempe watered with fine streams and thickly wooded
__label__MELVILLE unlike many of the other islands there extends nearly all round tahiti a belt of low alluvial soil teeming with the richest vegetation
__label__MELVILLE here chiefly the natives dwell
__label__MELVILLE seen from the sea the prospect is magnificent
__label__MELVILLE it is one mass of shaded tints of green from beach to mountain top endlessly diversified with valleys ridges glens and cascades
__label__MELVILLE over the ridges here and there the loftier peaks fling their shadows and far down the valleys
__label__MELVILLE at the head of these the waterfalls flash out into the sunlight as if pouring through vertical bowers of verdure
__label__MELVILLE such enchantment too breathes over the whole that it seems a fairy world all fresh and blooming from the hand of the creator
__label__MELVILLE upon a near approach the picture loses not its attractions
__label__MELVILLE it is no exaggeration to say that to a european of any sensibility who for the first time wanders back into these valleys away from the haunts of the natives the ineffable repose and beauty of the landscape is such that every object strikes him like something seen in a dream and for a time he almost refuses to believe that scenes like these should have a commonplace existence
__label__MELVILLE no wonder that the french bestowed upon the island the appellation of the new cytherea
__label__MELVILLE often says de bourgainville i thought i was walking in the garden of eden
__label__MELVILLE nor when first discovered did the inhabitants of this charming country at all diminish the wonder and admiration of the voyager
__label__MELVILLE their physical beauty and amiable dispositions harmonized completely with the softness of their clime
__label__MELVILLE in truth everything about them was calculated to awaken the liveliest interest
__label__MELVILLE glance at their civil and religious institutions
__label__MELVILLE to their king divine rights were paid while for poetry their mythology rivalled that of ancient greece
__label__MELVILLE of tahiti earlier and more full accounts were given than of any other island in polynesia and this is the reason why it still retains so strong a hold on the sympathies of all readers of south sea voyages
__label__MELVILLE the journals of its first visitors containing as they did such romantic descriptions of a country and people before unheard of produced a marked sensation throughout europe and when the first tahitiana were carried thither omai in london and aotooroo in paris were caressed by nobles scholars and ladies
__label__MELVILLE in addition to all this several eventful occurrences more or less connected with tahiti have tended to increase its celebrity
__label__MELVILLE over two centuries ago quiros the spaniard is supposed to have touched at the island and at intervals wallis byron cook de bourgainville vancouver le perouse and other illustrious navigators refitted their vessels in its harbours
__label__MELVILLE here the famous transit of venus was observed in 1769
__label__MELVILLE here the memorable mutiny of the bounty afterwards had its origin
__label__MELVILLE it was to the pagans of tahiti that the first regularly constituted protestant missionaries were sent and from their shores also have sailed successive missions to the neighbouring islands
__label__MELVILLE these with other events which might be mentioned have united in keeping up the first interest which the place awakened and the recent proceedings of the french have more than ever called forth the sympathies of the public
__label__MELVILLE a surprise more about bembo
__label__MELVILLE the sight of the island was right welcome
__label__MELVILLE going into harbour after a cruise is always joyous enough and the sailor is apt to indulge in all sorts of pleasant anticipations
__label__MELVILLE but to us the occasion was heightened by many things peculiar to our situation
__label__MELVILLE since steering for the land our prospects had been much talked over
__label__MELVILLE by many it was supposed that should the captain leave the ship the crew were no longer bound by her articles
__label__MELVILLE this was the opinion of our forecastle cokes though probably it would not have been sanctioned by the marine courts of law
__label__MELVILLE at any rate such was the state of both vessel and crew that whatever might be the event a long stay and many holidays in tahiti were confidently predicted
__label__MELVILLE everybody was in high spirits
__label__MELVILLE the sick who had been improving day by day since the change in our destination were on deck and leaning over the bulwarks some all animation and others silently admiring an object unrivalled for its stately beauty tahiti from the sea
__label__MELVILLE the quarter deck however furnished a marked contrast to what was going on at the other end of the ship
__label__MELVILLE the mowree was there as usual scowling by himself and jermin walked to and fro in deep thought every now and then looking to windward or darting into the cabin and quickly returning

__label__MELVILLE several ships were descried lying in the harbour and among them one which loomed up black and large her two rows of teeth proclaiming a frigate
__label__MELVILLE this was the reine blanche last from the marquesas and carrying at the fore the flag of rear admiral du petit thouars

__label__MELVILLE calabooza
__label__MELVILLE calabooza beretanee
__label__MELVILLE the english jail cried our conductor pointing to the building
__label__MELVILLE for a few months past having been used by the consul as a house of confinement for his refractory sailors it was thus styled to distinguish it from similar places in and about papeetee
__label__MELVILLE though extremely romantic in appearance on a near approach it proved hut ill adapted to domestic comfort
__label__MELVILLE in short it was a mere shell recently built and still unfinished
__label__MELVILLE it was open all round and tufts of grass were growing here and there under the very roof
__label__MELVILLE the only piece of furniture was the stocks a clumsy machine for keeping people in one place which i believe is pretty much out of date in most countries
__label__MELVILLE it is still in use however among the spaniards in south america from whom it seems the tahitians have borrowed the contrivance as well as the name by which all places of confinement are known among them
__label__MELVILLE the stocks were nothing more than two stout timbers about twenty feet in length and precisely alike
__label__MELVILLE one was placed edgeways on the ground and the other resting on top left at regular intervals along the seam several round holes the object of which was evident at a glance
__label__MELVILLE by this time our guide had informed us that he went by the name of capin bob captain bob and a hearty old bob he proved
__label__MELVILLE it was just the name for him
__label__MELVILLE from the first so pleased were we with the old man that we cheerfully acquiesced in his authority
__label__MELVILLE entering the building he set us about fetching heaps of dry leaves to spread behind the stocks for a couch
__label__MELVILLE a trunk of a small cocoa nut tree was then placed for a bolster rather a hard one but the natives are used to it
__label__MELVILLE for a pillow they use a little billet of wood scooped out and standing on four short legs a sort of head stool
__label__MELVILLE these arrangements completed captain bob proceeded to hanna par or secure us for the night
__label__MELVILLE the upper timber of the machine being lifted at one end and our ankles placed in the semicircular spaces of the lower one the other beam was then dropped both being finally secured together by an old iron hoop at either extremity
__label__MELVILLE this initiation was performed to the boisterous mirth of the natives and diverted ourselves not a little
__label__MELVILLE captain bob now bustled about like an old woman seeing the children to bed
__label__MELVILLE a basket of baked taro or indian turnip was brought in and we were given a piece all round
__label__MELVILLE then a great counterpane of coarse brown tappa was stretched over the whole party and after sundry injunctions to moee moee and be maitai in other words to go to sleep and be good boys we were left to ourselves fairly put to bed and tucked in

__label__MELVILLE after sliding from one reverie into another i started and gave the doctor a pinch

__label__MELVILLE the consciousness of having ones foot pinned and the impossibility of getting it anywhere else than just where it was was most distressing
__label__MELVILLE but this was not all there was no way of lying but straight on your back unless to be sure ones limb went round and round in the ankle like a swivel

__label__MELVILLE captain bob and his friends lived in a little hamlet hard by and when morning showed in the east the old gentleman came forth from that direction likewise emerging from a grove and saluting us loudly as he approached

__label__MELVILLE bob was a linguist and had been to sea in his day as he many a time afterwards told us
__label__MELVILLE at this moment we were all alone with him and it would have been the easiest thing in the world to have given him the slip but he seemed to have no idea of such a thing treating us so frankly and cordially indeed that even had we thought of running we should have been ashamed of attempting it

__label__MELVILLE close by was a taro patch of his which he occasionally visited
__label__MELVILLE bob seldom disposed of the produce of his lands it was all needed for domestic consumption

__label__MELVILLE a friend of bobs told me that owing to his voraciousness his visits to other parts of the island were much dreaded for according to tahitian customs hospitality without charge is enjoined upon everyone and though it is reciprocal in most cases in bobs it was almost out of the question

__label__MELVILLE this we agreed to and every morning afterward when the bucket came its contents were at once handed over to bob and his friends who never ceased munching until nightfall
__label__MELVILLE our exceedingly frugal meal of bread fruit over captain bob waddled up to us with a couple of long poles hooked at one end and several large baskets of woven cocoa nut branches
__label__MELVILLE not far off was an extensive grove of orange trees in full bearing and myself and another were selected to go with him and gather a supply for the party
__label__MELVILLE when we went in among the trees the sumptuousness of the orchard was unlike anything i had ever seen while the fragrance shaken from the gently waving boughs regaled our senses most delightfully
__label__MELVILLE in many places the trees formed a dense shade spreading overhead a dark rustling vault groined with boughs and studded here and there with the ripened spheres like gilded balls
__label__MELVILLE in several places the overladen branches were borne to the earth hiding the trunk in a tent of foliage

__label__MELVILLE to preserve the fruit from bruising bob hooking the twigs with his pole let them fall into his basket
__label__MELVILLE but this would not do for us
__label__MELVILLE seizing hold of a bough we brought such a shower to the ground that our old friend was fain to run from under

__label__MELVILLE heaping up the baskets afterwards we returned to our comrades by whom our arrival was hailed with loud plaudits and in a marvellously short time nothing was left of the oranges we brought but the rinds
__label__MELVILLE while inmates of the calabooza we had as much of the fruit as we wanted and to this cause and others that might be mentioned may be ascribed the speedy restoration of our sick to comparative health
__label__MELVILLE the orange of tahiti is delicious small and sweet with a thin dry rind
__label__MELVILLE though now abounding it was unknown before cooks time to whom the natives are indebted for so great a blessing
__label__MELVILLE he likewise introduced several other kinds of fruit among these were the fig pineapple and lemon now seldom met with
__label__MELVILLE the lime still grows and some of the poorer natives express the juice to sell to the shipping
__label__MELVILLE it is highly valued as an anti scorbutic

__label__MELVILLE more of them anon
__label__MELVILLE thus after all that of late years has been done for these islanders cook and vancouver may in one sense at least be considered their greatest benefactors
__label__MELVILLE proceedings of the french at tahiti
__label__MELVILLE as i happened to arrive at the island at a very interesting period in its political affairs it may be well to give some little account here of the proceedings of the french by way of episode to the narrative
__label__MELVILLE my information was obtained at the time from the general reports then rife among the natives as well as from what i learned upon a subsequent visit and reliable accounts which i have seen since reaching home
__label__MELVILLE it seems that for some time back the french had been making repeated ineffectual attempts to plant a roman catholic mission here
__label__MELVILLE but invariably treated with contumely they sometimes met with open violence and in every case those directly concerned in the enterprise were ultimately forced to depart
__label__MELVILLE in one instance two priests laval and caset after enduring a series of persecutions were set upon by the natives maltreated and finally carried aboard a small trading schooner which eventually put them ashore at wallis island a savage place some two thousand miles to the westward
__label__MELVILLE now that the resident english missionaries authorized the banishment of these priests is a fact undenied by themselves
__label__MELVILLE i was also repeatedly informed that by their inflammatory harangues they instigated the riots which preceded the sailing of the schooner
__label__MELVILLE at all events it is certain that their unbounded influence with the natives would easily have enabled them to prevent everything that took place on this occasion had they felt so inclined
__label__MELVILLE melancholy as such an example of intolerance on the part of protestant missionaries must appear it is not the only one and by no means the most flagrant which might be presented
__label__MELVILLE but i forbear to mention any others since they have been more than hinted at by recent voyagers and their repetition here would perhaps be attended with no good effect
__label__MELVILLE besides the conduct of the sandwich island missionaries in particular has latterly much amended in this respect
__label__MELVILLE the treatment of the two priests formed the principal ground and the only justifiable one upon which du petit thouars demanded satisfaction and which subsequently led to his seizure of the island
__label__MELVILLE in addition to other things he also charged that the flag of merenhout the consul had been repeatedly insulted and the property of a certain french resident violently appropriated by the government
__label__MELVILLE in the latter instance the natives were perfectly in the right
__label__MELVILLE at that time the law against the traffic in ardent spirits every now and then suspended and revived happened to be in force and finding a large quantity on the premises of victor a low knavish adventurer from marseilles the tahitians pronounced it forfeit
__label__MELVILLE for these and similar alleged outrages a large pecuniary restitution was demanded 10000 dollars which there being no exchequer to supply the island was forthwith seized under cover of a mock treaty dictated to the chiefs on the gun deck of du petit thouars frigate
__label__MELVILLE but notwithstanding this formality there seems now little doubt that the downfall of the pomarees was decided upon at the tuilleries
__label__MELVILLE after establishing the protectorate so called the rear admiral sailed leaving m bruat governor assisted by reine and carpegne civilians named members of the council of government and merenhout the consul now made commissioner royal
__label__MELVILLE no soldiers however were landed until several months afterward
__label__MELVILLE as men reine and carpegne were not disliked by the natives but bruat and merenhout they bitterly detested
__label__MELVILLE in several interviews with the poor queen the unfeeling governor sought to terrify her into compliance with his demands clapping his hand upon his sword shaking his fist in her face and swearing violently
__label__MELVILLE oh king of a great nation said pomaree in her letter to louis philippe fetch away this man i and my people cannot endure his evil doings

__label__MELVILLE although the excitement among the natives did not wholly subside upon the rear admirals departure no overt act of violence immediately followed
__label__MELVILLE the queen had fled to imeeo and the dissensions among the chiefs together with the ill advised conduct of the missionaries prevented a union upon some common plan of resistance
__label__MELVILLE but the great body of the people as well as their queen confidently relied upon the speedy interposition of england a nation bound to them by many ties and which more than once had solemnly guaranteed their independence
__label__MELVILLE as for the missionaries they openly defied the french governor childishly predicting fleets and armies from britain
__label__MELVILLE but what is the welfare of a spot like tahiti to the mighty interests of france and england
__label__MELVILLE there was a remonstrance on one side and a reply on the other and there the matter rested
__label__MELVILLE for once in their brawling lives st george and st denis were hand and glove and they were not going to cross sabres about tahiti
__label__MELVILLE during my stay upon the island so far as i could see there was little to denote that any change had taken place in the government
__label__MELVILLE such laws as they had were administered the same as ever the missionaries went about unmolested and comparative tranquillity everywhere prevailed
__label__MELVILLE nevertheless i sometimes heard the natives inveighing against the french no favourites by the bye throughout polynesia and bitterly regretting that the queen had not at the outset made a stand
__label__MELVILLE in the house of the chief adeea frequent discussions took place concerning the ability of the island to cope with the french the number of fighting men and muskets among the natives were talked of as well as the propriety of fortifying several heights overlooking papeetee
__label__MELVILLE imputing these symptoms to the mere resentment of a recent outrage and not to any determined spirit of resistance i little anticipated the gallant though useless warfare so soon to follow my departure
__label__MELVILLE at a period subsequent to my first visit the island which before was divided into nineteen districts with a native chief over each in capacity of governor and judge was by bruat divided into four
__label__MELVILLE over these he set as many recreant chiefs kitoti tati utamai and paraita to whom he paid 1000 dollars each to secure their assistance in carrying out his evil designs
__label__MELVILLE the first blood shed in any regular conflict was at mahanar upon the peninsula of taraiboo
__label__MELVILLE the fight originated in the seizure of a number of women from the shore by men belonging to one of the french vessels of war
__label__MELVILLE in this affair the islanders fought desperately killing about fifty of the enemy and losing ninety of their own number
__label__MELVILLE the french sailors and marines who at the time were reported to be infuriated with liquor gave no quarter and the survivors only saved themselves by fleeing to the mountains
__label__MELVILLE subsequently the battles of hararparpi and fararar were fought in which the invaders met with indifferent success
__label__MELVILLE shortly after the engagement at hararparpi three frenchmen were waylaid in a pass of the valleys and murdered by the incensed natives

__label__MELVILLE this circumstance violently inflamed the hostility of both parties
__label__MELVILLE about this time kitoti a depraved chief and the pliant tool of bruat was induced by him to give a great feast in the vale of paree to which all his countrymen were invited
__label__MELVILLE the governors object was to gain over all he could to his interests he supplied an abundance of wine and brandy and a scene of bestial intoxication was the natural consequence

__label__MELVILLE this is a very good feast said the reeling old man and the wine also is very good but you evil minded wee wees french and you false hearted men of tahiti are all very bad
__label__MELVILLE by the latest accounts most of the islanders still refuse to submit to the french and what turn events may hereafter take it is hard to predict
__label__MELVILLE at any rate these disorders must accelerate the final extinction of their race
__label__MELVILLE along with the few officers left by du petit thouars were several french priests for whose unobstructed exertions in the dissemination of their faith the strongest guarantees were provided by an article of the treaty
__label__MELVILLE but no one was bound to offer them facilities much less a luncheon the first day they went ashore
__label__MELVILLE true they had plenty of gold but to the natives it was anathema taboo and for several hours and some odd minutes they would not touch it
__label__MELVILLE emissaries of the pope and the devil as the strangers were considered the smell of sulphur hardly yet shaken out of their canonicals what islander would venture to jeopardize his soul and call down a blight on his breadfruit by holding any intercourse with them
__label__MELVILLE that morning the priests actually picknicked in grove of cocoa nut trees but before night christian hospitality in exchange for a commercial equivalent of hard dollars was given them in an adjoining house
__label__MELVILLE wanting in civility as the conduct of the english missionaries may be thought in withholding a decent reception to these persons the latter were certainly to blame in needlessly placing themselves in so unpleasant a predicament
__label__MELVILLE under far better auspices they might have settled upon some one of the thousand unconverted isles of the pacific rather than have forced themselves thus upon a people already professedly christians
__label__MELVILLE we receive calls at the hotel de calabooza
__label__MELVILLE our place of confinement being open all round and so near the broom road of course we were in plain sight of everybody passing and therefore we had no lack of visitors among such an idle inquisitive set as the tahitians
__label__MELVILLE for a few days they were coming and going continually while thus ignobly fast by the foot we were fain to give passive audience
__label__MELVILLE during this period we were the lions of the neighbourhood and no doubt strangers from the distant villages were taken to see the karhowrees white men in the same way that countrymen in a city are gallanted to the zoological gardens
__label__MELVILLE all this gave us a fine opportunity of making observations
__label__MELVILLE i was painfully struck by the considerable number of sickly or deformed persons undoubtedly made so by a virulent complaint which under native treatment almost invariably affects in the end the muscles and bones of the body
__label__MELVILLE in particular there is a distortion of the back most unsightly to behold originating in a horrible form of the malady
__label__MELVILLE although this and other bodily afflictions were unknown before the discovery of the islands by the whites there are several cases found of the pa fa or elephantiasis a native disease which seems to have prevailed among them from the earliest antiquity
__label__MELVILLE affecting the legs and feet alone it swells them in some instances to the girth of a mans body covering the skin with scales
__label__MELVILLE it might be supposed that one thus afflicted would be incapable of walking but to all appearance they seem to be nearly as active as anybody apparently suffering no pain and bearing the calamity with a degree of cheerfulness truly marvellous
__label__MELVILLE the fa fa is very gradual in its approaches and years elapse before the limb is fully swollen
__label__MELVILLE its origin is ascribed by the natives to various causes but the general impression seems to be that it arises in most cases from the eating of unripe bread fruit and indian turnip
__label__MELVILLE so far as i could find out it is not hereditary
__label__MELVILLE in no stage do they attempt a cure the complaint being held incurable
__label__MELVILLE speaking of the fa fa reminds me of a poor fellow a sailor whom i afterward saw at roorootoo a lone island some two days sail from tahiti
__label__MELVILLE the island is very small and its inhabitants nearly extinct
__label__MELVILLE we sent a boat off to see whether any yams were to be had as formerly the yams of roorootoo were as famous among the islands round about as sicily oranges in the mediterranean

__label__MELVILLE but when it became plain that his only chance for recovery was a speedy change of climate no ship would receive him as a sailor to think of being taken as a passenger was idle

__label__MELVILLE i afterwards heard of this melancholy object from two seamen
__label__MELVILLE his attempts to leave were still unavailing and his hard fate was fast closing in
__label__MELVILLE notwithstanding the physical degeneracy of the tahitians as a people among the chiefs individuals of personable figures are still frequently met with and occasionally majestic looking men and diminutive women as lovely as the nymphs who nearly a century ago swam round the ships of wallis
__label__MELVILLE in these instances tahitian beauty is quite as seducing as it proved to the crew of the bounty the young girls being just such creatures as a poet would picture in the tropics soft plump and dreamy eyed
__label__MELVILLE the natural complexion of both sexes is quite light but the males appear much darker from their exposure to the sun
__label__MELVILLE a dark complexion however in a man is highly esteemed as indicating strength of both body and soul
__label__MELVILLE hence there is a saying of great antiquity among them
__label__MELVILLE if dark the cheek of the mother the son will sound the war conch if strong her frame he will give laws
__label__MELVILLE with this idea of manliness no wonder the tahitians regarded all pale and tepid looking europeans as weak and feminine whereas a sailor with a cheek like the breast of a roast turkey is held a lad of brawn to use their own phrase a taata tona or man of bones
__label__MELVILLE speaking of bones recalls an ugly custom of theirs now obsolete that of making fish hooks and gimlets out of those of their enemies
__label__MELVILLE this beats the scandinavians turning peoples skulls into cups and saucers
__label__MELVILLE but to return to the calabooza beretanee
__label__MELVILLE immense was the interest we excited among the throngs that called there they would stand talking about us by the hour growing most unnecessarily excited too and dancing up and down with all the vivacity of their race
__label__MELVILLE they invariably sided with us flying out against the consul and denouncing him as ita maitai nuee or very bad exceedingly
__label__MELVILLE they must have borne him some grudge or other
__label__MELVILLE nor were the women sweet souls at all backward in visiting
__label__MELVILLE indeed they manifested even more interest than the men gazing at us with eyes full of a thousand meanings and conversing with marvellous rapidity
__label__MELVILLE but alas

__label__MELVILLE many of them laughed outright at us noting only what was ridiculous in our plight

__label__MELVILLE she was a heartless one tickled to death with black dans nursing his chafed ankle and indulging in certain moral reflections on the consul and captain guy
__label__MELVILLE after laughing her fill at him she condescended to notice the rest glancing from one to another in the most methodical and provoking manner imaginable
__label__MELVILLE whenever anything struck her comically you saw it like a flash her finger levelled instantaneously and flinging herself back she gave loose to strange hollow little notes of laughter that sounded like the bass of a music box playing a lively air with the lid down
__label__MELVILLE now i knew not that there was anything in my own appearance calculated to disarm ridicule and indeed to have looked at all heroic under the circumstances would have been rather difficult

__label__MELVILLE though my face was averted i soon felt it flush and knew that the glance was on me deeper and deeper grew the flush and not a sound of laughter
__label__MELVILLE delicious thought
__label__MELVILLE she was moved at the sight of me
__label__MELVILLE i could stand it no longer but started up
__label__MELVILLE lo
__label__MELVILLE there she was her great hazel eyes rounding and rounding in her head like two stars her whole frame in a merry quiver and an expression about the mouth that was sudden and violent death to anything like sentiment
__label__MELVILLE the next moment she spun round and bursting from peal to peal of laughter went racing out of the calabooza and in mercy to me never returned
__label__MELVILLE life at the calabooza
__label__MELVILLE a few days passed and at last our docility was rewarded by some indulgence on the part of captain bob
__label__MELVILLE he allowed the entire party to be at large during the day only enjoining upon us always to keep within hail
__label__MELVILLE this to be sure was in positive disobedience to wilsons orders and so care had to be taken that he should not hear of it
__label__MELVILLE there was little fear of the natives telling him but strangers travelling the broom road might
__label__MELVILLE by way of precaution boys were stationed as scouts along the road
__label__MELVILLE at sight of a white man they sounded the alarm
__label__MELVILLE when we all made for our respective holes the stocks being purposely left open the beam then descended and we were prisoners
__label__MELVILLE as soon as the traveller was out of sight of course we were liberated
__label__MELVILLE notwithstanding the regular supply of food which we obtained from captain bob and his friends it was so small that we often felt most intolerably hungry
__label__MELVILLE we could not blame them for not bringing us more for we soon became aware that they had to pinch themselves in order to give us what they did besides they received nothing for their kindness but the daily bucket of bread
__label__MELVILLE among a people like the tahitians what we call hard times can only be experienced in the scarcity of edibles yet so destitute are many of the common people that this most distressing consequence of civilization may be said with them to be ever present
__label__MELVILLE to be sure the natives about the calabooza had abundance of limes and oranges but what were these good for except to impart a still keener edge to appetites which there was so little else to gratify
__label__MELVILLE during the height of the bread fruit season they fare better but at other times the demands of the shipping exhaust the uncultivated resources of the island and the lands being mostly owned by the chiefs the inferior orders have to suffer for their cupidity
__label__MELVILLE deprived of their nets many of them would starve
__label__MELVILLE as captain bob insensibly remitted his watchfulness and we began to stroll farther and farther from the calabooza we managed by a systematic foraging upon the country round about to make up some of our deficiencies
__label__MELVILLE and fortunate it was that the houses of the wealthier natives were just as open to us as those of the most destitute we were treated as kindly in one as the other
__label__MELVILLE once in a while we came in at the death of a chiefs pig the noise of whose slaughtering was generally to be heard at a great distance
__label__MELVILLE an occasion like this gathers the neighbours together and they have a bit of a feast where a stranger is always welcome
__label__MELVILLE a good loud squeal therefore was music in our ears
__label__MELVILLE it showed something going on in that direction
__label__MELVILLE breaking in upon the party tumultuously as we did we always created a sensation
__label__MELVILLE sometimes we found the animal still alive and struggling in which case it was generally dropped at our approach
__label__MELVILLE to provide for these emergencies flash jack generally repaired to the scene of operations with a sheath knife between his teeth and a club in his hand
__label__MELVILLE others were exceedingly officious in singeing off the bristles and disembowelling
__label__MELVILLE doctor long ghost and myself however never meddled with these preliminaries but came to the feast itself with unimpaired energies
__label__MELVILLE like all lank men my long friend had an appetite of his own
__label__MELVILLE others occasionally went about seeking what they might devour but he was always on the alert
__label__MELVILLE he had an ingenious way of obviating an inconvenience which we all experienced at times
__label__MELVILLE the islanders seldom use salt with their food so he begged rope yarn to bring him some from the ship also a little pepper if he could which accordingly was done
__label__MELVILLE this he placed in a small leather wallet a monkey bag so called by sailors usually worn as a purse about the neck
__label__MELVILLE in my opinion said long ghost as he tucked the wallet out of sight it behooves a stranger in tahiti to have his knife in readiness and his castor slung
__label__MELVILLE visit from an old acquaintance
__label__MELVILLE we had not been many days ashore when doctor johnson was espied coming along the broom road
__label__MELVILLE we had heard that he meditated a visit and suspected what he was after
__label__MELVILLE being upon the consuls hands all our expenses were of course payable by him in his official capacity and therefore as a friend of wilson and sure of good pay the shore doctor had some idea of allowing us to run up a bill with him
__label__MELVILLE true it was rather awkward to ask us to take medicines which on board the ship he told us were not needed
__label__MELVILLE however he resolved to put a bold face on the matter and give us a call
__label__MELVILLE his approach was announced by one of the scouts upon which someone suggested that we should let him enter and then put him in the stocks
__label__MELVILLE but long ghost proposed better sport
__label__MELVILLE what it was we shall presently see
__label__MELVILLE very bland and amiable doctor johnson advanced and resting his cane on the stocks glanced to right and left as we lay before him
__label__MELVILLE well my lads he began how do you find yourselves to day
__label__MELVILLE looking very demure the men made some rejoinder and he went on
__label__MELVILLE those poor fellows i saw the other day the sick i mean how are they
__label__MELVILLE and he scrutinized the company
__label__MELVILLE at last he singled out one who was assuming a most unearthly appearance and remarked that he looked as if he were extremely ill yes said the sailor dolefully im afeard doctor ill soon be losing the number of my mess
__label__MELVILLE a sea phrase for departing this life and he closed his eyes and moaned
__label__MELVILLE what does he say
__label__MELVILLE said johnson turning round eagerly

__label__MELVILLE croak
__label__MELVILLE and what does that mean applied to a patient
__label__MELVILLE oh
__label__MELVILLE i understand said he when the word was explained and he stepped over the stocks and felt the mans pulse
__label__MELVILLE whats his name
__label__MELVILLE he asked turning this time to old navy bob
__label__MELVILLE we calls him jingling joe replied that worthy
__label__MELVILLE well then men you must take good care of poor joseph and i will send him a powder which must be taken according to the directions
__label__MELVILLE some of you know how to read i presume
__label__MELVILLE that ere young cove does replied bob pointing toward the place where i lay as if he were directing attention to a sail at sea
__label__MELVILLE after examining the rest some of whom were really invalids but convalescent and others only pretending to be labouring under divers maladies johnson turned round and addressed the party
__label__MELVILLE men said he if any more of you are ailing speak up and let me know
__label__MELVILLE by order of the consul im to call every day so if any of you are at all sick its my duty to prescribe for you
__label__MELVILLE this sudden change from ship fare to shore living plays the deuce with you sailors so be cautious about eating fruit
__label__MELVILLE good day
__label__MELVILLE ill send you the medicines the first thing in the morning
__label__MELVILLE now i am inclined to suspect that with all his want of understanding johnson must have had some idea that we were quizzing him
__label__MELVILLE still that was nothing so long as it answered his purpose and therefore if he did see through us he never showed it
__label__MELVILLE sure enough at the time appointed along came a native lad with a small basket of cocoa nut stalks filled with powders pill boxes and vials each with names and directions written in a large round hand
__label__MELVILLE the sailors one and all made a snatch at the collection under the strange impression that some of the vials were seasoned with spirits
__label__MELVILLE but asserting his privilege as physician to the first reading of the labels doctor long ghost was at last permitted to take possession of the basket
__label__MELVILLE the first thing lighted upon was a large vial labelled for william rub well in
__label__MELVILLE this vial certainly had a spirituous smell and upon handing it to the patient he made a summary internal application of its contents
__label__MELVILLE the doctor looked aghast
__label__MELVILLE there was now a mighty commotion
__label__MELVILLE powders and pills were voted mere drugs in the market and the holders of vials were pronounced lucky dogs
__label__MELVILLE johnson must have known enough of sailors to make some of his medicines palatable this at least long ghost suspected
__label__MELVILLE certain it was everyone took to the vials if at all spicy directions were unheeded their contents all going one road
__label__MELVILLE the largest one of all quite a bottle indeed and having a sort of burnt brandy odour was labelled for daniel drink freely and until relieved
__label__MELVILLE this black dan proceeded to do and would have made an end of it at once had not the bottle after a hard struggle been snatched from his hands and passed round like a jovial decanter
__label__MELVILLE the old tar had complained of the effects of an immoderate eating of fruit
__label__MELVILLE upon calling the following morning our physician found his precious row of patients reclining behind the stocks and doing as well as could be expected
__label__MELVILLE but the pills and powders were found to have been perfectly inactive probably because none had been taken
__label__MELVILLE to make them efficacious it was suggested that for the future a bottle of pisco should be sent along with them
__label__MELVILLE according to flash jacks notions unmitigated medical compounds were but dry stuff at the best and needed something good to wash them down
__label__MELVILLE thus far our own md doctor long ghost after starting the frolic had taken no further part in it but on the physicians third visit he took him to one side and had a private confabulation
__label__MELVILLE what it was exactly we could not tell but from certain illustrative signs and gestures i fancied that he was describing the symptoms of some mysterious disorganization of the vitals which must have come on within the hour
__label__MELVILLE assisted by his familiarity with medical terms he seemed to produce a marked impression
__label__MELVILLE at last johnson went his way promising aloud that he would send long ghost what he desired
__label__MELVILLE when the medicine boy came along the following morning the doctor was the first to accost him walking off with a small purple vial
__label__MELVILLE this time there was little else in the basket but a case bottle of the burnt brandy cordial which after much debate was finally disposed of by someone pouring the contents little by little into the half of a cocoa nut shell and so giving all who desired a glass
__label__MELVILLE no further medicinal cheer remaining the men dispersed
__label__MELVILLE an hour or two passed when flash jack directed attention to my long friend who since the medicine boy left had not been noticed till now
__label__MELVILLE with eyes closed he was lying behind the stocks and jack was lifting his arm and letting it fall as if life were extinct

__label__MELVILLE searching his pocket i found it and holding it up it proved to be laudanum
__label__MELVILLE flash jack snatching it from my hand in a rapture quickly informed all present what it was and with much glee proposed a nap for the company
__label__MELVILLE some of them not comprehending him exactly the apparently defunct long ghost who lay so still that i a little suspected the genuineness of his sleep was rolled about as an illustration of the virtues of the vials contents
__label__MELVILLE the idea tickled everybody mightily and throwing themselves down the magic draught was passed from hand to hand
__label__MELVILLE thinking that as a matter of course they must at once become insensible each man upon taking his sip fell back and closed his eyes
__label__MELVILLE there was little fear of the result since the narcotic was equally distributed
__label__MELVILLE but curious to see how it would operate i raised myself gently after a while and looked around

__label__MELVILLE still in one or two instances i thought i detected a little peeping
__label__MELVILLE presently i heard a footstep and saw doctor johnson approaching
__label__MELVILLE and perplexed enough did he look at the sight of his prostrate file of patients plunged apparently in such unaccountable slumbers

__label__MELVILLE do you hear
__label__MELVILLE but black dan was immovable and he poked the next sleeper
__label__MELVILLE joseph joseph
__label__MELVILLE come wake up
__label__MELVILLE its me doctor johnson
__label__MELVILLE but jingling joe with mouth open and eyes shut was not to be started
__label__MELVILLE bless my soul
__label__MELVILLE he exclaimed with uplifted hands and cane whats got into em
__label__MELVILLE i say men he shouted running up and down come to life men
__label__MELVILLE what under the suns the matter with you
__label__MELVILLE and he struck the stocks and bawled with increased vigour
__label__MELVILLE at last he paused folded his hands over the head of his cane and steadfastly gazed upon us
__label__MELVILLE the notes of the nasal orchestra were rising and falling upon his ear and a new idea suggested itself
__label__MELVILLE yes yes the rascals must have been getting boozy
__label__MELVILLE well its none of my business ill be off and off he went
__label__MELVILLE no sooner was he out of sight than nearly all started to their feet and a hearty laugh ensued
__label__MELVILLE like myself most of them had been watching the event from under a sly eyelid
__label__MELVILLE by this time too doctor long ghost was as wide awake as anybody
__label__MELVILLE what were his reasons for taking laudanum if indeed he took any whatever is best known to himself and as it is neither mine nor the readers business we will say no more about it
__label__MELVILLE we are carried before the consul and captain
__label__MELVILLE we had been inmates of the calabooza beretanee about two weeks when one morning captain bob coming from the bath in a state of utter nudity brought into the building an armful of old tappa and began to dress to go out
__label__MELVILLE the operation was quite simple
__label__MELVILLE the tappa of the coarsest kind was in one long heavy piece and fastening one end to a column of habiscus wood supporting the calabooza he went off a few paces and putting the other about his waist wound himself right up to the post
__label__MELVILLE this unique costume in rotundity something like a farthingale added immensely to his large hulk so much so that he fairly waddled in his gait
__label__MELVILLE but he was only adhering to the fashion of his fathers for in the olden time the kihee or big girdle was quite the mode for both sexes
__label__MELVILLE bob despising recent innovations still clung to it
__label__MELVILLE he was a gentleman of the old school one of the last of the kihees
__label__MELVILLE he now told us that he had orders to take us before the consul
__label__MELVILLE nothing loth we formed in procession and with the old man at our head sighing and labouring like an engine and flanked by a guard of some twenty natives we started for the village
__label__MELVILLE arrived at the consular office we found wilson there and four or five europeans seated in a row facing us probably with the view of presenting as judicial an appearance as possible
__label__MELVILLE on one side was a couch where captain guy reclined
__label__MELVILLE he looked convalescent and as we found out intended soon to go aboard his ship
__label__MELVILLE he said nothing but left everything to the consul
__label__MELVILLE the latter now rose and drawing forth a paper from a large roll tied with red tape commenced reading aloud
__label__MELVILLE it purported to be the affidavit of john jennin first officer of the british colonial barque julia guy master and proved to be a long statement of matters from the time of leaving sydney down to our arrival in the harbour
__label__MELVILLE though artfully drawn up so as to bear hard against every one of us it was pretty correct in the de nan
__label__MELVILLE tails excepting that it was wholly silent as to the manifold derelictions of the mate himself a fact which imparted unusual significance to the concluding sentence and furthermore this deponent sayeth not
__label__MELVILLE no comments were made although we all looked round for the mate to see whether it was possible that he could have authorized this use of his name
__label__MELVILLE but he was not present
__label__MELVILLE the next document produced was the deposition of the captain himself
__label__MELVILLE as on all other occasions however he had very little to say for himself and it was soon set aside
__label__MELVILLE the third affidavit was that of the seamen remaining aboard the vessel including the traitor bungs who it seemed had turned ships evidence
__label__MELVILLE it was an atrocious piece of exaggeration from beginning to end and those who signed it could not have known what they were about
__label__MELVILLE certainly wymontoo did not though his mark was there
__label__MELVILLE in vain the consul commanded silence during the reading of this paper comments were shouted out upon every paragraph
__label__MELVILLE the affidavits read wilson who all the while looked as stiff as a poker solemnly drew forth the ships articles from their tin case
__label__MELVILLE this document was a discoloured musty bilious looking affair and hard to read
__label__MELVILLE when finished the consul held it up and pointing to the marks of the ships company at the bottom asked us one by one whether we acknowledged the same for our own
__label__MELVILLE whats the use of asking that
__label__MELVILLE said black dan captain guy there knows as well as we they are
__label__MELVILLE silence sir
__label__MELVILLE said wilson who intending to produce a suitable impression by this ridiculous parade was not a little mortified by the old sailors bluntness

__label__MELVILLE the general idea seemed to be that it was done with a view of bouncing or frightening us into submission

__label__MELVILLE you see men that every preparation has been made to send you to sydney for trial

__label__MELVILLE the julia sails on a cruise this day week
__label__MELVILLE do you still refuse duty
__label__MELVILLE we did
__label__MELVILLE hereupon the consul and captain exchanged glances and the latter looked bitterly disappointed
__label__MELVILLE presently i noticed guys eye upon me and for the first time he spoke and told me to come near
__label__MELVILLE i stepped forward
__label__MELVILLE was it not you that was taken off the island
__label__MELVILLE it was
__label__MELVILLE it was you then who owe your life to my humanity
__label__MELVILLE yet this is the gratitude of a sailor mr
__label__MELVILLE wilson
__label__MELVILLE not so sir
__label__MELVILLE and i at once gave him to understand that i was perfectly acquainted with his motives in sending a boat into the bay his crew was reduced and he merely wished to procure the sailor whom he expected to find there
__label__MELVILLE the ship was the means of my deliverance and no thanks to the benevolence of its captain
__label__MELVILLE doctor long ghost also had a word to say
__label__MELVILLE in two masterly sentences he summed up captain guys character to the complete satisfaction of every seaman present
__label__MELVILLE matters were now growing serious especially as the sailors became riotous and talked about taking the consul and the captain back to the calabooza with them
__label__MELVILLE the other judges fidgeted and loudly commanded silence
__label__MELVILLE it was at length restored when wilson for the last time addressing us said something more about the rose and sydney and concluded by reminding us that a week would elapse ere the julia sailed
__label__MELVILLE leaving these hints to operate for themselves he dismissed the party ordering captain bob and his friends to escort us back whence we came
__label__MELVILLE the french priests pay their respects
__label__MELVILLE a day or two after the events just related we were lounging in the calabooza beretanee when we were honoured by a visit from three of the french priests and as about the only notice ever taken of us by the english missionaries was their leaving their cards for us in the shape of a package of tracts we could not help thinking that the frenchmen in making a personal call were at least much better bred
__label__MELVILLE by this time they had settled themselves down quite near our habitation
__label__MELVILLE a pleasant little stroll down the broom road and a rustic cross peeped through the trees and soon you came to as charming a place as one would wish to see a soft knoll planted with old breadfruit trees in front a savannah sloping to a grove of palms and between these glimpses of blue sunny waves
__label__MELVILLE on the summit of the knoll was a rude chapel of bamboos quite small and surmounted by the cross
__label__MELVILLE between the canes at nightfall the natives stole peeps at a small portable altar a crucifix to correspond and gilded candlesticks and censers
__label__MELVILLE their curiosity carried them no further nothing could induce them to worship there
__label__MELVILLE such queer ideas as they entertained of the hated strangers
__label__MELVILLE masses and chants were nothing more than evil spells
__label__MELVILLE as for the priests themselves they were no better than diabolical sorcerers like those who in old times terrified their fathers
__label__MELVILLE close by the chapel was a range of native houses rented from a chief and handsomely furnished
__label__MELVILLE here lived the priests and very comfortably too
__label__MELVILLE they looked sanctimonious enough abroad but that went for nothing since at home in their retreat they were a club of friar tucks holding priestly wassail over many a good cup of red brandy and rising late in the morning
__label__MELVILLE pity it was they couldnt marry pity for the ladies of the island i mean and the cause of morality for what business had the ecclesiastical old bachelors with such a set of trim little native handmaidens
__label__MELVILLE these damsels were their first converts and devoted ones they were
__label__MELVILLE the priests as i have said before were accounted necromancers the appearance of two of our three visitors might have justified the conceit
__label__MELVILLE they were little dried up frenchmen in long straight gowns of black cloth and unsightly three cornered hats so preposterously big that in putting them on the reverend fathers seemed to extinguish themselves
__label__MELVILLE their companion was dressed differently
__label__MELVILLE he wore a sort of yellow flannel morning gown and a broad brimmed manilla hat
__label__MELVILLE large and portly he was also hale and fifty with a complexion like an autumnal leaf handsome blue eyes fine teeth and a racy milesian brogue
__label__MELVILLE in short he was an irishman father murphy by name and as such pretty well known and very thoroughly disliked throughout all the protestant missionary settlements in polynesia
__label__MELVILLE in early youth he had been sent to a religious seminary in france and taking orders there had but once or twice afterwards revisited his native land
__label__MELVILLE father murphy marched up to us briskly and the first words he uttered were to ask whether there were any of his countrymen among us
__label__MELVILLE there were two of them one a lad of sixteen a bright curly headed rascal and being a young irishman of course his name was pat
__label__MELVILLE the other was an ugly and rather melancholy looking scamp one mgee whose prospects in life had been blasted by a premature transportation to sydney
__label__MELVILLE this was the report at least though it might have been scandal
__label__MELVILLE in most of my shipmates were some redeeming qualities but about mgee there was nothing of the kind and forced to consort with him i could not help regretting a thousand times that the gallows had been so tardy
__label__MELVILLE as if impelled against her will to send him into the world nature had done all she could to insure his being taken for what he was
__label__MELVILLE about the eyes there was no mistaking him with a villainous cast in one they seemed suspicious of each other
__label__MELVILLE glancing away from him at once the bluff priest rested his gaze on the good humoured face of pat who with a pleasant roguishness was twigging the enormous hats or hytee belteezers as land beavers are called by sailors from under which like a couple of snails peeped the two little frenchmen
__label__MELVILLE pat and the priest were both from the same town in meath and when this was found out there was no end to the questions of the latter
__label__MELVILLE to him pat seemed a letter from home and said a hundred times as much
__label__MELVILLE after a long talk between these two and a little broken english from the frenchmen our visitors took leave but father murphy had hardly gone a dozen rods when back he came inquiring whether we were in want of anything
__label__MELVILLE yes cried one something to eat
__label__MELVILLE upon this he promised to send us some fresh wheat bread of his own baking a great luxury in tahiti
__label__MELVILLE we all felicitated pat upon picking up such a friend and told him his fortune was made
__label__MELVILLE the next morning a french servant of the priests made his appearance with a small bundle of clothing for our young hibernian and the promised bread for the party
__label__MELVILLE pat being out at the knees and elbows and like the rest of us not full inside the present was acceptable all round
__label__MELVILLE in the afternoon father murphy himself came along and in addition to his previous gifts gave pat a good deal of advice said he was sorry to see him in limbo and that he would have a talk with the consul about having him set free
__label__MELVILLE we saw nothing more of him for two or three days at the end of which time he paid us another call telling pat that wilson was inexorable having refused to set him at liberty unless to go aboard the ship
__label__MELVILLE this the priest now besought him to do forthwith and so escape the punishment which it seems wilson had been hinting at to his intercessor
__label__MELVILLE pat however was staunch against entreaties and with all the ardour of a sophomorean sailor protested his intention to hold out to the last
__label__MELVILLE with none of the meekness of a good little boy about him the blunt youngster stormed away at such a rate that it was hard to pacify him and the priest said no more
__label__MELVILLE how it came to pass whether from murphys speaking to the consul or otherwise we could not tell but the next day pat was sent for by wilson and being escorted to the village by our good old keeper three days elapsed before he returned
__label__MELVILLE bent upon reclaiming him they had taken him on board the ship feasted him in the cabin and finding that of no avail down they thrust him into the hold in double irons and on bread and water
__label__MELVILLE all would not do and so he was sent back to the calabooza
__label__MELVILLE boy that he was they must have counted upon his being more susceptible to discipline than the rest
__label__MELVILLE the interest felt in pats welfare by his benevolent countryman was very serviceable to the rest of us especially as we all turned catholics and went to mass every morning much to captain bobs consternation
__label__MELVILLE upon finding it out he threatened to keep us in the stocks if we did not desist
__label__MELVILLE he went no farther than this though and so every few days we strolled down to the priests residence and had a mouthful to eat and something generous to drink
__label__MELVILLE in particular dr long ghost and myself became huge favourites with pats friend and many a time he regaled us from a quaint looking travelling case for spirits stowed away in one corner of his dwelling
__label__MELVILLE it held four square flasks which somehow or other always contained just enough to need emptying
__label__MELVILLE in truth the fine old irishman was a rosy fellow in canonicals
__label__MELVILLE his countenance and his soul were always in a glow
__label__MELVILLE it may be ungenerous to reveal his failings but he often talked thick and sometimes was perceptibly eccentric in his gait
__label__MELVILLE i never drink french brandy but i pledge father murphy
__label__MELVILLE his health again
__label__MELVILLE and many jolly proselytes may he make in polynesia
__label__MELVILLE little julia sails without us
__label__MELVILLE to make good the hint thrown out by the consul upon the conclusion of the farce of the affidavits we were again brought before him within the time specified
__label__MELVILLE it was the same thing over again he got nothing out of us and we were remanded our resolute behaviour annoying him prodigiously
__label__MELVILLE what we observed led us to form the idea that on first learning the state of affairs on board the julia wilson must have addressed his invalid friend the captain something in the following style
__label__MELVILLE guy my poor fellow dont worry yourself now about those rascally sailors of yours
