__label__MELVILLE but handcuffs and stocks big looks threats dark hints and depositions had all gone for nought
__label__MELVILLE conscious that as matters now stood nothing serious could grow out of what had happened and never dreaming that our being sent home for trial had ever been really thought of we thoroughly understood wilson and laughed at him accordingly
__label__MELVILLE since leaving the julia we had caught no glimpse of the mate but we often heard of him
__label__MELVILLE it seemed that he remained on board keeping house in the cabin for himself and viner who going to see him according to promise was induced to remain a guest
__label__MELVILLE these two cronies now had fine times tapping the captains quarter casks playing cards on the transom and giving balls of an evening to the ladies ashore
__label__MELVILLE in short they cut up so many queer capers that the missionaries complained of them to the consul and jermin received a sharp reprimand
__label__MELVILLE this so affected him that he still drank more freely than before and one afternoon when mellow as a grape he took umbrage at a canoe full of natives who on being hailed from the deck to come aboard and show their papers got frightened and paddled for the shore
__label__MELVILLE lowering a boat instantly he equipped wymontoo and the dane with a cutlass apiece and seizing another himself off they started in pursuit the ships ensign flying in the boats stern
__label__MELVILLE the alarmed islanders beaching their canoe with loud cries fled through the village the mate after them slashing his naked weapon to right and left
__label__MELVILLE a crowd soon collected and the karhowree toonee or crazy stranger was quickly taken before wilson
__label__MELVILLE now it so chanced that in a native house hard by the consul and captain guy were having a quiet game at cribbage by themselves a decanter on the table standing sentry
__label__MELVILLE the obstreperous jermin was brought in and finding the two thus pleasantly occupied it had a soothing effect upon him and he insisted upon taking a hand at the cards and a drink of the brandy
__label__MELVILLE as the consul was nearly as tipsy as himself and the captain dared not object for fear of giving offence at it they went all three of them and made a night of it the mates delinquencies being summarily passed over and his captors sent away
__label__MELVILLE an incident worth relating grew out of this freak
__label__MELVILLE there wandered about papeetee at this time a shrivelled little fright of an englishwoman known among sailors as old mother tot
__label__MELVILLE from new zealand to the sandwich islands she had been all over the south seas keeping a rude hut of entertainment for mariners and supplying them with rum and dice
__label__MELVILLE upon the missionary islands of course such conduct was severely punishable and at various places mother tots establishment had been shut up and its proprietor made to quit in the first vessel that could be hired to land her elsewhere
__label__MELVILLE but with a perseverance invincible wherever she went she always started afresh and so became notorious everywhere
__label__MELVILLE by some wicked spell of hers a patient one eyed little cobbler followed her about mending shoes for white men doing the old womans cooking and bearing all her abuse without grumbling
__label__MELVILLE strange to relate a battered bible was seldom out of his sight and whenever he had leisure and his mistress back was turned he was forever poring over it
__label__MELVILLE this pious propensity used to enrage the old crone past belief and oftentimes she boxed his ears with the book and tried to burn it
__label__MELVILLE mother tot and her man josy were indeed a curious pair
__label__MELVILLE but to my story
__label__MELVILLE a week or so after our arrival in the harbour the old lady had once again been hunted down and forced for the time to abandon her nefarious calling
__label__MELVILLE this was brought about chiefly by wilson who for some reason unknown had contracted the most violent hatred for her which on her part was more than reciprocated
__label__MELVILLE well passing in the evening where the consul and his party were making merry she peeped through the bamboos of the house and straightway resolved to gratify her spite
__label__MELVILLE the night was very dark and providing herself with a huge ships lantern which usually swung in her hut she waited till they came forth
__label__MELVILLE this happened about midnight wilson making his appearance supported by two natives holding him up by the arms
__label__MELVILLE these three went first and just as they got under a deep shade a bright light was thrust within an inch of wilsons nose
__label__MELVILLE the old hag was kneeling before him holding the lantern with uplifted hands
__label__MELVILLE ha ha
__label__MELVILLE my fine counsellor she shrieked ye persecute a lone old body like me for selling rum do ye
__label__MELVILLE and here ye are carried home drunk hoot
__label__MELVILLE ye villain i scorn ye
__label__MELVILLE and she spat upon him
__label__MELVILLE terrified at the apparition the poor natives arrant believers in ghosts dropped the trembling consul and fled in all directions
__label__MELVILLE after giving full vent to her rage mother tot hobbled away and left the three revellers to stagger home the best way they could
__label__MELVILLE the day following our last interview with wilson we learned that captain guy had gone on board his vessel for the purpose of shipping a new crew
__label__MELVILLE there was a round bounty offered and a heavy bag of spanish dollars with the julias articles ready for signing were laid on the capstan head
__label__MELVILLE now there was no lack of idle sailors ashore mostly beachcombers who had formed themselves into an organized gang headed by one mack a scotchman whom they styled the commodore
__label__MELVILLE by the laws of the fraternity no member was allowed to ship on board a vessel unless granted permission by the rest
__label__MELVILLE in this way the gang controlled the port all discharged seamen being forced to join them
__label__MELVILLE to mack and his men our story was well known indeed they had several times called to see us and of course as sailors and congenial spirits they were hard against captain guy
__label__MELVILLE deeming the matter important they came in a body to the calabooza and wished to know whether all things considered we thought it best for any of them to join the julia
__label__MELVILLE anxious to pack the ship off as soon as possible we answered by all means
__label__MELVILLE some went so far as to laud the julia to the skies as the best and fastest of ships
__label__MELVILLE jermin too as a good fellow and a sailor every inch came in for his share of praise and as for the captain quiet man he would never trouble anyone
__label__MELVILLE in short every inducement we could think of was presented and plash jack ended by assuring the beachcombers solemnly that now we were all well and hearty nothing but a regard to principle prevented us from returning on board ourselves
__label__MELVILLE the result was that a new crew was finally obtained together with a steady new englander for second mate and three good whalemen for harpooners
__label__MELVILLE in part what was wanting for the ships larder was also supplied and as far as could be done in a place like tahiti the damages the vessel had sustained were repaired
__label__MELVILLE as for the mowree the authorities refusing to let him be put ashore he was carried to sea in irons down in the hold
__label__MELVILLE what eventually became of him we never heard
__label__MELVILLE ropey poor poor ropey who a few days previous had fallen sick was left ashore at the sailor hospital at townor a small place upon the beach between papeetee and matavai
__label__MELVILLE here some time after he breathed his last
__label__MELVILLE no one knew his complaint he must have died of hard times
__label__MELVILLE several of us saw him interred in the sand and i planted a rude post to mark his resting place
__label__MELVILLE the cooper and the rest who had remained aboard from the first of course composed part of the julias new crew
__label__MELVILLE to account for the conduct all along of the consul and captain in trying so hard to alter our purpose with respect to the ship the following statement is all that is requisite
__label__MELVILLE beside an advance of from fifteen to twenty five dollars demanded by every sailor shipping at tahiti an additional sum for each man so shipped has to be paid into the hands of the government as a charge of the port
__label__MELVILLE beside this the men with here and there an exception will only ship for one cruise thus becoming entitled to a discharge before the vessel reaches home which in time creates the necessity of obtaining other men at a similar cost
__label__MELVILLE now the julias exchequer was at low water mark or rather it was quite empty and to meet these expenses a good part of what little oil there was aboard had to be sold for a song to a merchant of papeetee
__label__MELVILLE it was sunday in tahiti and a glorious morning when captain bob waddling into the calabooza startled us by announcing ah my boy shippy you harre maky sail
__label__MELVILLE in other words the julia was off
__label__MELVILLE the beach was quite near and in this quarter altogether uninhabited so down we ran and at cables length saw little jule gliding past top gallant sails hoisting and a boy aloft with one leg thrown over the yard loosing the fore royal
__label__MELVILLE the decks were all life and commotion the sailors on the forecastle singing ho cheerly men
__label__MELVILLE as they catted the anchor and the gallant jennin bare headed as his wont standing up on the bowsprit and issuing his orders
__label__MELVILLE by the man at the helm stood captain guy very quiet and gentlemanly and smoking a cigar
__label__MELVILLE soon the ship drew near the reef and altering her course glided out through the break and went on her way
__label__MELVILLE thus disappeared little jule about three weeks after entering the harbour and nothing more have i ever heard of her
__label__MELVILLE jermin serves us a good turn friendships in polynesia
__label__MELVILLE the ship out of the way we were quite anxious to know what was going to be done with us
__label__MELVILLE on this head captain bob could tell us nothing no further at least than that he still considered himself responsible for our safe keeping
__label__MELVILLE however he never put us to bed any more and we had everything our own way
__label__MELVILLE the day after the julia left the old man came up to us in great tribulation saying that the bucket of bread was no longer forthcoming and that wilson had refused to send anything in its place
__label__MELVILLE one and all we took this for a hint to disperse quietly and go about our business
__label__MELVILLE nevertheless we were not to be shaken off so easily and taking a malicious pleasure in annoying our old enemy we resolved for the present to stay where we were
__label__MELVILLE for the part he had been acting we learned that the consul was the laughing stock of all the foreigners ashore who frequently twitted him upon his hopeful proteges of the calabooza beretanee
__label__MELVILLE as we were wholly without resources so long as we remained on the island no better place than captain bobs could be selected for an abiding place
__label__MELVILLE beside we heartily loved the old gentleman and could not think of leaving him so telling him to give no thought as to wherewithal we should be clothed and fed we resolved by extending and systematizing our foraging operations to provide for ourselves
__label__MELVILLE we were greatly assisted by a parting legacy of jermins
__label__MELVILLE to him we were indebted for having all our chests sent ashore and everything left therein
__label__MELVILLE they were placed in the custody of a petty chief living near by who was instructed by the consul not to allow them to be taken away but we might call and make our toilets whenever we pleased
__label__MELVILLE we went to see mahinee the old chief captain bob going along and stoutly insisting upon having the chattels delivered up
__label__MELVILLE at last this was done and in solemn procession the chests were borne by the natives to the calabooza
__label__MELVILLE here we disposed them about quite tastefully and made such a figure that in the eyes of old bob and his friends the calabooza beretanee was by far the most sumptuously furnished saloon in tahiti
__label__MELVILLE indeed so long as it remained thus furnished the native courts of the district were held there the judge mahinee and his associates sitting upon one of the chests and the culprits and spectators thrown at full length upon the ground both inside of the building and under the shade of the trees without while leaning over the stocks as from a gallery the worshipful crew of the julia looked on and canvassed the proceedings
__label__MELVILLE i should have mentioned before that previous to the vessels departure the men had bartered away all the clothing they could possibly spare but now it was resolved to be more provident
__label__MELVILLE the contents of the chests were of the most miscellaneous description sewing utensils marling spikes strips of calico bits of rope jack knives nearly everything in short that a seaman could think of
__label__MELVILLE but of wearing apparel there was little but old frocks remnants of jackets and legs of trousers with now and then the foot of a stocking
__label__MELVILLE these however were far from being valueless for among the poorer tahitians everything european is highly esteemed
__label__MELVILLE they come from beretanee fenooa pararee britain land of wonders and that is enough
__label__MELVILLE the chests themselves were deemed exceedingly precious especially those with unfractured looks which would absolutely click and enable the owner to walk off with the key
__label__MELVILLE scars however and bruises were considered great blemishes
__label__MELVILLE one old fellow smitten with the doctors large mahogany chest a well filled one by the bye and finding infinite satisfaction in merely sitting thereon was detected in the act of applying a healing ointment to a shocking scratch which impaired the beauty of the lid
__label__MELVILLE there is no telling the love of a tahitian for a sailors trunk
__label__MELVILLE so ornamental is it held as an article of furniture in the hut that the women are incessantly tormenting their husbands to bestir themselves and make them a present of one
__label__MELVILLE when obtained no pier table just placed in a drawing room is regarded with half the delight
__label__MELVILLE for these reasons then our coming into possession of our estate at this time was an important event
__label__MELVILLE the islanders are much like the rest of the world and the news of our good fortune brought us troops of tayos or friends eager to form an alliance after the national custom and do our slightest bidding
__label__MELVILLE the really curious way in which all the polynesians are in the habit of making bosom friends at the shortest possible notice is deserving of remark
__label__MELVILLE although among a people like the tahitians vitiated as they are by sophisticating influences this custom has in most cases degenerated into a mere mercenary relation it nevertheless had its origin in a fine and in some instances heroic sentiment formerly entertained by their fathers
__label__MELVILLE in the annals of the island are examples of extravagant friendships unsurpassed by the story of damon and pythias in truth much more wonderful for notwithstanding the devotion even of life in some cases to which they led they were frequently entertained at first sight for some stranger from another island
__label__MELVILLE filled with love and admiration for the first whites who came among them the polynesians could not testify the warmth of their emotions more strongly than by instantaneously making their abrupt proffer of friendship
__label__MELVILLE hence in old voyages we read of chiefs coming off from the shore in their canoes and going through with strange antics expressive of the desire
__label__MELVILLE in the same way their inferiors accosted the seamen and thus the practice has continued in some islands down to the present day
__label__MELVILLE there is a small place not many days sail from tahiti and seldom visited by shipping where the vessel touched to which i then happened to belong
__label__MELVILLE of course among the simple hearted natives we had a friend all round
__label__MELVILLE mine was poky a handsome youth who never could do enough for me
__label__MELVILLE every morning at sunrise his canoe came alongside loaded with fruits of all kinds upon being emptied it was secured by a line to the bowsprit under which it lay all day long ready at any time to carry its owner ashore on an errand
__label__MELVILLE seeing him so indefatigable i told poky one day that i was a virtuoso in shells and curiosities of all kinds
__label__MELVILLE that was enough away he paddled for the head of the bay and i never saw him again for twenty four hours
__label__MELVILLE the next morning his canoe came gliding slowly along the shore with the full leaved bough of a tree for a sail
__label__MELVILLE for the purpose of keeping the things dry he had also built a sort of platform just behind the prow railed in with green wicker work and here was a heap of yellow bananas and cowree shells young cocoa nuts and antlers of red coral two or three pieces of carved wood a little pocket idol black as jet and rolls of printed tappa
__label__MELVILLE we were given a holiday and upon going ashore poky of course was my companion and guide
__label__MELVILLE for this no mortal could be better qualified his native country was not large and he knew every inch of it
__label__MELVILLE gallanting me about everyone was stopped and ceremoniously introduced to potys tayo karhowree nuee or his particular white friend
__label__MELVILLE he showed me all the lions but more than all he took me to see a charming lioness a young damsel the daughter of a chief the reputation of whose charms had spread to the neighbouring islands and even brought suitors therefrom
__label__MELVILLE among these was tooboi the heir of tamatory king of eaiatair one of the society isles
__label__MELVILLE the girl was certainly fair to look upon
__label__MELVILLE many heavens were in her sunny eyes and the outline of that arm of hers peeping forth from a capricious tappa robe was the very curve of beauty
__label__MELVILLE though there was no end to pokys attentions not a syllable did he ever breathe of reward but sometimes he looked very knowing
__label__MELVILLE at last the day came for sailing and with it also his canoe loaded down to the gunwale with a sea stock of fruits
__label__MELVILLE giving him all i could spare from my chest i went on deck to take my place at the windlass for the anchor was weighing
__label__MELVILLE poky followed and heaved with me at the same handspike
__label__MELVILLE the anchor was soon up and away we went out of the bay with more than twenty shallops towing astern
__label__MELVILLE at last they left us but long as i could see him at all there was poky standing alone and motionless in the bow of his canoe
__label__MELVILLE part ii
__label__MELVILLE we take unto ourselves friends
__label__MELVILLE the arrival of the chests made my friend the doctor by far the wealthiest man of the party
__label__MELVILLE so much the better for me seeing that i had little or nothing myself though from our intimacy the natives courted my favour almost as much as his
__label__MELVILLE among others kooloo was a candidate for my friendship and being a comely youth quite a buck in his way i accepted his overtures
__label__MELVILLE by this i escaped the importunities of the rest for be it known that though little inclined to jealousy in love matters the tahitian will hear of no rivals in his friendship
__label__MELVILLE kooloo running over his qualifications as a friend first of all informed me that he was a mickonaree thus declaring his communion with the church
__label__MELVILLE the way this tayo of mine expressed his regard was by assuring me over and over again that the love he bore me was nuee nuee nuee or infinitesimally extensive
__label__MELVILLE all over these seas the word nuee is significant of quantity
__label__MELVILLE its repetition is like placing ciphers at the right hand of a numeral the more places you carry it out to the greater the sum
__label__MELVILLE judge then of kooloos esteem
__label__MELVILLE nor is the allusion to the ciphers at all inappropriate seeing that in themselves kooloos profession turned out to be worthless
__label__MELVILLE he was alas
__label__MELVILLE as sounding brass and a tinkling cymbal one of those who make no music unless the clapper be silver
__label__MELVILLE in the course of a few days the sailors like the doctor and myself were cajoled out of everything and our tayos all round began to cool off quite sensibly
__label__MELVILLE so remiss did they become in their attentions that we could no longer rely upon their bringing us the daily supply of food which all of them had faithfully promised
__label__MELVILLE as for kooloo after sponging me well he one morning played the part of a retrograde lover informing me that his affections had undergone a change he had fallen in love at first sight with a smart sailor who had just stepped ashore quite flush from a lucky whaling cruise
__label__MELVILLE it was a touching interview and with it our connection dissolved
__label__MELVILLE but the sadness which ensued would soon have been dissipated had not my sensibilities been wounded by his indelicately sporting some of my gifts very soon after this transfer of his affections
__label__MELVILLE hardly a day passed that i did not meet him on the broom road airing himself in a regatta shirt which i had given him in happier hours
__label__MELVILLE he went by with such an easy saunter too looking me pleasantly in the eye and merely exchanging the cold salute of the road yar onor boyoee a mere sidewalk how dye do
__label__MELVILLE after several experiences like this i began to entertain a sort of respect for kooloo as quite a man of the world
__label__MELVILLE in good sooth he turned out to be one in one weeks time giving me the cut direct and lounging by without even nodding
__label__MELVILLE he must have taken me for part of the landscape
__label__MELVILLE before the chests were quite empty we had a grand washing in the stream of our best raiment for the purpose of looking tidy and visiting the european chapel in the village
__label__MELVILLE every sunday morning it is open for divine service some member of the mission officiating
__label__MELVILLE this was the first time we ever entered papeetee unattended by an escort
__label__MELVILLE in the chapel there were about forty people present including the officers of several ships in harbour
__label__MELVILLE it was an energetic discourse and the pulpit cushion was well pounded
__label__MELVILLE occupying a high seat in the synagogue and stiff as a flagstaff was our beloved guardian wilson
__label__MELVILLE i shall never forget his look of wonder when his interesting wards filed in at the doorway and took up a seat directly facing him
__label__MELVILLE service over we waited outside in hopes of seeing more of him but sorely annoyed at the sight of us he reconnoitred from the window and never came forth until we had started for home
__label__MELVILLE we levy contributions on the shipping
__label__MELVILLE scarcely a week went by after the julias sailing when with the proverbial restlessness of sailors some of the men began to grow weary of the calabooza beretanee and resolved to go boldly among the vessels in the bay and offer to ship
__label__MELVILLE the thing was tried but though strongly recommended by the commodore of the beachcombers in the end they were invariably told by the captains to whom they applied that they bore an equivocal character ashore and would not answer
__label__MELVILLE so often were they repulsed that we pretty nearly gave up all thoughts of leaving the island in this way and growing domestic again settled down quietly at captain bobs
__label__MELVILLE it was about this time that the whaling ships which have their regular seasons for cruising began to arrive at papeetee and of course their crews frequently visited us
__label__MELVILLE this is customary all over the pacific
__label__MELVILLE no sailor steps ashore but he straightway goes to the calabooza where he is almost sure to find some poor fellow or other in confinement for desertion or alleged mutiny or something of that sort
__label__MELVILLE sympathy is proffered and if need be tobacco
__label__MELVILLE the latter however is most in request as a solace to the captive it is invaluable
__label__MELVILLE having fairly carried the day against both consul and captain we were objects of even more than ordinary interest to these philanthropists and they always cordially applauded our conduct
__label__MELVILLE besides they invariably brought along something in the way of refreshments occasionally smuggling in a little pisco
__label__MELVILLE upon one occasion when there was quite a number present a calabash was passed round and a pecuniary collection taken up for our benefit
__label__MELVILLE one day a newcomer proposed that two or three of us should pay him a sly nocturnal visit aboard his ship engaging to send us away well freighted with provisions
__label__MELVILLE this was not a bad idea nor were we at all backward in acting upon it
__label__MELVILLE right after night every vessel in the harbour was visited in rotation the foragers borrowing captain bobs canoe for the purpose
__label__MELVILLE as we all took turns at this two by two in due course it came to long ghost and myself for the sailors invariably linked us together
__label__MELVILLE in such an enterprise i somewhat distrusted the doctor for he was no sailor and very tall and a canoe is the most ticklish of navigable things
__label__MELVILLE however it could not be helped and so we went
__label__MELVILLE but a word about the canoes before we go any further
__label__MELVILLE among the society islands the art of building them like all native accomplishments has greatly deteriorated and they are now the most inelegant as well as the most insecure of any in the south seas
__label__MELVILLE in cooks time according to his account there was at tahiti a royal fleet of seventeen hundred and twenty large war canoes handsomely carved and otherwise adorned
__label__MELVILLE at present those used are quite small nothing more than logs hollowed out sharpened at one end and then launched into the water
__label__MELVILLE to obviate a certain rolling propensity the tahitians like all polynesians attach to them what sailors call an outrigger
__label__MELVILLE it consists of a pole floating alongside parallel to the canoe and connected with it by a couple of cross sticks a yard or more in length
__label__MELVILLE thus equipped the canoe cannot be overturned unless you overcome the buoyancy of the pole or lift it entirely out of the water
__label__MELVILLE now captain bobs gig was exceedingly small so small and of such a grotesque shape that the sailors christened it the pill box and by this appellation it always went
__label__MELVILLE in fact it was a sort of sulky meant for a solitary paddler but on an emergency capable of floating two or three
__label__MELVILLE the outrigger was a mere switch alternately rising in air and then depressed in the water
__label__MELVILLE assuming the command of the expedition upon the strength of my being a sailor i packed the long doctor with a paddle in the bow and then shoving off leaped into the stern thus leaving him to do all the work and reserving to myself the dignified sinecure of steering
__label__MELVILLE all would have gone on well were it not that my paddler made such clumsy work that the water spattered and showered down upon us without ceasing
__label__MELVILLE continuing to ply his tool however quite energetically i thought he would improve after a while and so let him alone
__label__MELVILLE but by and bye getting wet through with this little storm we were raising and seeing no signs of its clearing off i conjured him in mercys name to stop short and let me wring myself out
__label__MELVILLE upon this he suddenly turned round when the canoe gave a roll the outrigger flew overhead and the next moment came rap on the doctors skull and we were both in the water
__label__MELVILLE fortunately we were just over a ledge of coral not half a fathom under the surface
__label__MELVILLE depressing one end of the filled canoe and letting go of it quickly it bounced up and discharged a great part of its contents so that we easily baled out the remainder and again embarked
__label__MELVILLE this time my comrade coiled himself away in a very small space and enjoining upon him not to draw a single unnecessary breath i proceeded to urge the canoe along by myself
__label__MELVILLE i was astonished at his docility never speaking a word and stirring neither hand nor foot but the secret was he was unable to swim and in case we met with a second mishap there were no more ledges beneath to stand upon
__label__MELVILLE crownings but a shabby way of going out of the world he exclaimed upon my rallying him and im not going to be guilty of it
__label__MELVILLE at last the ship was at hand and we approached with much caution wishing to avoid being hailed by anyone from the quarter deck
__label__MELVILLE dropping silently under her bows we heard a low whistle the signal agreed upon and presently a goodly sized bag was lowered over to us
__label__MELVILLE we cut the line and then paddled away as fast as we could and made the best of our way home
__label__MELVILLE here we found the rest waiting impatiently
__label__MELVILLE the bag turned out to be well filled with sweet potatoes boiled cubes of salt beef and pork and a famous sailors pudding what they call duff made of flour and water and of about the consistence of an underdone brick
__label__MELVILLE with these delicacies and keen appetites we went out into the moonlight and had a nocturnal picnic
__label__MELVILLE motoo otoo a tahitian casuist
__label__MELVILLE the pill box was sometimes employed for other purposes than that described in the last chapter
__label__MELVILLE we sometimes went a pleasuring in it
__label__MELVILLE right in the middle of papeetee harbour is a bright green island one circular grove of waving palms and scarcely a hundred yards across
__label__MELVILLE it is of coral formation and all round for many rods out the bay is so shallow that you might wade anywhere
__label__MELVILLE down in these waters as transparent as air you see coral plants of every hue and shape imaginable antlers tufts of azure waving reeds like stalks of grain and pale green buds and mosses
__label__MELVILLE in some places you look through prickly branches down to a snow white floor of sand sprouting with flinty bulbs and crawling among these are strange shapes some bristling with spikes others clad in shining coats of mail and here and there round forms all spangled with eyes
__label__MELVILLE the island is called hotoo otoo and around hotoo otoo have i often paddled of a white moonlight night pausing now and then to admire the marine gardens beneath
__label__MELVILLE the place is the private property of the queen who has a residence there a melancholy looking range of bamboo houses neglected and falling to decay among the trees
__label__MELVILLE commanding the harbour as it does her majesty has done all she could to make a fortress of the island
__label__MELVILLE the margin has been raised and levelled and built up with a low parapet of hewn hocks of coral
__label__MELVILLE behind the parapet are ranged at wide intervals a number of rusty old cannon of all fashions and calibres
__label__MELVILLE they are mounted upon lame decrepit looking carriages ready to sink under the useless burden of bearing them up
__label__MELVILLE indeed two or three have given up the ghost altogether and the pieces they sustained lie half buried among their bleaching bones
__label__MELVILLE several of the cannon are spiked probably with a view of making them more formidable as they certainly must be to anyone undertaking to fire them off
__label__MELVILLE presented to pomaree at various times by captains of british armed ships these poor old dogs of war thus toothless and turned out to die formerly bayed in full pack as the battle hounds of old england
__label__MELVILLE there was something about hotoo otoo that struck my fancy and i registered a vow to plant my foot upon its soil notwithstanding an old bareheaded sentry menaced me in the moonlight with an unsightly musket
__label__MELVILLE as my canoe drew scarcely three inches of water i could paddle close up to the parapet without grounding but every time i came near the old man ran toward me pushing his piece forward but never clapping it to his shoulder

__label__MELVILLE at last i was obliged to retreat and to this day my vow remains unfulfilled
__label__MELVILLE it was a few days after my repulse from before the walls of hotoo otoo that i heard a curious case of casuistry argued between one of the most clever and intelligent natives i ever saw in tahiti a man by the name of arheetoo and our learned theban of a doctor

__label__MELVILLE for this reason vessels coming round cape horn as they most all do nowadays find it sunday in tahiti when according to their own view of the matter it ought to be saturday
__label__MELVILLE but as it wont do to alter the log the sailors keep their sabbath and the islanders theirs
__label__MELVILLE this confusion perplexes the poor natives mightily and it is to no purpose that you endeavour to explain so incomprehensible a phenomenon
__label__MELVILLE i once saw a worthy old missionary essay to shed some light on the subject and though i understood but a few of the words employed i could easily get at the meaning of his illustrations

__label__MELVILLE cathedral of papoar the church of the cocoa nuts
__label__MELVILLE on sundays i always attended the principal native church on the outskirts of the village of papeetee and not far from the calabooza beretanee
__label__MELVILLE it was esteemed the best specimen of architecture in tahiti
__label__MELVILLE of late they have built their places of worship with more reference to durability than formerly
__label__MELVILLE at one time there were no less than thirty six on the island mere barns tied together with thongs which went to destruction in a very few years
__label__MELVILLE one built many years ago in this style was a most remarkable structure
__label__MELVILLE it was erected by pomaree ii who on this occasion showed all the zeal of a royal proselyte
__label__MELVILLE the building was over seven hundred feet in length and of a proportionate width the vast ridge pole was at intervals supported by a row of thirty six cylindrical trunks of the bread fruit tree and all round the wall plates rested on shafts of the palm
__label__MELVILLE the roof steeply inclining to within a mans height of the ground was thatched with leaves and the sides of the edifice were open

__label__MELVILLE at its dedication three distinct sermons were from different pulpits preached to an immense concourse gathered from all parts of the island
__label__MELVILLE as the chapel was built by the kings command nearly as great a multitude was employed in its construction as swarmed over the scaffolding of the great temple of the jews
__label__MELVILLE much less time however was expended
__label__MELVILLE in less than three weeks from planting the first post the last tier of palmetto leaves drooped from the eaves and the work was done
__label__MELVILLE apportioned to the several chiefs and their dependants the labour though immense was greatly facilitated by everyones bringing his post or his rafter or his pole strung with thatching ready for instant use
__label__MELVILLE the materials thus prepared being afterwards secured together by thongs there was literally neither hammer nor axe nor any tool of iron heard in the house while it was building
__label__MELVILLE but the most singular circumstance connected with this south sea cathedral remains to be related
__label__MELVILLE as well for the beauty as the advantages of such a site the islanders love to dwell near the mountain streams and so a considerable brook after descending from the hills and watering the valley was bridged over in three places and swept clean through the chapel

__label__MELVILLE what an accompaniment to the songs of the sanctuary mingling with them the praises and thanksgivings of the green solitudes inland

__label__MELVILLE it is of moderate dimensions boarded over and painted white
__label__MELVILLE it is furnished also with blinds but no sashes indeed were it not for the rustic thatch it would remind one of a plain chapel at home

__label__MELVILLE for the most part the congregation attending this church is composed of the better and wealthier orders the chiefs and their retainers in short the rank and fashion of the island

__label__MELVILLE and hark
__label__MELVILLE hanging from the bough of a bread fruit tree without a bell is being struck with a bar of iron by a native lad

__label__MELVILLE the place is well filled
__label__MELVILLE everywhere meets the eye the gay calico draperies worn on great occasions by the higher classes and forming a strange contrast of patterns and colours

__label__MELVILLE some degree of order at length restored the service was continued by singing

__label__MELVILLE having been informed from various sources that the discourses of the missionaries being calculated to engage the attention of their simple auditors were naturally enough of a rather amusing description to strangers in short that they had much to say about steamboats lord mayors coaches and the way fires are put out in london i had taken care to provide myself with a good interpreter in the person of an intelligent hawaiian sailor whose acquaintance i had made

__label__MELVILLE such was the substance of great part of this discourse and whatever may be thought of it it was specially adapted to the minds of the islanders who are susceptible to no impressions except from things palpable or novel and striking
__label__MELVILLE to them a dry sermon would be dry indeed
__label__MELVILLE the tahitians can hardly ever be said to reflect they are all impulse and so instead of expounding dogmas the missionaries give them the large type pleasing cuts and short and easy lessons of the primer
__label__MELVILLE hence anything like a permanent religious impression is seldom or never produced
__label__MELVILLE in fact there is perhaps no race upon earth less disposed by nature to the monitions of christianity than the people of the south seas
__label__MELVILLE and this assertion is made with full knowledge of what is called the great revival at the sandwich islands about the year 1836 when several thousands were in the course of a few weeks admitted into the bosom of the church
__label__MELVILLE but this result was brought about by no sober moral convictions as an almost instantaneous relapse into every kind of licentiousness soon after testified
__label__MELVILLE it was the legitimate effect of a morbid feeling engendered by the sense of severe physical wants preying upon minds excessively prone to superstition and by fanatical preaching inflamed into the belief that the gods of the missionaries were taking vengeance upon the wickedness of the land
__label__MELVILLE it is a noteworthy fact that those very traits in the tahitians which induced the london missionary society to regard them as the most promising subjects for conversion and which led moreover to the selection of their island as the very first field for missionary labour eventually proved the most serious obstruction
__label__MELVILLE an air of softness in their manners great apparent ingenuousness and docility at first misled but these were the mere accompaniments of an indolence bodily and mental a constitutional voluptuousness and an aversion to the least restraint which however fitted for the luxurious state of nature in the tropics are the greatest possible hindrances to the strict moralities of christianity
__label__MELVILLE added to all this is a quality inherent in polynesians and more akin to hypocrisy than anything else
__label__MELVILLE it leads them to assume the most passionate interest in matters for which they really feel little or none whatever but in which those whose power they dread or whose favour they court they believe to be at all affected
__label__MELVILLE thus in their heathen state the sandwich islanders actually knocked out their teeth tore their hair and mangled their bodies with shells to testify their inconsolable grief at the demise of a high chief or member of the royal family
__label__MELVILLE and yet vancouver relates that on such an occasion upon which he happened to be present those apparently the most abandoned to their feelings immediately assumed the utmost light heartedness on receiving the present of a penny whistle or a dutch looking glass
__label__MELVILLE similar instances also have come under my own observation
__label__MELVILLE the following is an illustration of the trait alluded to as occasionally manifested among the converted polynesians
__label__MELVILLE at one of the society islands baiatair i believe the natives for special reasons desired to commend themselves particularly to the favour of the missionaries

__label__MELVILLE they pretended to be wrought up to madness by the preaching which they heard
__label__MELVILLE they rolled their eyes foamed at the mouth fell down in fits and so were carried home

__label__MELVILLE the sabbath is no ordinary day with the tahitians
__label__MELVILLE so far as doing any work is concerned it is scrupulously observed
__label__MELVILLE the canoes are hauled up on the beach the nets are spread to dry

__label__MELVILLE after service repose broods over the whole island the valleys reaching inland look stiller than ever

__label__MELVILLE the explanation terminated in a burst of laughter in which all three sisters joined and for fear of looking silly the doctor and myself
__label__MELVILLE as soon as good breeding would permit we took leave
__label__MELVILLE the hypocrisy in matters of religion so apparent in all polynesian converts is most injudiciously nourished in tahiti by a zealous and in many cases a coercive superintendence over their spiritual well being
__label__MELVILLE but it is only manifested with respect to the common people their superiors being exempted
__label__MELVILLE on sunday mornings when the prospect is rather small for a full house in the minor churches a parcel of fellows are actually sent out with ratans into the highways and byways as whippers in of the congregation
__label__MELVILLE this is a sober fact
__label__MELVILLE these worthies constitute a religious police and you always know them by the great white diapers they wear
__label__MELVILLE on week days they are quite as busy as on sundays to the great terror of the inhabitants going all over the island and spying out the wickedness thereof
__label__MELVILLE moreover they are the collectors of fines levied generally in grass mats for obstinate non attendance upon divine worship and other offences amenable to the ecclesiastical judicature of the missionaries
__label__MELVILLE old bob called these fellows kannakippers a corruption i fancy of our word constable
__label__MELVILLE he bore them a bitter grudge and one day drawing near home and learning that two of them were just then making a domiciliary visit at his house he ran behind a bush and as they came forth two green bread fruit from a hand unseen took them each between the shoulders
__label__MELVILLE the sailors in the calabooza were witnesses to this as well as several natives who when the intruders were out of sight applauded captain bobs spirit in no measured terms the ladies present vehemently joining in
__label__MELVILLE indeed the kannakippers have no greater enemies than the latter
__label__MELVILLE and no wonder the impertinent varlets popping into their houses at all hours are forever prying into their peccadilloes
__label__MELVILLE kooloo who at times was patriotic and pensive and mourned the evils under which his country was groaning frequently inveighed against the statute which thus authorized an utter stranger to interfere with domestic arrangements
__label__MELVILLE he himself quite a ladies man had often been annoyed thereby
__label__MELVILLE he considered the kannakippers a bore
__label__MELVILLE beside their confounded inquisitiveness they add insult to injury by making a point of dining out every day at some hut within the limits of their jurisdiction
__label__MELVILLE as for the gentleman of the house his meek endurance of these things is amazing
__label__MELVILLE but good easy man there is nothing for him but to be as hospitable as possible
__label__MELVILLE these gentry are indefatigable
__label__MELVILLE at the dead of night prowling round the houses and in the daytime hunting amorous couples in the groves
__label__MELVILLE yet in one instance the chase completely baffled them
__label__MELVILLE it was thus
__label__MELVILLE several weeks previous to our arrival at the island someones husband and another persons wife having taken a mutual fancy for each other went out for a walk
__label__MELVILLE the alarm was raised and with hue and cry they were pursued but nothing was seen of them again until the lapse of some ninety days when we were called out from the calabooza to behold a great mob inclosing the lovers and escorting them for trial to the village
__label__MELVILLE their appearance was most singular
__label__MELVILLE the girdle excepted they were quite naked their hair was long burned yellow at the ends and entangled with burrs and their bodies scratched and scarred in all directions
__label__MELVILLE it seems that acting upon the love in a cottage principle they had gone right into the interior and throwing up a hut in an uninhabited valley had lived there until in an unlucky stroll they were observed and captured
__label__MELVILLE they were subsequently condemned to make one hundred fathoms of broom road a six months work if not more
__label__MELVILLE often when seated in a house conversing quietly with its inmates i have known them betray the greatest confusion at the sudden announcement of a kannakippers being in sight
__label__MELVILLE to be reported by one of these officials as a tootai owree in general signifying a bad person or disbeliever in christianity is as much dreaded as the forefinger of titus gates was levelled at an alleged papist
__label__MELVILLE but the islanders take a sly revenge upon them
__label__MELVILLE upon entering a dwelling the kannakippers oftentimes volunteer a pharisaical prayer meeting hence they go in secret by the name of boora artuas literally pray to gods
__label__MELVILLE how they dress in tahiti
__label__MELVILLE except where the employment of making tappa is inflicted as a punishment the echoes of the cloth mallet have long since died away in the listless valleys of tahiti
__label__MELVILLE formerly the girls spent their mornings like ladies at their tambour frames now they are lounged away in almost utter indolence
__label__MELVILLE true most of them make their own garments but this comprises but a stitch or two the ladies of the mission by the bye being entitled to the credit of teaching them to sew
__label__MELVILLE the kihee whihenee or petticoat is a mere breadth of white cotton or calico loosely enveloping the person from the waist to the feet
__label__MELVILLE fastened simply by a single tuck or by twisting the upper corners together this garment frequently becomes disordered thus affording an opportunity of being coquettishly adjusted
__label__MELVILLE over the kihee they wear a sort of gown open in front very loose and as negligent as you please
__label__MELVILLE the ladies here never dress for dinner
__label__MELVILLE but what shall be said of those horrid hats
__label__MELVILLE fancy a bunch of straw plaited into the shape of a coal scuttle and stuck bolt upright on the crown with a yard or two of red ribbon flying about like kite strings
__label__MELVILLE milliners of paris what would ye say to them
__label__MELVILLE though made by the natives they are said to have been first contrived and recommended by the missionaries wives a report which i really trust is nothing but scandal
__label__MELVILLE curious to relate these things for the head are esteemed exceedingly becoming
__label__MELVILLE the braiding of the straw is one of the few employments of the higher classes all of which but minister to the silliest vanity
__label__MELVILLE the young girls however wholly eschew the hats leaving those dowdy old souls their mothers to make frights of themselves
__label__MELVILLE as for the men those who aspire to european garments seem to have no perception of the relation subsisting between the various parts of a gentlemans costume
__label__MELVILLE to the wearer of a coat for instance pantaloons are by no means indispensable and a bell crowned hat and a girdle are full dress
__label__MELVILLE the young sailor for whom kooloo deserted me presented him with a shaggy old pea jacket and with this buttoned up to his chin under a tropical sun he promenaded the broom road quite elated
__label__MELVILLE doctor long ghost who saw him thus ran away with the idea that he was under medical treatment at the time in the act of taking what the quacks call a sweat
__label__MELVILLE a bachelor friend of captain bob rejoiced in the possession of a full european suit in which he often stormed the ladies hearts
__label__MELVILLE having a military leaning he ornamented the coat with a great scarlet patch on the breast and mounted it also here and there with several regimental buttons slyly cut from the uniform of a parcel of drunken marines sent ashore on a holiday from a man of war
__label__MELVILLE but in spite of the ornaments the dress was not exactly the thing
__label__MELVILLE from the tightness of the cloth across the shoulders his elbows projected from his sides like an ungainly riders and his ponderous legs were jammed so hard into his slim nether garments that the threads of every seam showed and at every step you looked for a catastrophe
__label__MELVILLE in general there seems to be no settled style of dressing among the males they wear anything they can get in some cases awkwardly modifying the fashions of their fathers so as to accord with their own altered views of what is becoming
__label__MELVILLE but ridiculous as many of them now appear in foreign habiliments the tahitians presented a far different appearance in the original national costume which was graceful in the extreme modest to all but the prudish and peculiarly adapted to the climate
__label__MELVILLE but the short kilts of dyed tappa the tasselled maroes and other articles formerly worn are at the present day prohibited by law as indecorous
__label__MELVILLE for what reason necklaces and garlands of flowers among the women are also forbidden i never could learn but it is said that they were associated in some way with a forgotten heathen observance
__label__MELVILLE many pleasant and seemingly innocent sports and pastimes are likewise interdicted
__label__MELVILLE in old times there were several athletic games practised such as wrestling foot racing throwing the javelin and archery
__label__MELVILLE in all these they greatly excelled and for some splendid festivals were instituted
__label__MELVILLE among their everyday amusements were dancing tossing the football kite flying flute playing and singing traditional ballads now all punishable offences though most of them have been so long in disuse that they are nearly forgotten
__label__MELVILLE in the same way the opio or festive harvest home of the breadfruit has been suppressed though as described to me by captain bob it seemed wholly free from any immoral tendency
__label__MELVILLE against tattooing of any kind there is a severe law
__label__MELVILLE that this abolition of their national amusements and customs was not willingly acquiesced in is shown in the frequent violation of many of the statutes inhibiting them and especially in the frequency with which their hevars or dances are practised in secret
__label__MELVILLE doubtless in thus denationalizing the tahitians as it were the missionaries were prompted by a sincere desire for good but the effect has been lamentable
__label__MELVILLE supplied with no amusements in place of those forbidden the tahitians who require more recreation than other people have sunk into a listlessness or indulge in sensualities a hundred times more pernicious than all the games ever celebrated in the temple of tanee
__label__MELVILLE tahiti as it is
__label__MELVILLE as in the last few chapters several matters connected with the general condition of the natives have been incidentally touched upon it may be well not to leave so important a subject in a state calculated to convey erroneous impressions
__label__MELVILLE let us bestow upon it therefore something more than a mere cursory glance
__label__MELVILLE but in the first place let it be distinctly understood that in all i have to say upon this subject both here and elsewhere i mean no harm to the missionaries nor their cause i merely desire to set forth things as they actually exist
__label__MELVILLE of the results which have flowed from the intercourse of foreigners with the polynesians including the attempts to civilize and christianize them by the missionaries tahiti on many accounts is obviously the fairest practical example
__label__MELVILLE indeed it may now be asserted that the experiment of christianizing the tahitians and improving their social condition by the introduction of foreign customs has been fully tried
__label__MELVILLE the present generation have grown up under the auspices of their religious instructors
__label__MELVILLE and although it may be urged that the labours of the latter have at times been more or less obstructed by unprincipled foreigners still this in no wise renders tahiti any the less a fair illustration for with obstacles like these the missionaries in polynesia must always and everywhere struggle
__label__MELVILLE nearly sixty years have elapsed since the tahitian mission was started and during this period it has received the unceasing prayers and contributions of its friends abroad
__label__MELVILLE nor has any enterprise of the kind called forth more devotion on the part of those directly employed in it
__label__MELVILLE it matters not that the earlier labourers in the work although strictly conscientious were as a class ignorant and in many cases deplorably bigoted such traits have in some degree characterized the pioneers of all faiths
__label__MELVILLE and although in zeal and disinterestedness the missionaries now on the island are perhaps inferior to their predecessors they have nevertheless in their own way at least laboured hard to make a christian people of their charge
__label__MELVILLE let us now glance at the most obvious changes wrought in their condition
__label__MELVILLE the entire system of idolatry has been done away together with several barbarous practices engrafted thereon
__label__MELVILLE but this result is not so much to be ascribed to the missionaries as to the civilizing effects of a long and constant intercourse with whites of all nations to whom for many years tahiti has been one of the principal places of resort in the south seas
__label__MELVILLE at the sandwich islands the potent institution of the taboo together with the entire paganism of the land was utterly abolished by a voluntary act of the natives some time previous to the arrival of the first missionaries among them
__label__MELVILLE the next most striking change in the tahitians is this
__label__MELVILLE from the permanent residence among them of influential and respectable foreigners as well as from the frequent visits of ships of war recognizing the nationality of the island its inhabitants are no longer deemed fit subjects for the atrocities practised upon mere savages and hence secure from retaliation vessels of all kinds now enter their harbours with perfect safety
__label__MELVILLE but let us consider what results are directly ascribable to the missionaries alone
__label__MELVILLE in all cases they have striven hard to mitigate the evils resulting from the commerce with the whites in general
__label__MELVILLE such attempts however have been rather injudicious and often ineffectual in truth a barrier almost insurmountable is presented in the dispositions of the people themselves
__label__MELVILLE still in this respect the morality of the islanders is upon the whole improved by the presence of the missionaries
__label__MELVILLE but the greatest achievement of the latter and one which in itself is most hopeful and gratifying is that they have translated the entire bible into the language of the island and i have myself known several who were able to read it with facility
__label__MELVILLE they have also established churches and schools for both children and adults the latter i regret to say are now much neglected which must be ascribed in a great measure to the disorders growing out of the proceedings of the french
__label__MELVILLE it were unnecessary here to enter diffusely into matters connected with the internal government of the tahitian churches and schools
__label__MELVILLE nor upon this head is my information copious enough to warrant me in presenting details
__label__MELVILLE but we do not need them
__label__MELVILLE we are merely considering general results as made apparent in the moral and religious condition of the island at large
__label__MELVILLE upon a subject like this however it would be altogether too assuming for a single individual to decide and so in place of my own random observations which may be found elsewhere i will here present those of several known authors made under various circumstances at different periods and down to a comparative late date
__label__MELVILLE a few very brief extracts will enable the reader to mark for himself what progressive improvement if any has taken place
__label__MELVILLE nor must it be overlooked that of these authorities the two first in order are largely quoted by the right reverend m kussell in a work composed for the express purpose of imparting information on the subject of christian missions in polynesia
__label__MELVILLE and he frankly acknowledges moreover that they are such as cannot fail to have great weight with the public
__label__MELVILLE after alluding to the manifold evils entailed upon the natives by foreigners and their singularly inert condition and after somewhat too severely denouncing the undeniable errors of the mission kotzebue the russian navigator says a religion like this which forbids every innocent pleasure and cramps or annihilates every mental power is a libel on the divine founder of christianity
__label__MELVILLE it is true that the religion of the missionaries has with a great deal of evil effected some good
__label__MELVILLE it has restrained the vices of theft and incontinence but it has given birth to ignorance hypocrisy and a hatred of all other modes of faith which was once foreign to the open and benevolent character of the tahitian
__label__MELVILLE captain beechy says that while at tahiti he saw scenes which must have convinced the great sceptic of the thoroughly immoral condition of the people and which would force him to conclude as turnbull did many years previous that their intercourse with the europeans had tended to debase rather than exalt their condition
__label__MELVILLE about the year 1834 daniel wheeler an honest hearted quaker prompted by motives of the purest philanthropy visited in a vessel of his own most of the missionary settlements in the south seas
__label__MELVILLE he remained some time at tahiti receiving the hospitalities of the missionaries there and from time to time exhorting the natives
__label__MELVILLE after bewailing their social condition he frankly says of their religious state certainly appearances are unpromising and however unwilling to adopt such a conclusion there is reason to apprehend that christian principle is a great rarity
__label__MELVILLE such then is the testimony of good and unbiassed men who have been upon the spot but how comes it to differ so widely from impressions of others at home
__label__MELVILLE simply thus instead of estimating the result of missionary labours by the number of heathens who have actually been made to understand and practise in some measure at least the precepts of christianity this result has been unwarrantably inferred from the number of those who without any understanding of these things have in any way been induced to abandon idolatry and conform to certain outward observances
__label__MELVILLE by authority of some kind or other exerted upon the natives through their chiefs and prompted by the hope of some worldly benefit to the latter and not by appeals to the reason have conversions in polynesia been in most cases brought about
__label__MELVILLE even in one or two instances so often held up as wonderful examples of divine power where the natives have impulsively burned their idols and rushed to the waters of baptism the very suddenness of the change has but indicated its unsoundness
__label__MELVILLE williams the martyr of erromanga relates an instance where the inhabitants of an island professing christianity voluntarily assembled and solemnly revived all their heathen customs
__label__MELVILLE all the world over facts are more eloquent than words the following will show in what estimation the missionaries themselves hold the present state of christianity and morals among the converted polynesians
__label__MELVILLE on the island of imeeo attached to the tahitian mission is a seminary under the charge of the rev
__label__MELVILLE mr simpson and wife for the education of the children of the missionaries exclusively
__label__MELVILLE sent home in many cases at a very early age to finish their education the pupils here are taught nothing but the rudiments of knowledge nothing more than may be learned in the native schools
__label__MELVILLE notwithstanding this the two races are kept as far as possible from associating the avowed reason being to preserve the young whites from moral contamination
__label__MELVILLE the better to insure this end every effort is made to prevent them from acquiring the native language
__label__MELVILLE they went even further at the sandwich islands where a few years ago a playground for the children of the missionaries was inclosed with a fence many feet high the more effectually to exclude the wicked little hawaiians
__label__MELVILLE and yet strange as it may seem the depravity among the polynesians which renders precautions like these necessary was in a measure unknown before their intercourse with the whites
__label__MELVILLE the excellent captain wilson who took the first missionaries out to tahiti affirms that the people of that island had in many things more refined ideas of decency than ourselves
__label__MELVILLE vancouver also has some noteworthy ideas on this subject respecting the sandwich islanders
__label__MELVILLE that the immorality alluded to is continually increasing is plainly shown in the numerous severe and perpetually violated laws against licentiousness of all kinds in both groups of islands
__label__MELVILLE it is hardly to be expected that the missionaries would send home accounts of this state of things
__label__MELVILLE hence captain beechy in alluding to the polynesian researches of ellis says that the author has impressed his readers with a far more elevated idea of the moral condition of the tahitians and the degree of civilization to which they have attained than they deserve or at least than the facts which came under his observation authorized
__label__MELVILLE he then goes on to say that in his intercourse with the islanders they had no fear of him and consequently acted from the impulse of their natural feeling so that he was the better enabled to obtain a correct knowledge of their real disposition and habits
__label__MELVILLE prom my own familiar intercourse with the natives this last reflection still more forcibly applies to myself
__label__MELVILLE same subject continued
__label__MELVILLE we have glanced at their moral and religious condition let us see how it is with them socially and in other respects
__label__MELVILLE it has been said that the only way to civilize a people is to form in them habits of industry
__label__MELVILLE judged by this principle the tahitians are less civilized now than formerly
__label__MELVILLE true their constitutional indolence is excessive but surely if the spirit of christianity is among them so unchristian a vice ought to be at least partially remedied
__label__MELVILLE but the reverse is the fact
__label__MELVILLE instead of acquiring new occupations old ones have been discontinued
__label__MELVILLE as previously remarked the manufacture of tappa is nearly obsolete in many parts of the island
__label__MELVILLE so too with that of the native tools and domestic utensils very few of which are now fabricated since the superiority of european wares has been made so evident
__label__MELVILLE this however would be all very well were the natives to apply themselves to such occupations as would enable them to supply the few articles they need
__label__MELVILLE but they are far from doing so and the majority being unable to obtain european substitutes for many things before made by themselves the inevitable consequence is seen in the present wretched and destitute mode of life among the common people
__label__MELVILLE to me so recently from a primitive valley of the marquesas the aspect of most of the dwellings of the poorer tahitians and their general habits seemed anything but tidy nor could i avoid a comparison immeasurably to the disadvantage of these partially civilized islanders
__label__MELVILLE in tahiti the people have nothing to do and idleness everywhere is the parent of vice
__label__MELVILLE there is scarcely anything says the good old quaker wheeler so striking or pitiable as their aimless nerveless mode of spending life
__label__MELVILLE attempts have repeatedly been made to rouse them from their sluggishness but in vain
__label__MELVILLE several years ago the cultivation of cotton was introduced and with their usual love of novelty they went to work with great alacrity but the interest excited quickly subsided and now not a pound of the article is raised
__label__MELVILLE about the same time machinery for weaving was sent out from london and a factory was started at afrehitoo in imeeo
__label__MELVILLE the whiz of the wheels and spindles brought in volunteers from all quarters who deemed it a privilege to be admitted to work yet in six months not a boy could be hired and the machinery was knocked down and packed off to sydney
__label__MELVILLE it was the same way with the cultivation of the sugar cane a plant indigenous to the island peculiarly fitted to the soil and climate and of so excellent a quality that bligh took slips of it to the west indies
__label__MELVILLE all the plantations went on famously for a while the natives swarming in the fields like ants and making a prodigious stir
__label__MELVILLE what few plantations now remain are owned and worked by whites who would rather pay a drunken sailor eighteen or twenty spanish dollars a month than hire a sober native for his fish and tarro
__label__MELVILLE it is well worthy remark here that every evidence of civilization among the south sea islands directly pertains to foreigners though the fact of such evidence existing at all is usually urged as a proof of the elevated condition of the natives
__label__MELVILLE thus at honolulu the capital of the sandwich islands there are fine dwelling houses several hotels and barber shops ay even billiard rooms but all these are owned and used be it observed by whites
__label__MELVILLE there are tailors and blacksmiths and carpenters also but not one of them is a native
__label__MELVILLE the fact is that the mechanical and agricultural employment of civilized life require a kind of exertion altogether too steady and sustained to agree with an indolent people like the polynesians
__label__MELVILLE calculated for a state of nature in a climate providentially adapted to it they are unfit for any other
__label__MELVILLE nay as a race they cannot otherwise long exist
__label__MELVILLE the following statement speaks for itself
__label__MELVILLE about the year 1777 captain cook estimated the population of tahiti at about two hundred thousand
__label__MELVILLE by a regular census taken some four or five years ago it was found to be only nine thousand
__label__MELVILLE this amazing decrease not only shows the malignancy of the evils necessary to produce it but from the fact the inference unavoidably follows that all the wars child murders and other depopulating causes alleged to have existed in former times were nothing in comparison to them
__label__MELVILLE these evils of course are solely of foreign origin
__label__MELVILLE to say nothing of the effects of drunkenness the occasional inroads of the small pox and other things which might be mentioned it is sufficient to allude to a virulent disease which now taints the blood of at least two thirds of the common people of the island and in some form or other is transmitted from father to son
__label__MELVILLE their first horror and consternation at the earlier ravages of this scourge were pitiable in the extreme
__label__MELVILLE the very name bestowed upon it is a combination of all that is horrid and unmentionable to a civilized being
__label__MELVILLE distracted with their sufferings they brought forth their sick before the missionaries when they were preaching and cried out lies lies
__label__MELVILLE you tell us of salvation and behold we are dying
__label__MELVILLE we want no other salvation than to live in this world
__label__MELVILLE where are there any saved through your speech
__label__MELVILLE pomaree is dead and we are all dying with your cursed diseases
__label__MELVILLE when will you give over
__label__MELVILLE at present the virulence of the disorder in individual cases has somewhat abated but the poison is only the more widely diffused
__label__MELVILLE how dreadful and appalling breaks forth old wheeler the consideration that the intercourse of distant nations should have entailed upon these poor untutored islanders a curse unprecedented and unheard of in the annals of history
__label__MELVILLE in view of these things who can remain blind to the fact that so far as mere temporal felicity is concerned the tahitians are far worse off now than formerly and although their circumstances upon the whole are bettered by the presence of the missionaries the benefits conferred by the latter become utterly insignificant when confronted with the vast preponderance of evil brought about by other means
__label__MELVILLE their prospects are hopeless
__label__MELVILLE nor can the most devoted efforts now exempt them from furnishing a marked illustration of a principle which history has always exemplified
__label__MELVILLE years ago brought to a stand where all that is corrupt in barbarism and civilization unite to the exclusion of the virtues of either state like other uncivilized beings brought into contact with europeans they must here remain stationary until utterly extinct
__label__MELVILLE the islanders themselves are mournfully watching their doom
__label__MELVILLE several years since pomaree ii
__label__MELVILLE said to tyreman and bennet the deputies of the london missionary society you have come to see me at a very bad time
__label__MELVILLE your ancestors came in the time of men when tahiti was inhabited you are come to behold just the remnant of my people
__label__MELVILLE of like import was the prediction of teearmoar the high priest of paree who lived over a hundred years ago
__label__MELVILLE i have frequently heard it chanted in a low sad tone by aged tahitiana
__label__MELVILLE a harree ta fow a toro ta farraro a now ta tararta
__label__MELVILLE the palm tree shall grow the coral shall spread but man shall cease
__label__MELVILLE something happens to long ghost
__label__MELVILLE we will now return to the narrative
__label__MELVILLE the day before the julia sailed dr johnson paid his last call
__label__MELVILLE he was not quite so bland as usual
__label__MELVILLE all he wanted was the mens names to a paper certifying to their having received from him sundry medicaments therein mentioned
__label__MELVILLE this voucher endorsed by captain guy secured his pay
__label__MELVILLE but he would not have obtained for it the sailors signs manual had either the doctor or myself been present at the time
__label__MELVILLE now my long friend wasted no love upon johnson but for reasons of his own hated him heartily all the same thing in one sense for either passion argues an object deserving thereof
__label__MELVILLE and so to be hated cordially is only a left handed compliment which shows how foolish it is to be bitter against anyone
__label__MELVILLE for my own part i merely felt a cool purely incidental and passive contempt for johnson as a selfish mercenary apothecary and hence i often remonstrated with long ghost when he flew out against him and heaped upon him all manner of scurrilous epithets
__label__MELVILLE in his professional brothers presence however he never acted thus maintaining an amiable exterior to help along the jokes which were played
__label__MELVILLE i am now going to tell another story in which my long friend figures with the physician i do not wish to bring one or the other of them too often upon the stage but as the thing actually happened i must relate it
__label__MELVILLE a few days after johnson presented his bill as above mentioned the doctor expressed to me his regret that although he johnson had apparently been played off for our entertainment yet nevertheless he had made money out of the transaction
__label__MELVILLE and i wonder added the doctor if that now he cannot expect to receive any further pay he could be induced to call again
__label__MELVILLE by a curious coincidence not five minutes after making this observation doctor long ghost himself fell down in an unaccountable fit and without asking anybodys leave captain bob who was by at once dispatched a boy hot foot for johnson
__label__MELVILLE meanwhile we carried him into the calabooza and the natives who assembled in numbers suggested various modes of treatment
__label__MELVILLE one rather energetic practitioner was for holding the patient by the shoulders while somebody tugged at his feet
__label__MELVILLE this resuscitatory operation was called the potata but thinking our long comrade sufficiently lengthy without additional stretching we declined potataing him
__label__MELVILLE presently the physician was spied coming along the broom road at a great rate and so absorbed in the business of locomotion that he heeded not the imprudence of being in a hurry in a tropical climate
__label__MELVILLE he was in a profuse perspiration which must have been owing to the warmth of his feelings notwithstanding we had supposed him a man of no heart
__label__MELVILLE but his benevolent haste upon this occasion was subsequently accounted for it merely arose from professional curiosity to behold a case most unusual in his polynesian practice
__label__MELVILLE now under certain circumstances sailors generally so frolicsome are exceedingly particular in having everything conducted with the strictest propriety
__label__MELVILLE accordingly they deputed me as his intimate friend to sit at long ghosts head so as to be ready to officiate as spokesman and answer all questions propounded the rest to keep silent
__label__MELVILLE whats the matter
__label__MELVILLE exclaimed johnson out of breath and bursting into the calabooza how did it happen speak quick
__label__MELVILLE and he looked at long ghost
__label__MELVILLE i told him how the fit came on
