__label__MELVILLE the area of the dock itself exclusive of the inclosed quays surrounding it may be estimated at say ten acres
__label__MELVILLE access to the interior from the streets is had through several gateways so that upon their being closed the whole dock is shut up like a house
__label__MELVILLE from the river the entrance is through a water gate and ingress to ships is only to be had when the level of the dock coincides with that of the river that is about the time of high tide as the level of the dock is always at that mark
__label__MELVILLE so that when it is low tide in the river the keels of the ships inclosed by the quays are elevated more than twenty feet above those of the vessels in the stream
__label__MELVILLE this of course produces a striking effect to a stranger to see hundreds of immense ships floating high aloft in the heart of a mass of masonry
__label__MELVILLE princes dock is generally so filled with shipping that the entrance of a new comer is apt to occasion a universal stir among all the older occupants
__label__MELVILLE the dock masters whose authority is declared by tin signs worn conspicuously over their hats mount the poops and forecastles of the various vessels and hail the surrounding strangers in all directions highlander ahoy
__label__MELVILLE cast off your bowline and sheer alongside the neptune
__label__MELVILLE neptune ahoy
__label__MELVILLE get out a stern line and sheer alongside the trident
__label__MELVILLE trident ahoy
__label__MELVILLE get out a bowline and drop astern of the undaunted
__label__MELVILLE and so it runs round like a shock of electricity touch one and you touch all
__label__MELVILLE this kind of work irritates and exasperates the sailors to the last degree but it is only one of the unavoidable inconveniences of inclosed docks which are outweighed by innumerable advantages
__label__MELVILLE just without the water gate is a basin always connecting with the open river through a narrow entrance between pierheads
__label__MELVILLE this basin forms a sort of ante chamber to the dock itself where vessels lie waiting their turn to enter
__label__MELVILLE during a storm the necessity of this basin is obvious for it would be impossible to dock a ship under full headway from a voyage across the ocean
__label__MELVILLE from the turbulent waves she first glides into the ante chamber between the pier heads and from thence into the docks
__label__MELVILLE concerning the cost of the docks i can only state that the kings dock comprehending but a comparatively small area was completed at an expense of some 20000
__label__MELVILLE our old ship keeper a liverpool man by birth who had long followed the seas related a curious story concerning this dock
__label__MELVILLE one of the ships which carried over troops from england to ireland in king williams war in 1688 entered the kings dock on the first day of its being opened in 1788 after an interval of just one century
__label__MELVILLE she was a dark little brig called the port a ferry
__label__MELVILLE and probably as her timbers must have been frequently renewed in the course of a hundred years the name alone could have been all that was left of her at the time
__label__MELVILLE a paved area very wide is included within the walls and along the edge of the quays are ranges of iron sheds intended as a temporary shelter for the goods unladed from the shipping
__label__MELVILLE nothing can exceed the bustle and activity displayed along these quays during the day bales crates boxes and cases are being tumbled about by thousands of laborers trucks are coming and going dock masters are shouting sailors of all nations are singing out at their ropes and all this commotion is greatly increased by the resoundings from the lofty walls that hem in the din
__label__MELVILLE surrounded by its broad belt of masonry each liverpool dock is a walled town full of life and commotion or rather it is a small archipelago an epitome of the world where all the nations of christendom and even those of heathendom are represented
__label__MELVILLE for in itself each ship is an island a floating colony of the tribe to which it belongs
__label__MELVILLE here are brought together the remotest limits of the earth and in the collective spars and timbers of these ships all the forests of the globe are represented as in a grand parliament of masts
__label__MELVILLE canada and new zealand send their pines america her live oak india her teak norway her spruce and the right honorable mahogany member for honduras and campeachy is seen at his post by the wheel
__label__MELVILLE here under the beneficent sway of the genius of commerce all climes and countries embrace and yard arm touches yard arm in brotherly love
__label__MELVILLE a liverpool dock is a grand caravansary inn and hotel on the spacious and liberal plan of the astor house
__label__MELVILLE here ships are lodged at a moderate charge and payment is not demanded till the time of departure
__label__MELVILLE here they are comfortably housed and provided for sheltered from all weathers and secured from all calamities
__label__MELVILLE for i can hardly credit a story i have heard that sometimes in heavy gales ships lying in the very middle of the docks have lost their top gallant masts
__label__MELVILLE whatever the toils and hardships encountered on the voyage whether they come from iceland or the coast of new guinea here their sufferings are ended and they take their ease in their watery inn
__label__MELVILLE i know not how many hours i spent in gazing at the shipping in princes dock and speculating concerning their past voyages and future prospects in life
__label__MELVILLE some had just arrived from the most distant ports worn battered and disabled others were all a taunt o spruce gay and brilliant in readiness for sea
__label__MELVILLE every day the highlander had some new neighbor
__label__MELVILLE a black brig from glasgow with its crew of sober scotch caps and its staid thrifty looking skipper would be replaced by a jovial french hermaphrodite its forecastle echoing with songs and its quarter deck elastic from much dancing
__label__MELVILLE on the other side perhaps a magnificent new york liner huge as a seventy four and suggesting the idea of a mivarts or delmonicos afloat would give way to a sidney emigrant ship receiving on board its live freight of shepherds from the grampians ere long to be tending their flocks on the hills and downs of new holland
__label__MELVILLE i was particularly pleased and tickled with a multitude of little salt droghers rigged like sloops and not much bigger than a pilot boat but with broad bows painted black and carrying red sails which looked as if they had been pickled and stained in a tan yard
__label__MELVILLE these little fellows were continually coming in with their cargoes for ships bound to america and lying five or six together alongside of those lofty yankee hulls resembled a parcel of red ants about the carcass of a black buffalo
__label__MELVILLE when loaded these comical little craft are about level with the water and frequently when blowing fresh in the river i have seen them flying through the foam with nothing visible but the mast and sail and a man at the tiller their entire cargo being snugly secured under hatches
__label__MELVILLE it was diverting to observe the self importance of the skipper of any of these diminutive vessels
__label__MELVILLE he would give himself all the airs of an admiral on a three deckers poop and no doubt thought quite as much of himself
__label__MELVILLE and why not
__label__MELVILLE what could caesar want more
__label__MELVILLE though his craft was none of the largest it was subject to him and though his crew might only consist of himself yet if he governed it well he achieved a triumph which the moralists of all ages have set above the victories of alexander
__label__MELVILLE these craft have each a little cabin the prettiest charmingest most delightful little dog hole in the world not much bigger than an old fashioned alcove for a bed
__label__MELVILLE it is lighted by little round glasses placed in the deck so that to the insider the ceiling is like a small firmament twinkling with astral radiations
__label__MELVILLE for tall men nevertheless the place is but ill adapted a sitting or recumbent position being indispensable to an occupancy of the premises
__label__MELVILLE yet small low and narrow as the cabin is somehow it affords accommodations to the skipper and his family
__label__MELVILLE often i used to watch the tidy good wife seated at the open little scuttle like a woman at a cottage door engaged in knitting socks for her husband or perhaps cutting his hair as he kneeled before her
__label__MELVILLE and once while marveling how a couple like this found room to turn in below i was amazed by a noisy irruption of cherry cheeked young tars from the scuttle whence they came rolling forth like so many curly spaniels from a kennel
__label__MELVILLE upon one occasion i had the curiosity to go on board a salt drogher and fall into conversation with its skipper a bachelor who kept house all alone
__label__MELVILLE i found him a very sociable comfortable old fellow who had an eye to having things cozy around him
__label__MELVILLE it was in the evening and he invited me down into his sanctum to supper and there we sat together like a couple in a box at an oyster cellar
__label__MELVILLE he he he chuckled kneeling down before a fat moist little cask of beer and holding a cocked hat pitcher to the faucet you see jack i keep every thing down here and nice times i have by myself
__label__MELVILLE just before going to bed it aint bad to take a nightcap you know eh
__label__MELVILLE jack here now smack your lips over that my boy have a pipe but stop lets to supper first
__label__MELVILLE so he went to a little locker a fixture against the side and groping in it awhile and addressing it with what cheer here what cheer
__label__MELVILLE at last produced a loaf a small cheese a bit of ham and a jar of butter
__label__MELVILLE and then placing a board on his lap spread the table the pitcher of beer in the center
__label__MELVILLE why thats but a two legged table said i lets make it four
__label__MELVILLE so we divided the burthen and supped merrily together on our knees
__label__MELVILLE he was an old ruby of a fellow his cheeks toasted brown and it did my soul good to see the froth of the beer bubbling at his mouth and sparkling on his nut brown beard
__label__MELVILLE he looked so like a great mug of ale that i almost felt like taking him by the neck and pouring him out
__label__MELVILLE now jack said he when supper was over now jack my boy do you smoke well then load away
__label__MELVILLE and he handed me a seal skin pouch of tobacco and a pipe
__label__MELVILLE we sat smoking together in this little sea cabinet of his till it began to look much like a state room in tophet and notwithstanding my hosts rubicund nose i could hardly see him for the fog
__label__MELVILLE he he my boy then said he i dont never have any bugs here i tell ye i smokes em all out every night before going to bed
__label__MELVILLE and where may you sleep
__label__MELVILLE said i looking round and seeing no sign of a bed
__label__MELVILLE sleep
__label__MELVILLE says he why i sleep in my jacket thats the best counterpane and i use my head for a pillow
__label__MELVILLE he he funny aint it
__label__MELVILLE very funny says i
__label__MELVILLE have some more ale
__label__MELVILLE says he plenty more
__label__MELVILLE no more thank you says i i guess ill go for what with the tobacco smoke and the ale i began to feel like breathing fresh air
__label__MELVILLE besides my conscience smote me for thus freely indulging in the pleasures of the table
__label__MELVILLE now dont go said he dont go my boy dont go out into the damp take an old christians advice laying his hand on my shoulder it wont do
__label__MELVILLE you see by going out now youll shake off the ale and get broad awake again but if you stay here youll soon be dropping off for a nice little nap
__label__MELVILLE but notwithstanding these inducements i shook my hosts hand and departed
__label__MELVILLE there was hardly any thing i witnessed in the docks that interested me more than the german emigrants who come on board the large new york ships several days before their sailing to make every thing comfortable ere starting
__label__MELVILLE old men tottering with age and little infants in arms laughing girls in bright buttoned bodices and astute middle aged men with pictured pipes in their mouths would be seen mingling together in crowds of five six and seven or eight hundred in one ship
__label__MELVILLE every evening these countrymen of luther and melancthon gathered on the forecastle to sing and pray
__label__MELVILLE and it was exalting to listen to their fine ringing anthems reverberating among the crowded shipping and rebounding from the lofty walls of the docks
__label__MELVILLE shut your eyes and you would think you were in a cathedral
__label__MELVILLE they keep up this custom at sea and every night in the dog watch sing the songs of zion to the roll of the great ocean organ a pious custom of a devout race who thus send over their hallelujahs before them as they hie to the land of the stranger
__label__MELVILLE and among these sober germans my country counts the most orderly and valuable of her foreign population
__label__MELVILLE it is they who have swelled the census of her northwestern states and transferring their ploughs from the hills of transylvania to the prairies of wisconsin and sowing the wheat of the rhine on the banks of the ohio raise the grain that a hundred fold increased may return to their kinsmen in europe
__label__MELVILLE there is something in the contemplation of the mode in which america has been settled that in a noble breast should forever extinguish the prejudices of national dislikes
__label__MELVILLE settled by the people of all nations all nations may claim her for their own
__label__MELVILLE you can not spill a drop of american blood without spilling the blood of the whole world
__label__MELVILLE be he englishman frenchman german dane or scot the european who scoffs at an american calls his own brother raca and stands in danger of the judgment
__label__MELVILLE we are not a narrow tribe of men with a bigoted hebrew nationality whose blood has been debased in the attempt to ennoble it by maintaining an exclusive succession among ourselves
__label__MELVILLE no our blood is as the flood of the amazon made up of a thousand noble currents all pouring into one
__label__MELVILLE we are not a nation so much as a world for unless we may claim all the world for our sire like melchisedec we are without father or mother
__label__MELVILLE for who was our father and our mother
__label__MELVILLE or can we point to any romulus and remus for our founders
__label__MELVILLE our ancestry is lost in the universal paternity and caesar and alfred st paul and luther and homer and shakespeare are as much ours as washington who is as much the worlds as our own
__label__MELVILLE we are the heirs of all time and with all nations we divide our inheritance
__label__MELVILLE on this western hemisphere all tribes and people are forming into one federated whole and there is a future which shall see the estranged children of adam restored as to the old hearthstone in eden
__label__MELVILLE the other world beyond this which was longed for by the devout before columbus time was found in the new and the deep sea lead that first struck these soundings brought up the soil of earths paradise
__label__MELVILLE not a paradise then or now but to be made so at gods good pleasure and in the fullness and mellowness of time
__label__MELVILLE the seed is sown and the harvest must come and our childrens children on the worlds jubilee morning shall all go with their sickles to the reaping
__label__MELVILLE then shall the curse of babel be revoked a new pentecost come and the language they shall speak shall be the language of britain
__label__MELVILLE frenchmen and danes and scots and the dwellers on the shores of the mediterranean and in the regions round about italians and indians and moors there shall appear unto them cloven tongues as of fire
__label__MELVILLE among the various ships lying in princes dock none interested me more than the irrawaddy of bombay a country ship which is the name bestowed by europeans upon the large native vessels of india
__label__MELVILLE forty years ago these merchantmen were nearly the largest in the world and they still exceed the generality
__label__MELVILLE they are built of the celebrated teak wood the oak of the east or in eastern phrase the king of the oaks
__label__MELVILLE the irrawaddy had just arrived from hindostan with a cargo of cotton
__label__MELVILLE she was manned by forty or fifty lascars the native seamen of india who seemed to be immediately governed by a countryman of theirs of a higher caste
__label__MELVILLE while his inferiors went about in strips of white linen this dignitary was arrayed in a red army coat brilliant with gold lace a cocked hat and drawn sword
__label__MELVILLE but the general effect was quite spoiled by his bare feet
__label__MELVILLE in discharging the cargo his business seemed to consist in flagellating the crew with the flat of his saber an exercise in which long practice had made him exceedingly expert
__label__MELVILLE the poor fellows jumped away with the tackle rope elastic as cats
__label__MELVILLE one sunday i went aboard of the irrawaddy when this oriental usher accosted me at the gangway with his sword at my throat
__label__MELVILLE i gently pushed it aside making a sign expressive of the pacific character of my motives in paying a visit to the ship
__label__MELVILLE whereupon he very considerately let me pass
__label__MELVILLE i thought i was in pegu so strangely woody was the smell of the dark colored timbers whose odor was heightened by the rigging of kayar or cocoa nut fiber
__label__MELVILLE the lascars were on the forecastle deck
__label__MELVILLE among them were malays mahrattas burmese siamese and cingalese
__label__MELVILLE they were seated round kids full of rice from which according to their invariable custom they helped themselves with one hand the other being reserved for quite another purpose
__label__MELVILLE they were chattering like magpies in hindostanee but i found that several of them could also speak very good english
__label__MELVILLE they were a small limbed wiry tawny set and i was informed made excellent seamen though ill adapted to stand the hardships of northern voyaging
__label__MELVILLE they told me that seven of their number had died on the passage from bombay two or three after crossing the tropic of cancer and the rest met their fate in the channel where the ship had been tost about in violent seas attended with cold rains peculiar to that vicinity
__label__MELVILLE two more had been lost overboard from the flying jib boom
__label__MELVILLE i was condoling with a young english cabin boy on board upon the loss of these poor fellows when he said it was their own fault they would never wear monkey jackets but clung to their thin india robes even in the bitterest weather
__label__MELVILLE he talked about them much as a farmer would about the loss of so many sheep by the murrain
__label__MELVILLE the captain of the vessel was an englishman as were also the three mates master and boatswain
__label__MELVILLE these officers lived astern in the cabin where every sunday they read the church of englands prayers while the heathen at the other end of the ship were left to their false gods and idols
__label__MELVILLE and thus with christianity on the quarter deck and paganism on the forecastle the irrawaddy ploughed the sea
__label__MELVILLE as if to symbolize this state of things the fancy piece astern comprised among numerous other carved decorations a cross and a miter while forward on the bows was a sort of devil for a figure head a dragon shaped creature with a fiery red mouth and a switchy looking tail
__label__MELVILLE after her cargo was discharged which was done to the sound of flutes and soft recorders something as work is done in the navy to the music of the boatswains pipe the lascars were set to stripping the ship that is to sending down all her spars and ropes
__label__MELVILLE at this time she lay alongside of us and the babel on board almost drowned our own voices
__label__MELVILLE in nothing but their girdles the lascars hopped about aloft chattering like so many monkeys but nevertheless showing much dexterity and seamanship in their manner of doing their work
__label__MELVILLE every sunday crowds of well dressed people came down to the dock to see this singular ship many of them perched themselves in the shrouds of the neighboring craft much to the wrath of captain riga who left strict orders with our old ship keeper to drive all strangers out of the highlanders rigging
__label__MELVILLE it was amusing at these times to watch the old women with umbrellas who stood on the quay staring at the lascars even when they desired to be private
__label__MELVILLE these inquisitive old ladies seemed to regard the strange sailors as a species of wild animal whom they might gaze at with as much impunity as at leopards in the zoological gardens
__label__MELVILLE one night i was returning to the ship when just as i was passing through the dock gate i noticed a white figure squatting against the wall outside
__label__MELVILLE it proved to be one of the lascars who was smoking as the regulations of the docks prohibit his indulging this luxury on board his vessel
__label__MELVILLE struck with the curious fashion of his pipe and the odor from it i inquired what he was smoking he replied joggerry which is a species of weed used in place of tobacco
__label__MELVILLE finding that he spoke good english and was quite communicative like most smokers i sat down by dattabdool mans as he called himself and we fell into conversation
__label__MELVILLE so instructive was his discourse that when we parted i had considerably added to my stock of knowledge
__label__MELVILLE indeed it is a godsend to fall in with a fellow like this
__label__MELVILLE he knows things you never dreamed of his experiences are like a man from the moon wholly strange a new revelation
__label__MELVILLE if you want to learn romance or gain an insight into things quaint curious and marvelous drop your books of travel and take a stroll along the docks of a great commercial port
__label__MELVILLE ten to one you will encounter crusoe himself among the crowds of mariners from all parts of the globe
__label__MELVILLE but this is no place for making mention of all the subjects upon which i and my lascar friend mostly discoursed i will only try to give his account of the teakwood and kayar rope concerning which things i was curious and sought information
__label__MELVILLE the sagoon as he called the tree which produces the teak grows in its greatest excellence among the mountains of malabar whence large quantities are sent to bombay for shipbuilding
__label__MELVILLE he also spoke of another kind of wood the sissor which supplies most of the shin logs or knees and crooked timbers in the country ships
__label__MELVILLE the sagoon grows to an immense size sometimes there is fifty feet of trunk three feet through before a single bough is put forth
__label__MELVILLE its leaves are very large and to convey some idea of them my lascar likened them to elephants ears
__label__MELVILLE he said a purple dye was extracted from them for the purpose of staining cottons and silks
__label__MELVILLE the wood is specifically heavier than water it is easily worked and extremely strong and durable
__label__MELVILLE but its chief merit lies in resisting the action of the salt water and the attacks of insects which resistance is caused by its containing a resinous oil called poonja
__label__MELVILLE to my surprise he informed me that the irrawaddy was wholly built by the native shipwrights of india who he modestly asserted surpassed the european artisans
__label__MELVILLE the rigging also was of native manufacture
__label__MELVILLE as the kayar of which it is composed is now getting into use both in england and america as well for ropes and rigging as for mats and rugs my lascar friends account of it joined to my own observations may not be uninteresting
__label__MELVILLE in india it is prepared very much in the same way as in polynesia
__label__MELVILLE the cocoa nut is gathered while the husk is still green and but partially ripe and this husk is removed by striking the nut forcibly with both hands upon a sharp pointed stake planted uprightly in the ground
__label__MELVILLE in this way a boy will strip nearly fifteen hundred in a day
__label__MELVILLE but the kayar is not made from the husk as might be supposed but from the rind of the nut which after being long soaked in water is beaten with mallets and rubbed together into fibers
__label__MELVILLE after this being dried in the sun you may spin it just like hemp or any similar substance
__label__MELVILLE the fiber thus produced makes very strong and durable ropes extremely well adapted from their lightness and durability for the running rigging of a ship while the same causes united with its great strength and buoyancy render it very suitable for large cables and hawsers
__label__MELVILLE but the elasticity of the kayar ill fits it for the shrouds and standing rigging of a ship which require to be comparatively firm
__label__MELVILLE hence as the irrawaddys shrouds were all of this substance the lascar told me they were continually setting up or slacking off her standing rigging according as the weather was cold or warm
__label__MELVILLE and the loss of a foretopmast between the tropics in a squall he attributed to this circumstance
__label__MELVILLE after a stay of about two weeks the irrawaddy had her heavy indian spars replaced with canadian pine and her kayar shrouds with hempen ones
__label__MELVILLE she then mustered her pagans and hoisted sail for london
__label__MELVILLE another very curious craft often seen in the liverpool docks is the dutch galliot an old fashioned looking gentleman with hollow waist high prow and stern and which seen lying among crowds of tight yankee traders and pert french brigantines always reminded me of a cocked hat among modish beavers
__label__MELVILLE the construction of the galliot has not altered for centuries and the northern european nations danes and dutch still sail the salt seas in this flat bottomed salt cellar of a ship although in addition to these they have vessels of a more modern kind
__label__MELVILLE they seldom paint the galliot but scrape and varnish all its planks and spars so that all over it resembles the bright side or polished streak usually banding round an american ship
__label__MELVILLE some of them are kept scrupulously neat and clean and remind one of a well scrubbed wooden platter or an old oak table upon which much wax and elbow vigor has been expended
__label__MELVILLE before the wind they sail well but on a bowline owing to their broad hulls and flat bottoms they make leeway at a sad rate
__label__MELVILLE every day some strange vessel entered princes dock and hardly would i gaze my fill at some outlandish craft from surat or the levant ere a still more outlandish one would absorb my attention
__label__MELVILLE among others i remember was a little brig from the coast of guinea
__label__MELVILLE in appearance she was the ideal of a slaver low black clipper built about the bows and her decks in a state of most piratical disorder
__label__MELVILLE she carried a long rusty gun on a swivel amid ships and that gun was a curiosity in itself
__label__MELVILLE it must have been some old veteran condemned by the government and sold for any thing it would fetch
__label__MELVILLE it was an antique covered with half effaced inscriptions crowns anchors eagles and it had two handles near the trunnions like those of a tureen
__label__MELVILLE the knob on the breach was fashioned into a dolphins head and by a comical conceit the touch hole formed the orifice of a human ear and a stout tympanum it must have had to have withstood the concussions it had heard
__label__MELVILLE the brig heavily loaded lay between two large ships in ballast so that its deck was at least twenty feet below those of its neighbors
__label__MELVILLE thus shut in its hatchways looked like the entrance to deep vaults or mines especially as her men were wheeling out of her hold some kind of ore which might have been gold ore so scrupulous were they in evening the bushel measures in which they transferred it to the quay and so particular was the captain a dark skinned whiskerando in a maltese cap and tassel in standing over the sailors with his pencil and memorandum book in hand
__label__MELVILLE the crew were a buccaneering looking set with hairy chests purple shirts and arms wildly tattooed
__label__MELVILLE the mate had a wooden leg and hobbled about with a crooked cane like a spiral staircase
__label__MELVILLE there was a deal of swearing on board of this craft which was rendered the more reprehensible when she came to moor alongside the floating chapel
__label__MELVILLE this was the hull of an old sloop of war which had been converted into a mariners church
__label__MELVILLE a house had been built upon it and a steeple took the place of a mast
__label__MELVILLE there was a little balcony near the base of the steeple some twenty feet from the water where on week days i used to see an old pensioner of a tar sitting on a camp stool reading his bible
__label__MELVILLE on sundays he hoisted the bethel flag and like the muezzin or cryer of prayers on the top of a turkish mosque would call the strolling sailors to their devotions not officially but on his own account conjuring them not to make fools of themselves but muster round the pulpit as they did about the capstan on a man of war
__label__MELVILLE this old worthy was the sexton
__label__MELVILLE i attended the chapel several times and found there a very orderly but small congregation
__label__MELVILLE the first time i went the chaplain was discoursing on future punishments and making allusions to the tartarean lake which coupled with the pitchy smell of the old hull summoned up the most forcible image of the thing which i ever experienced
__label__MELVILLE the floating chapels which are to be found in some of the docks form one of the means which have been tried to induce the seamen visiting liverpool to turn their thoughts toward serious things
__label__MELVILLE but as very few of them ever think of entering these chapels though they might pass them twenty times in the day some of the clergy of a sunday address them in the open air from the corners of the quays or wherever they can procure an audience
__label__MELVILLE whenever in my sunday strolls i caught sight of one of these congregations i always made a point of joining it and would find myself surrounded by a motley crowd of seamen from all quarters of the globe and women and lumpers and dock laborers of all sorts
__label__MELVILLE frequently the clergyman would be standing upon an old cask arrayed in full canonicals as a divine of the church of england
__label__MELVILLE never have i heard religious discourses better adapted to an audience of men who like sailors are chiefly if not only to be moved by the plainest of precepts and demonstrations of the misery of sin as conclusive and undeniable as those of euclid
__label__MELVILLE no mere rhetoric avails with such men fine periods are vanity
__label__MELVILLE you can not touch them with tropes
__label__MELVILLE they need to be pressed home by plain facts
__label__MELVILLE and such was generally the mode in which they were addressed by the clergy in question who taking familiar themes for their discourses which were leveled right at the wants of their auditors always succeeded in fastening their attention
__label__MELVILLE in particular the two great vices to which sailors are most addicted and which they practice to the ruin of both body and soul these things were the most enlarged upon

__label__MELVILLE the old women described as picking dirty fragments of cotton in the empty lot belong to the same class of beings who at all hours of the day are to be seen within the dock walls raking over and over the heaps of rubbish carried ashore from the holds of the shipping

__label__MELVILLE these are the haunts in which cursing gambling pickpocketing and common iniquities are virtues too lofty for the infected gorgons and hydras to practice
__label__MELVILLE propriety forbids that i should enter into details but kidnappers burkers and resurrectionists are almost saints and angels to them
__label__MELVILLE they seem leagued together a company of miscreant misanthropes bent upon doing all the malice to mankind in their power
__label__MELVILLE with sulphur and brimstone they ought to be burned out of their arches like vermin
__label__MELVILLE as i wish to group together what fell under my observation concerning the liverpool docks and the scenes roundabout i will try to throw into this chapter various minor things that i recall
__label__MELVILLE the advertisements of pauperism chalked upon the flagging round the dock walls are singularly accompanied by a multitude of quite different announcements placarded upon the walls themselves
__label__MELVILLE they are principally notices of the approaching departure of superior fast sailing coppered and copper fastened ships for the united states canada new south wales and other places
__label__MELVILLE interspersed with these are the advertisements of jewish clothesmen informing the judicious seamen where he can procure of the best and the cheapest together with ambiguous medical announcements of the tribe of quacks and empirics who prey upon all seafaring men
__label__MELVILLE not content with thus publicly giving notice of their whereabouts these indefatigable sangrados and pretended samaritans hire a parcel of shabby workhouse looking knaves whose business consists in haunting the dock walls about meal times and silently thrusting mysterious little billets duodecimo editions of the larger advertisements into the astonished hands of the tars
__label__MELVILLE they do this with such a mysterious hang dog wink such a sidelong air such a villainous assumption of your necessities that at first you are almost tempted to knock them down for their pains
__label__MELVILLE conspicuous among the notices on the walls are huge italic inducements to all seamen disgusted with the merchant service to accept a round bounty and embark in her majestys navy
__label__MELVILLE in the british armed marine in time of peace they do not ship men for the general service as in the american navy but for particular ships going upon particular cruises
__label__MELVILLE thus the frigate thetis may be announced as about to sail under the command of that fine old sailor and noble father to his crew lord george flagstaff
__label__MELVILLE similar announcements may be seen upon the walls concerning enlistments in the army
__label__MELVILLE and never did auctioneer dilate with more rapture upon the charms of some country seat put up for sale than the authors of these placards do upon the beauty and salubrity of the distant climes for which the regiments wanting recruits are about to sail
__label__MELVILLE bright lawns vine clad hills endless meadows of verdure here make up the landscape and adventurous young gentlemen fond of travel are informed that here is a chance for them to see the world at their leisure and be paid for enjoying themselves into the bargain
__label__MELVILLE the regiments for india are promised plantations among valleys of palms while to those destined for new holland a novel sphere of life and activity is opened and the companies bound to canada and nova scotia are lured by tales of summer suns that ripen grapes in december
__label__MELVILLE no word of war is breathed hushed is the clang of arms in these announcements and the sanguine recruit is almost tempted to expect that pruning hooks instead of swords will be the weapons he will wield
__label__MELVILLE alas
__label__MELVILLE is not this the cruel stratagem of bruce at bannockburn who decoyed to his war pits by covering them over with green boughs
__label__MELVILLE for instead of a farm at the blue base of the himalayas the indian recruit encounters the keen saber of the sikh and instead of basking in sunny bowers the canadian soldier stands a shivering sentry upon the bleak ramparts of quebec a lofty mark for the bitter blasts from baffins bay and labrador
__label__MELVILLE there as his eye sweeps down the st lawrence whose every billow is bound for the main that laves the shore of old england as he thinks of his long term of enlistment which sells him to the army as doctor faust sold himself to the devil how the poor fellow must groan in his grief and call to mind the church yard stile and his mary
__label__MELVILLE these army announcements are well fitted to draw recruits in liverpool
__label__MELVILLE among the vast number of emigrants who daily arrive from all parts of britain to embark for the united states or the colonies there are many young men who upon arriving at liverpool find themselves next to penniless or at least with only enough money to carry them over the sea without providing for future contingencies
__label__MELVILLE how easily and naturally then may such youths be induced to enter upon the military life which promises them a free passage to the most distant and flourishing colonies and certain pay for doing nothing besides holding out hopes of vineyards and farms to be verified in the fullness of time
__label__MELVILLE for in a moneyless youth the decision to leave home at all and embark upon a long voyage to reside in a remote clime is a piece of adventurousness only one removed from the spirit that prompts the army recruit to enlist
__label__MELVILLE i never passed these advertisements surrounded by crowds of gaping emigrants without thinking of rattraps
__label__MELVILLE besides the mysterious agents of the quacks who privily thrust their little notes into your hands folded up like a powder there are another set of rascals prowling about the docks chiefly at dusk who make strange motions to you and beckon you to one side as if they had some state secret to disclose intimately connected with the weal of the commonwealth
__label__MELVILLE they nudge you with an elbow full of indefinite hints and intimations they glitter upon you an eye like a jews or a pawnbrokers they dog you like italian assassins
__label__MELVILLE but if the blue coat of a policeman chances to approach how quickly they strive to look completely indifferent as to the surrounding universe how they saunter off as if lazily wending their way to an affectionate wife and family
__label__MELVILLE the first time one of these mysterious personages accosted me i fancied him crazy and hurried forward to avoid him
__label__MELVILLE but arm in arm with my shadow he followed after till amazed at his conduct i turned round and paused
__label__MELVILLE he was a little shabby old man with a forlorn looking coat and hat and his hand was fumbling in his vest pocket as if to take out a card with his address
__label__MELVILLE seeing me stand still he made a sign toward a dark angle of the wall near which we were when taking him for a cunning foot pad i again wheeled about and swiftly passed on
__label__MELVILLE but though i did not look round i felt him following me still so once more i stopped
__label__MELVILLE the fellow now assumed so mystic and admonitory an air that i began to fancy he came to me on some warning errand that perhaps a plot had been laid to blow up the liverpool docks and he was some monteagle bent upon accomplishing my flight
__label__MELVILLE i was determined to see what he was
__label__MELVILLE with all my eyes about me i followed him into the arch of a warehouse when he gazed round furtively and silently showing me a ring whispered you may have it for a shilling its pure gold i found it in the gutter hush
__label__MELVILLE dont speak
__label__MELVILLE give me the money and its yours
__label__MELVILLE my friend said i i dont trade in these articles i dont want your ring
__label__MELVILLE dont you
__label__MELVILLE then take that he whispered in an intense hushed passion and i fell flat from a blow on the chest while this infamous jeweler made away with himself out of sight
__label__MELVILLE this business transaction was conducted with a counting house promptitude that astonished me
__label__MELVILLE after that i shunned these scoundrels like the leprosy and the next time i was pertinaciously followed i stopped and in a loud voice pointed out the man to the passers by upon which he absconded rapidly turning up into sight a pair of obliquely worn and battered boot heels
__label__MELVILLE i could not help thinking that these sort of fellows so given to running away upon emergencies must furnish a good deal of work to the shoemakers as they might also to the growers of hemp and gallows joiners
__label__MELVILLE belonging to a somewhat similar fraternity with these irritable merchants of brass jewelry just mentioned are the peddlers of sheffield razors mostly boys who are hourly driven out of the dock gates by the police nevertheless they contrive to saunter back and board the vessels going among the sailors and privately exhibiting their wares
__label__MELVILLE incited by the extreme cheapness of one of the razors and the gilding on the case containing it a shipmate of mine purchased it on the spot for a commercial equivalent of the price in tobacco
__label__MELVILLE on the following sunday he used that razor and the result was a pair of tormented and tomahawked cheeks that almost required a surgeon to dress them
__label__MELVILLE in old times by the way it was not a bad thought that suggested the propriety of a barbers practicing surgery in connection with the chin harrowing vocation
__label__MELVILLE another class of knaves who practice upon the sailors in liverpool are the pawnbrokers inhabiting little rookeries among the narrow lanes adjoining the dock
__label__MELVILLE i was astonished at the multitude of gilded balls in these streets emblematic of their calling
__label__MELVILLE they were generally next neighbors to the gilded grapes over the spirit vaults and no doubt mutually to facilitate business operations some of these establishments have connecting doors inside so as to play their customers into each others hands
__label__MELVILLE i often saw sailors in a state of intoxication rushing from a spirit vault into a pawnbrokers stripping off their boots hats jackets and neckerchiefs and sometimes even their pantaloons on the spot and offering to pawn them for a song
__label__MELVILLE of course such applications were never refused
__label__MELVILLE but though on shore at liverpool poor jack finds more sharks than at sea he himself is by no means exempt from practices that do not savor of a rigid morality at least according to law
__label__MELVILLE in tobacco smuggling he is an adept and when cool and collected often manages to evade the customs completely and land goodly packages of the weed which owing to the immense duties upon it in england commands a very high price
__label__MELVILLE as soon as we came to anchor in the river before reaching the dock three custom house underlings boarded us and coming down into the forecastle ordered the men to produce all the tobacco they had
__label__MELVILLE accordingly several pounds were brought forth
__label__MELVILLE is that all
__label__MELVILLE asked the officers
__label__MELVILLE all said the men
__label__MELVILLE we will see returned the others
__label__MELVILLE and without more ado they emptied the chests right and left tossed over the bunks and made a thorough search of the premises but discovered nothing
__label__MELVILLE the sailors were then given to understand that while the ship lay in dock the tobacco must remain in the cabin under custody of the chief mate who every morning would dole out to them one plug per head as a security against their carrying it ashore
__label__MELVILLE very good said the men
__label__MELVILLE but several of them had secret places in the ship from whence they daily drew pound after pound of tobacco which they smuggled ashore in the manner following
__label__MELVILLE when the crew went to meals each man carried at least one plug in his pocket that he had a right to and as many more were hidden about his person as he dared
__label__MELVILLE among the great crowds pouring out of the dock gates at such hours of course these smugglers stood little chance of detection although vigilant looking policemen were always standing by
__label__MELVILLE and though these charlies might suppose there were tobacco smugglers passing yet to hit the right man among such a throng would be as hard as to harpoon a speckled porpoise one of ten thousand darting under a ships bows
__label__MELVILLE our forecastle was often visited by foreign sailors who knowing we came from america were anxious to purchase tobacco at a cheap rate for in liverpool it is about an american penny per pipe full
__label__MELVILLE along the docks they sell an english pennyworth put up in a little roll like confectioners mottoes with poetical lines or instructive little moral precepts printed in red on the back
__label__MELVILLE among all the sights of the docks the noble truck horses are not the least striking to a stranger
__label__MELVILLE they are large and powerful brutes with such sleek and glossy coats that they look as if brushed and put on by a valet every morning
__label__MELVILLE they march with a slow and stately step lifting their ponderous hoofs like royal siam elephants
__label__MELVILLE thou shalt not lay stripes upon these roman citizens for their docility is such they are guided without rein or lash they go or come halt or march on at a whisper
__label__MELVILLE so grave dignified gentlemanly and courteous did these fine truck horses look so full of calm intelligence and sagacity that often i endeavored to get into conversation with them as they stood in contemplative attitudes while their loads were preparing
__label__MELVILLE but all i could get from them was the mere recognition of a friendly neigh though i would stake much upon it that could i have spoken in their language i would have derived from them a good deal of valuable information touching the docks where they passed the whole of their dignified lives
__label__MELVILLE there are unknown worlds of knowledge in brutes and whenever you mark a horse or a dog with a peculiarly mild calm deep seated eye be sure he is an aristotle or a kant tranquilly speculating upon the mysteries in man
__label__MELVILLE no philosophers so thoroughly comprehend us as dogs and horses
__label__MELVILLE they see through us at a glance
__label__MELVILLE and after all what is a horse but a species of four footed dumb man in a leathern overall who happens to live upon oats and toils for his masters half requited or abused like the biped hewers of wood and drawers of water
__label__MELVILLE but there is a touch of divinity even in brutes and a special halo about a horse that should forever exempt him from indignities
__label__MELVILLE as for those majestic magisterial truck horses of the docks i would as soon think of striking a judge on the bench as to lay violent hand upon their holy hides
__label__MELVILLE it is wonderful what loads their majesties will condescend to draw
__label__MELVILLE the truck is a large square platform on four low wheels and upon this the lumpers pile bale after bale of cotton as if they were filling a large warehouse and yet a procession of three of these horses will tranquilly walk away with the whole
__label__MELVILLE the truckmen themselves are almost as singular a race as their animals
__label__MELVILLE like the judiciary in england they wear gowns not of the same cut and color though which reach below their knees and from the racket they make on the pavements with their hob nailed brogans you would think they patronized the same shoemaker with their horses
__label__MELVILLE i never could get any thing out of these truckmen
__label__MELVILLE they are a reserved sober sided set who with all possible solemnity march at the head of their animals now and then gently advising them to sheer to the right or the left in order to avoid some passing vehicle
__label__MELVILLE then spending so much of their lives in the high bred company of their horses seems to have mended their manners and improved their taste besides imparting to them something of the dignity of their animals but it has also given to them a sort of refined and uncomplaining aversion to human society
__label__MELVILLE there are many strange stories told of the truck horse
__label__MELVILLE among others is the following there was a parrot that from having long been suspended in its cage from a low window fronting a dock had learned to converse pretty fluently in the language of the stevedores and truckmen
__label__MELVILLE one day a truckman left his vehicle standing on the quay with its back to the water
__label__MELVILLE it was noon when an interval of silence falls upon the docks and poll seeing herself face to face with the horse and having a mind for a chat cried out to him back
__label__MELVILLE back
__label__MELVILLE back
__label__MELVILLE backward went the horse precipitating himself and truck into the water
__label__MELVILLE brunswick dock to the west of princes is one of the most interesting to be seen
__label__MELVILLE here lie the various black steamers so unlike the american boats since they have to navigate the boisterous narrow seas plying to all parts of the three kingdoms
__label__MELVILLE here you see vast quantities of produce imported from starving ireland here you see the decks turned into pens for oxen and sheep and often side by side with these inclosures irish deck passengers thick as they can stand seemingly penned in just like the cattle
__label__MELVILLE it was the beginning of july when the highlander arrived in port and the irish laborers were daily coming over by thousands to help harvest the english crops
__label__MELVILLE one morning going into the town i heard a tramp as of a drove of buffaloes behind me and turning round beheld the entire middle of the street filled by a great crowd of these men who had just emerged from brunswick dock gates arrayed in long tailed coats of hoddin gray corduroy knee breeches and shod with shoes that raised a mighty dust
__label__MELVILLE flourishing their donnybrook shillelahs they looked like an irruption of barbarians
__label__MELVILLE they were marching straight out of town into the country and perhaps out of consideration for the finances of the corporation took the middle of the street to save the side walks
__label__MELVILLE sing langolee and the lakes of killarney cried one fellow tossing his stick into the air as he danced in his brogans at the head of the rabble
__label__MELVILLE and so they went
__label__MELVILLE capering on merry as pipers
__label__MELVILLE when i thought of the multitudes of irish that annually land on the shores of the united states and canada and to my surprise witnessed the additional multitudes embarking from liverpool to new holland and when added to all this i daily saw these hordes of laborers descending thick as locusts upon the english corn fields i could not help marveling at the fertility of an island which though her crop of potatoes may fail never yet failed in bringing her annual crop of men into the world
__label__MELVILLE i do not know that any other traveler would think it worth while to mention such a thing but the fact is that during the summer months in liverpool the days are exceedingly lengthy and the first evening i found myself walking in the twilight after nine oclock i tried to recall my astronomical knowledge in order to account satisfactorily for so curious a phenomenon
__label__MELVILLE but the days in summer and the nights in winter are just as long in liverpool as at cape horn for the latitude of the two places very nearly corresponds
__label__MELVILLE these liverpool days however were a famous thing for me who thereby was enabled after my days work aboard the highlander to ramble about the town for several hours
__label__MELVILLE after i had visited all the noted places i could discover of those marked down upon my fathers map i began to extend my rovings indefinitely forming myself into a committee of one to investigate all accessible parts of the town though so many years have elapsed ere i have thought of bringing in my report
__label__MELVILLE this was a great delight to me for wherever i have been in the world i have always taken a vast deal of lonely satisfaction in wandering about up and down among out of the way streets and alleys and speculating upon the strangers i have met
__label__MELVILLE thus in liverpool i used to pace along endless streets of dwelling houses looking at the names on the doors admiring the pretty faces in the windows and invoking a passing blessing upon the chubby children on the door steps
__label__MELVILLE i was stared at myself to be sure but what of that
__label__MELVILLE we must give and take on such occasions
__label__MELVILLE in truth i and my shooting jacket produced quite a sensation in liverpool and i have no doubt that many a father of a family went home to his children with a curious story about a wandering phenomenon they had encountered traversing the side walks that day
__label__MELVILLE in the words of the old song i cared for nobody no not i and nobody cared for me
__label__MELVILLE i stared my fill with impunity and took all stares myself in good part
__label__MELVILLE once i was standing in a large square gaping at a splendid chariot drawn up at a portico
__label__MELVILLE the glossy horses quivered with good living and so did the sumptuous calves of the gold laced coachman and footmen in attendance
__label__MELVILLE i was particularly struck with the red cheeks of these men and the many evidences they furnished of their enjoying this meal with a wonderful relish
__label__MELVILLE while thus standing i all at once perceived that the objects of my curiosity were making me an object of their own and that they were gazing at me as if i were some unauthorized intruder upon the british soil
__label__MELVILLE truly they had reason for when i now think of the figure i must have cut in those days i only marvel that in my many strolls my passport was not a thousand times demanded
__label__MELVILLE nevertheless i was only a forlorn looking mortal among tens of thousands of rags and tatters
__label__MELVILLE for in some parts of the town inhabited by laborers and poor people generally i used to crowd my way through masses of squalid men women and children who at this evening hour in those quarters of liverpool seem to empty themselves into the street and live there for the time
__label__MELVILLE i had never seen any thing like it in new york
__label__MELVILLE often i witnessed some curious and many very sad scenes and especially i remembered encountering a pale ragged man rushing along frantically and striving to throw off his wife and children who clung to his arms and legs and in gods name conjured him not to desert them
__label__MELVILLE he seemed bent upon rushing down to the water and drowning himself in some despair and craziness of wretchedness
__label__MELVILLE in these haunts beggary went on before me wherever i walked and dogged me unceasingly at the heels
__label__MELVILLE poverty poverty poverty in almost endless vistas and want and woe staggered arm in arm along these miserable streets
__label__MELVILLE and here i must not omit one thing that struck me at the time
__label__MELVILLE it was the absence of negroes who in the large towns in the free states of america almost always form a considerable portion of the destitute
__label__MELVILLE but in these streets not a negro was to be seen
__label__MELVILLE all were whites and with the exception of the irish were natives of the soil even englishmen as much englishmen as the dukes in the house of lords
__label__MELVILLE this conveyed a strange feeling and more than any thing else reminded me that i was not in my own land
__label__MELVILLE for there such a being as a native beggar is almost unknown and to be a born american citizen seems a guarantee against pauperism and this perhaps springs from the virtue of a vote
__label__MELVILLE speaking of negroes recalls the looks of interest with which negro sailors are regarded when they walk the liverpool streets
__label__MELVILLE in liverpool indeed the negro steps with a prouder pace and lifts his head like a man for here no such exaggerated feeling exists in respect to him as in america
__label__MELVILLE three or four times i encountered our black steward dressed very handsomely and walking arm in arm with a good looking english woman
__label__MELVILLE in new york such a couple would have been mobbed in three minutes and the steward would have been lucky to escape with whole limbs
__label__MELVILLE owing to the friendly reception extended to them and the unwonted immunities they enjoy in liverpool the black cooks and stewards of american ships are very much attached to the place and like to make voyages to it
__label__MELVILLE being so young and inexperienced then and unconsciously swayed in some degree by those local and social prejudices that are the marring of most men and from which for the mass there seems no possible escape at first i was surprised that a colored man should be treated as he is in this town but a little reflection showed that after all it was but recognizing his claims to humanity and normal equality so that in some things we americans leave to other countries the carrying out of the principle that stands at the head of our declaration of independence
__label__MELVILLE during my evening strolls in the wealthier quarters i was subject to a continual mortification
__label__MELVILLE it was the humiliating fact wholly unforeseen by me that upon the whole and barring the poverty and beggary liverpool away from the docks was very much such a place as new york
__label__MELVILLE there were the same sort of streets pretty much the same rows of houses with stone steps the same kind of side walks and curbs and the same elbowing heartless looking crowd as ever
__label__MELVILLE i came across the leeds canal one afternoon but upon my word no one could have told it from the erie canal at albany
__label__MELVILLE i went into st johns market on a saturday night and though it was strange enough to see that great roof supported by so many pillars yet the most discriminating observer would not have been able to detect any difference between the articles exposed for sale and the articles exhibited in fulton market new york
__label__MELVILLE i walked down lord street peering into the jewelers shops but i thought i was walking down a block in broadway
__label__MELVILLE i began to think that all this talk about travel was a humbug and that he who lives in a nut shell lives in an epitome of the universe and has but little to see beyond him
__label__MELVILLE it is true that i often thought of londons being only seven or eight hours travel by railroad from where i was and that there surely must be a world of wonders waiting my eyes but more of london anon
__label__MELVILLE sundays were the days upon which i made my longest explorations
__label__MELVILLE i rose bright and early with my whole plan of operations in my head
__label__MELVILLE first walking into some dock hitherto unexamined and then to breakfast
__label__MELVILLE then a walk through the more fashionable streets to see the people going to church and then i myself went to church selecting the goodliest edifice and the tallest kentuckian of a spire i could find
__label__MELVILLE for i am an admirer of church architecture and though perhaps the sums spent in erecting magnificent cathedrals might better go to the founding of charities yet since these structures are built those who disapprove of them in one sense may as well have the benefit of them in another
__label__MELVILLE it is a most christian thing and a matter most sweet to dwell upon and simmer over in solitude that any poor sinner may go to church wherever he pleases and that even st peters in rome is open to him as to a cardinal that st pauls in london is not shut against him and that the broadway tabernacle in new york opens all her broad aisles to him and will not even have doors and thresholds to her pews the better to allure him by an unbounded invitation
__label__MELVILLE i say this consideration of the hospitality and democracy in churches is a most christian and charming thought
__label__MELVILLE it speaks whole volumes of folios and vatican libraries for christianity it is more eloquent and goes farther home than all the sermons of massillon jeremy taylor wesley and archbishop tillotson
__label__MELVILLE nothing daunted therefore by thinking of my being a stranger in the land nothing daunted by the architectural superiority and costliness of any liverpool church or by the streams of silk dresses and fine broadcloth coats flowing into the aisles i used humbly to present myself before the sexton as a candidate for admission
__label__MELVILLE he would stare a little perhaps one of them once hesitated but in the end what could he do but show me into a pew not the most commodious of pews to be sure nor commandingly located nor within very plain sight or hearing of the pulpit
__label__MELVILLE no it was remarkable that there was always some confounded pillar or obstinate angle of the wall in the way and i used to think that the sextons of liverpool must have held a secret meeting on my account and resolved to apportion me the most inconvenient pew in the churches under their charge
__label__MELVILLE however they always gave me a seat of some sort or other sometimes even on an oaken bench in the open air of the aisle where i would sit dividing the attention of the congregation between myself and the clergyman
__label__MELVILLE the whole congregation seemed to know that i was a foreigner of distinction
__label__MELVILLE it was sweet to hear the service read the organ roll the sermon preached just as the same things were going on three thousand five hundred miles off at home
__label__MELVILLE but then the prayer in behalf of her majesty the queen somewhat threw me back
__label__MELVILLE nevertheless i joined in that prayer and invoked for the lady the best wishes of a poor yankee
__label__MELVILLE how i loved to sit in the holy hush of those brown old monastic aisles thinking of harry the eighth and the reformation
__label__MELVILLE how i loved to go a roving with my eye all along the sculptured walls and buttresses winding in among the intricacies of the pendent ceiling and wriggling my fancied way like a wood worm
__label__MELVILLE i could have sat there all the morning long through noon unto night
__label__MELVILLE but at last the benediction would come and appropriating my share of it i would slowly move away thinking how i should like to go home with some of the portly old gentlemen with high polished boots and malacca canes and take a seat at their cosy and comfortable dinner tables
__label__MELVILLE but alas
__label__MELVILLE there was no dinner for me except at the sign of the baltimore clipper
__label__MELVILLE yet the sunday dinners that handsome mary served up were not to be scorned
__label__MELVILLE the roast beef of old england abounded and so did the immortal plum puddings and the unspeakably capital gooseberry pies
__label__MELVILLE but to finish off with that abominable swipes almost spoiled all the rest not that i myself patronized swipes but my shipmates did and every cup i saw them drink i could not choose but taste in imagination and even then the flavor was bad
__label__MELVILLE on sundays at dinner time as indeed on every other day it was curious to watch the proceedings at the sign of the clipper
__label__MELVILLE the servant girls were running about mustering the various crews whose dinners were spread each in a separate apartment and who were collectively known by the names of their ships
__label__MELVILLE where are the arethusas heres their beef been smoking this half hour
__label__MELVILLE fly betty my dear here come the splendids
__label__MELVILLE run molly my love get the salt cellars for the highlanders
__label__MELVILLE you peggy wheres the siddons pickle pat
__label__MELVILLE i say judy are you never coming with that pudding for the lord nelsons
__label__MELVILLE on week days we did not fare quite so well as on sundays and once we came to dinner and found two enormous bullock hearts smoking at each end of the highlanders table
__label__MELVILLE jackson was indignant at the outrage
__label__MELVILLE he always sat at the head of the table and this time he squared himself on his bench and erecting his knife and fork like flag staffs so as to include the two hearts between them he called out for danby the boarding house keeper for although his wife mary was in fact at the head of the establishment yet danby himself always came in for the fault findings
__label__MELVILLE danby obsequiously appeared and stood in the doorway well knowing the philippics that were coming

__label__MELVILLE the jacket

__label__MELVILLE when our frigate lay in callao on the coast of peru her last harbour in the pacific i found myself without a grego or sailors surtout and as toward the end of a three years cruise no pea jackets could be had from the pursers steward and being bound for cape horn some sort of a substitute was indispensable i employed myself for several days in manufacturing an outlandish garment of my own devising to shelter me from the boisterous weather we were so soon to encounter

__label__MELVILLE a glance at the principal divisions into which a man of wars crew is divided
__label__MELVILLE having just designated the place where white jacket belonged it must needs be related how white jacket came to belong there
__label__MELVILLE every one knows that in merchantmen the seamen are divided into watches starboard and larboard taking their turn at the ships duty by night
__label__MELVILLE this plan is followed in all men of war
__label__MELVILLE but in all men of war besides this division there are others rendered indispensable from the great number of men and the necessity of precision and discipline
__label__MELVILLE not only are particular bands assigned to the three tops but in getting under weigh or any other proceeding requiring all hands particular men of these bands are assigned to each yard of the tops
__label__MELVILLE thus when the order is given to loose the main royal white jacket flies to obey it and no one but him
__label__MELVILLE and not only are particular bands stationed on the three decks of the ship at such times but particular men of those bands are also assigned to particular duties
__label__MELVILLE also in tacking ship reefing top sails or coming to every man of a frigates five hundred strong knows his own special place and is infallibly found there
__label__MELVILLE he sees nothing else attends to nothing else and will stay there till grim death or an epaulette orders him away
__label__MELVILLE yet there are times when through the negligence of the officers some exceptions are found to this rule
__label__MELVILLE a rather serious circumstance growing out of such a case will be related in some future chapter
__label__MELVILLE were it not for these regulations a man of wars crew would be nothing but a mob more ungovernable stripping the canvas in a gale than lord george gordons tearing down the lofty house of lord mansfield
__label__MELVILLE but this is not all
__label__MELVILLE besides white jackets office as looser of the main royal when all hands were called to make sail and besides his special offices in tacking ship coming to anchor etc
__label__MELVILLE nan he permanently belonged to the starboard watch one of the two primary grand divisions of the ships company
__label__MELVILLE and in this watch he was a maintop man that is was stationed in the main top with a number of other seamen always in readiness to execute any orders pertaining to the main mast from above the main yard
__label__MELVILLE for including the main yard and below it to the deck the main mast belongs to another detachment
__label__MELVILLE now the fore main and mizen top men of each watch starboard and larboard are at sea respectively subdivided into quarter watches which regularly relieve each other in the tops to which they may belong while collectively they relieve the whole larboard watch of top men
__label__MELVILLE besides these topmen who are always made up of active sailors there are sheet anchor men old veterans all whose place is on the forecastle the fore yard anchors and all the sails on the bowsprit being under their care
__label__MELVILLE they are an old weather beaten set culled from the most experienced seamen on board
__label__MELVILLE these are the fellows that sing you the bay of biscay oh and here a sheer hulk lies poor torn bowling cease rude boreas blustering railer who when ashore at an eating house call for a bowl of tar and a biscuit
__label__MELVILLE these are the fellows who spin interminable yarns about decatur hull and bainbridge and carry about their persons bits of old ironsides as catholics do the wood of the true cross
__label__MELVILLE these are the fellows that some officers never pretend to damn however much they may anathematize others
__label__MELVILLE these are the fellows that it does your soul good to look at hearty old members of the old guard grim sea grenadiers who in tempest time have lost many a tarpaulin overboard
__label__MELVILLE these are the fellows whose society some of the youngster midshipmen much affect from whom they learn their best seamanship and to whom they look up as veterans if so be that they have any reverence in their souls which is not the case with all midshipmen
__label__MELVILLE then there is the after guard stationed on the quarterdeck who under the quarter masters and quarter gunners attend to the main sail and spanker and help haul the main brace and other ropes in the stern of the vessel
__label__MELVILLE the duties assigned to the after guards men being comparatively light and easy and but little seamanship being expected from them they are composed chiefly of landsmen the least robust least hardy and least sailor like of the crew and being stationed on the quarter deck they are generally selected with some eye to their personal appearance
__label__MELVILLE hence they are mostly slender young fellows of a genteel figure and gentlemanly address not weighing much on a rope but weighing considerably in the estimation of all foreign ladies who may chance to visit the ship
__label__MELVILLE they lounge away the most part of their time in reading novels and romances talking over their lover affairs ashore and comparing notes concerning the melancholy and sentimental career which drove them poor young gentlemen into the hard hearted navy
__label__MELVILLE indeed many of them show tokens of having moved in very respectable society
__label__MELVILLE they always maintain a tidy exterior and express an abhorrence of the tar bucket into which they are seldom or never called to dip their digits
__label__MELVILLE and pluming themselves upon the cut of their trowsers and the glossiness of their tarpaulins from the rest of the ships company they acquire the name of sea dandies and silk sock gentry
__label__MELVILLE then there are the waisters always stationed on the gun deck
__label__MELVILLE these haul aft the fore and main sheets besides being subject to ignoble duties attending to the drainage and sewerage below hatches
__label__MELVILLE these fellows are all jimmy duxes sorry chaps who never put foot in ratlin or venture above the bulwarks
__label__MELVILLE inveterate sons of farmers with the hayseed yet in their hair they are consigned to the congenial superintendence of the chicken coops pig pens and potato lockers
__label__MELVILLE these are generally placed amidships on the gun deck of a frigate between the fore and main hatches and comprise so extensive an area that it much resembles the market place of a small town
__label__MELVILLE the melodious sounds thence issuing continually draw tears from the eyes of the waisters reminding them of their old paternal pig pens and potato patches
__label__MELVILLE they are the tag rag and bob tail of the crew and he who is good for nothing else is good enough for a waister
__label__MELVILLE three decks down spar deck gun deck and berth deck and we come to a parcel of troglodytes or holders who burrow like rabbits in warrens among the water tanks casks and cables
__label__MELVILLE like cornwall miners wash off the soot from their skins and they are all pale as ghosts
__label__MELVILLE unless upon rare occasions they seldom come on deck to sun themselves
__label__MELVILLE they may circumnavigate the world fifty times and they see about as much of it as jonah did in the whales belly
__label__MELVILLE they are a lazy lumpish torpid set and when going ashore after a long cruise come out into the day like terrapins from their caves or bears in the spring from tree trunks
__label__MELVILLE no one ever knows the names of these fellows after a three years voyage they still remain strangers to you
__label__MELVILLE in time of tempests when all hands are called to save ship they issue forth into the gale like the mysterious old men of paris during the massacre of the three days of september every one marvels who they are and whence they come they disappear as mysteriously and are seen no more until another general commotion
__label__MELVILLE such are the principal divisions into which a man of wars crew is divided but the inferior allotments of duties are endless and would require a german commentator to chronicle
__label__MELVILLE we say nothing here of boatswains mates gunners mates carpenters mates sail makers mates armorers mates master at arms ships corporals cockswains quarter masters quarter gunners captains of the forecastle captains of the fore top captains of the main top captains of the mizen top captains of the after guard captains of the main hold captains of the fore hold captains of the head coopers painters tinkers commodores steward captains steward ward room steward steerage steward commodores cook captains cook officers cook cooks of the range mess cooks hammock boys messenger boys cot boys loblolly boys and numberless others whose functions are fixed and peculiar
