__label__MELVILLE it was now late in the afternoon and for the present bent upon avoiding land and gaining the shoreless sea never mind where samoa again forced round his craft before the wind leaving the island astern
__label__MELVILLE the decks were still cumbered with the bodies of the lahineese which heel to point and crosswise had log like been piled up on the main hatch
__label__MELVILLE these one by one were committed to the sea after which the decks were washed down
__label__MELVILLE at sunrise next morning finding themselves out of sight of land with little or no wind they stopped their headway and lashed the tiller alee the better to enable them to overhaul the brigantine especially the recesses of the cabin
__label__MELVILLE for there were stores of goods adapted for barter among the islanders also several bags of dollars
__label__MELVILLE now nothing can exceed the cupidity of the polynesian when through partial commerce with the whites his eyes are opened to his nakedness and he perceives that in some things they are richer than himself
__label__MELVILLE the poor skippers wardrobe was first explored his chests of clothes being capsized and their contents strown about the cabin floor
__label__MELVILLE then took place the costuming
__label__MELVILLE samoa and annatoo trying on coats and pantaloons shirts and drawers and admiring themselves in the little mirror panneled in the bulk head
__label__MELVILLE then were broken open boxes and bales rolls of printed cotton were inspected and vastly admired insomuch that the trumpery found in the captains chests was disdainfully doffed and donned were loose folds of calico more congenial to their tastes
__label__MELVILLE as case after case was opened and overturned slippery grew the cabin deck with torrents of glass beads and heavy the necks of samoa and annatoo with goodly bunches thereof
__label__MELVILLE among other things came to light brass jewelry rag fair gewgaws and baubles a plenty more admired than all annatoo bedecking herself like a tragedy queen one blaze of brass
__label__MELVILLE much mourned the married dame that thus arrayed there was none to admire but samoa her husband but he was all the while admiring himself and not her
__label__MELVILLE and here must needs be related what has hitherto remained unsaid
__label__MELVILLE very often this husband and wife were no darby and joan
__label__MELVILLE their married life was one long campaign whereof the truces were only by night
__label__MELVILLE they billed and they cooed on their arms rising fresh in the morning to battle and often samoa got more than a hen pecking
__label__MELVILLE to be short annatoo was a tartar a regular calmuc and samoa heaven help him her husband
__label__MELVILLE yet awhile joined together by a sense of common danger and long engrossed in turning over their tinsel acquisitions without present thought of proprietorship the pair refrained from all squabbles
__label__MELVILLE but soon burst the storm
__label__MELVILLE having given every bale and every case a good shaking annatoo making an estimate of the whole very coolly proceeded to set apart for herself whatever she fancied
__label__MELVILLE to this samoa objected to which objection annatoo objected and then they went at it
__label__MELVILLE the lady vowed that the things were no more samoas than hers nay not so much and that whatever she wanted that same would she have
__label__MELVILLE and furthermore by way of codicil she declared that she was slave to nobody
__label__MELVILLE now samoa sad to tell stood in no little awe of his bellicose spouse
__label__MELVILLE what though a hero in other respects what though he had slain his savages and gallantly carried his craft from their clutches like the valiant captains marlborough and belisarius he was a poltroon to his wife
__label__MELVILLE and annatoo was worse than either sarah or antonina
__label__MELVILLE however like every thing partaking of the nature of a scratch most conjugal squabbles are quickly healed for if they healed not they would never anew break out which is the beauty of the thing
__label__MELVILLE so at length they made up but the treaty stipulations of annatoo told much against the interests of samoa
__label__MELVILLE nevertheless ostensibly it was agreed upon that they should strictly go halves the lady however laying special claim to certain valuables more particularly fancied
__label__MELVILLE but as a set off to this she generously renounced all claims upon the spare rigging all claims upon the fore mast and mainmast and all claims upon the captains arms and ammunition
__label__MELVILLE of the latter by the way dame antonina stood in no need
__label__MELVILLE her voice was a park of artillery her talons a charge of bayonets
__label__MELVILLE dedicated to the college of physicians and surgeons
__label__MELVILLE by this time samoas wounded arm was in such a state that amputation became necessary
__label__MELVILLE among savages severe personal injuries are for the most part accounted but trifles
__label__MELVILLE when a european would be taking to his couch in despair the savage would disdain to recline
__label__MELVILLE more yet
__label__MELVILLE in polynesia every man is his own barber and surgeon cutting off his beard or arm as occasion demands
__label__MELVILLE no unusual thing for the warriors of varvoo to saw off their own limbs desperately wounded in battle
__label__MELVILLE but owing to the clumsiness of the instrument employed a flinty serrated shell the operation has been known to last several days
__label__MELVILLE nor will they suffer any friend to help them maintaining that a matter so nearly concerning a warrior is far better attended to by himself
__label__MELVILLE hence it may be said that they amputate themselves at their leisure and hang up their tools when tired
__label__MELVILLE but though thus beholden to no one for aught connected with the practice of surgery they never cut off their own heads that ever i heard a species of amputation to which metaphorically speaking many would be independent sort of people in civilized lands are addicted
__label__MELVILLE samoas operation was very summary
__label__MELVILLE a fire was kindled in the little caboose or cook house and so made as to produce much smoke
__label__MELVILLE he then placed his arm upon one of the windlass bitts a short upright timber breast high and seizing the blunt cooks ax would have struck the blow but for some reason distrusting the precision of his aim annatoo was assigned to the task
__label__MELVILLE three strokes and the limb from just above the elbow was no longer samoas and he saw his own bones which many a centenarian can not say
__label__MELVILLE the very clumsiness of the operation was safety to the subject
__label__MELVILLE the weight and bluntness of the instrument both deadened the pain and lessened the hemorrhage
__label__MELVILLE the wound was then scorched and held over the smoke of the fire till all signs of blood vanished

__label__MELVILLE but that eye was a world
__label__MELVILLE now it was fixed upon yillah with a sinister glance and now upon me but with a different expression
__label__MELVILLE however great the crowd however tumultuous that fathomless eye gazed on till at last it seemed no eye but a spirit forever prying into my soul
__label__MELVILLE often i strove to approach it but it would evade me soon reappearing
__label__MELVILLE pointing out the apparition to media i intreated him to take means to fix it that my suspicions might be dispelled as to its being incorporeal
__label__MELVILLE he replied that by courtesy incognitos were sacred
__label__MELVILLE insomuch that the close plaited robe and the wimple were secure as a castle
__label__MELVILLE at last to my relief the phantom disappeared and was seen no more
__label__MELVILLE numerous and fervent the invitations received to return the calls wherewith we were honored
__label__MELVILLE but for the present we declined them preferring to establish ourselves firmly in the heart of media ere encountering the vicissitudes of roaming
__label__MELVILLE in a multitude of acquaintances is less security than in one faithful friend
__label__MELVILLE now while these civilities were being received and on the fourth morning after our arrival there landed on the beach three black eyed damsels deep brunettes habited in long variegated robes and with gay blossoms on their heads
__label__MELVILLE with many salams the strangers were ushered into my presence by an old white haired servitor of medias who with a parting conge murmured from queen hautia then departed
__label__MELVILLE surprised i stood mute and welcomed them
__label__MELVILLE the first with many smiles and blandishments waved before me a many tinted iris the flag flower streaming with pennons
__label__MELVILLE advancing the second then presented three rose hued purple veined circea flowers the dew still clinging to them
__label__MELVILLE the third placed in my hand a moss rose bud then a venus car
__label__MELVILLE thanks for your favors
__label__MELVILLE now your message
__label__MELVILLE starting at this reception graciously intended they conferred a moment when the iris bearer said in winning phrase we come from hautia whose moss rose you hold
__label__MELVILLE all thanks to hautia then the bud is very fragrant
__label__MELVILLE then she pointed to the venus car
__label__MELVILLE this too is sweet thanks to hautia for her flowers
__label__MELVILLE pray bring me more
__label__MELVILLE he mocks our mistress and gliding from me they waved witch hazels leaving me alone and wondering
__label__MELVILLE informing media of this scene he smiled threw out queer hints of hautia but knew not what her message meant
__label__MELVILLE at first this affair occasioned me no little uneasiness with much matter for marveling but in the novel pleasure of our sojourn in odo it soon slipped from my mind nor for some time did i again hear aught of queen hautia
__label__MELVILLE taji retires from the world
__label__MELVILLE after a while when the strangers came not in shoals as before i proposed to our host a stroll over his dominions desirous of beholding the same and secretly induced by the hope of selecting an abode more agreeable to my fastidious taste than the one already assigned me
__label__MELVILLE the ramble over a pleasant one it was it resulted in a determination on my part to quit odo
__label__MELVILLE yet not to go very far only ten or twelve yards to a little green tuft of an islet one of many which here and there all round the island nestled like birds nests in the branching boughs of the coral grove whose roots laid hold of the foundations of the deep
__label__MELVILLE between these islets and the shore extended shelving ledges with shallows above just sufficient to float a canoe
__label__MELVILLE one of these islets was wooded and wined an arbor in the sea
__label__MELVILLE and here media permitting i decided to dwell
__label__MELVILLE not long was media in complying nor long ere my retreat was in readiness
__label__MELVILLE laced together the twisting boughs were closely thatched
__label__MELVILLE and thatched were the sides also with deep crimson pandannus leaves whose long forked spears lifted by the breeze caused the whole place to blaze as with flames
__label__MELVILLE canes laid on palm trunks formed the floor
__label__MELVILLE how elastic
__label__MELVILLE in vogue all over odo among the chiefs it imparted such a buoyancy to the person that to this special cause may be imputed in good part the famous fine spirits of the nobles
__label__MELVILLE hypochondriac
__label__MELVILLE essay the elastic flooring
__label__MELVILLE it shall so pleasantly and gently jolt thee as to shake up and pack off the stagnant humors mantling thy pool like soul
__label__MELVILLE such was my dwelling
__label__MELVILLE but i make no mention of sundry little appurtenances of tropical housekeeping calabashes cocoanut shells and rolls of fine tappa till with yillah seated at last in my arbor i looked round and wanted for naught
__label__MELVILLE but what of jarl and samoa
__label__MELVILLE why jarl must needs be fanciful as well as myself
__label__MELVILLE like a bachelor in chambers he settled down right opposite to me on the main land in a little wigwam in the grove
__label__MELVILLE but samoa following not his comrades example still tarried in the camp of the hittites and jebusites of odo
__label__MELVILLE beguiling men of their leisure by his marvelous stories and maidens of their hearts by his marvelous wiles
__label__MELVILLE when i chose i was completely undisturbed in my arbor an ukase of medias forbidding indiscriminate intrusion
__label__MELVILLE but thrice in the day came a garrulous old man with my viands
__label__MELVILLE thus sequestered however i could not entirely elude the pryings of the people of the neighboring islands who often passed by slowly paddling and earnestly regarding my retreat
__label__MELVILLE but gliding along at a distance and never essaying a nan their occasional vicinity troubled me but little
__label__MELVILLE but now and then of an evening when thick and fleet the shadows were falling dim glimpses of a canoe would be spied hovering about the place like a ghost
__label__MELVILLE and once in the stillness of the night hearing the near ripple of a prow i sallied forth but the phantom quickly departed
__label__MELVILLE that night yillah shuddered as she slept
__label__MELVILLE the whirl pool she murmured sweet mosses
__label__MELVILLE next day she was lost in reveries plucking pensive hyacinths or gazing intently into the lagoon
__label__MELVILLE odo and its lord
__label__MELVILLE time now to enter upon some further description of the island and its lord
__label__MELVILLE and first for media a gallant gentleman and king
__label__MELVILLE from a goodly stock he came
__label__MELVILLE in his endless pedigree reckoning deities by decimals innumerable kings and scores of great heroes chiefs and priests
__label__MELVILLE nor in person did he belie his origin
__label__MELVILLE no far descended dwarf was he the least of a receding race
__label__MELVILLE he stood like a palm tree about whose acanthus capital droops not more gracefully the silken fringes than medias locks upon his noble brow
__label__MELVILLE strong was his arm to wield the club or hurl the javelin and potent i ween round a maidens waist
__label__MELVILLE thus much here for media
__label__MELVILLE now comes his isle
__label__MELVILLE our pleasant ramble found it a little round world by itself full of beauties as a garden chequered by charming groves watered by roving brooks and fringed all round by a border of palm trees whose roots drew nourishment from the water
__label__MELVILLE but though abounding in other quarters of the archipelago not a solitary bread fruit grew in odo
__label__MELVILLE a noteworthy circumstance observable in these regions where islands close adjoining so differ in their soil that certain fruits growing genially in one are foreign to another
__label__MELVILLE but odo was famed for its guavas whose flavor was likened to the flavor of new blown lips and for its grapes whose juices prompted many a laugh and many a groan
__label__MELVILLE beside the city where media dwelt there were few other clusters of habitations in odo
__label__MELVILLE the higher classes living here and there in separate households but not as eremites
__label__MELVILLE some buried themselves in the cool quivering bosoms of the groves
__label__MELVILLE others fancying a marine vicinity dwelt hard by the beach in little cages of bamboo whence of mornings they sallied out with jocund cries and went plunging into the refreshing bath whose frothy margin was the threshold of their dwellings
__label__MELVILLE others still like birds built their nests among the sylvan nooks of the elevated interior whence all below and hazy green lay steeped in languor the islands throbbing heart
__label__MELVILLE thus dwelt the chiefs and merry men of mark
__label__MELVILLE the common sort including serfs and helots war captives held in bondage lived in secret places hard to find
__label__MELVILLE whence it came that to a stranger the whole isle looked care free and beautiful
__label__MELVILLE deep among the ravines and the rocks these beings lived in noisome caves lairs for beasts not human homes or built them coops of rotten boughs living trees were banned them whose mouldy hearts hatched vermin
__label__MELVILLE fearing infection of some plague born of this filth the chiefs of odo seldom passed that way and looking round within their green retreats and pouring out their wine and plucking from orchards of the best marveled how these swine could grovel in the mire and wear such sallow cheeks
__label__MELVILLE but they offered no sweet homes from that mire they never sought to drag them out they open threw no orchard and intermitted not the mandates that condemned their drudges to a life of deaths
__label__MELVILLE sad sight
__label__MELVILLE to see those round shouldered helots stooping in their trenches artificial three in number and concentric the isle well nigh surrounding
__label__MELVILLE and herein fed by oozy loam and kindly dew from heaven and bitter sweat from men grew as in hot beds the nutritious taro
__label__MELVILLE toil is mans allotment toil of brain or toil of hands or a grief thats more than either the grief and sin of idleness
__label__MELVILLE but when man toils and slays himself for masters who withhold the life he gives to them then then the soul screams out and every sinew cracks
__label__MELVILLE so with these poor serfs
__label__MELVILLE and few of them could choose but be the brutes they seemed
__label__MELVILLE now needs it to be said that odo was no land of pleasure unalloyed and plenty without a pause odo in whose lurking places infants turned from breasts whence flowed no nourishment odo in whose inmost haunts dark groves were brooding passing which you heard most dismal cries and voices cursing media
__label__MELVILLE there men were scourged their crime a heresy the heresy that media was no demigod
__label__MELVILLE for this they shrieked
__label__MELVILLE their fathers shrieked before their fathers who tormented said happy we to groan that our childrens children may be glad
__label__MELVILLE but their childrens children howled
__label__MELVILLE yet these too echoed previous generations and loudly swore the pit thats dug for us may prove anothers grave
__label__MELVILLE but let all pass
__label__MELVILLE to look at and to roam about of holidays odo seemed a happy land
__label__MELVILLE the palm trees waved though here and there you marked one sear and palsy smitten the flowers bloomed though dead ones moldered in decay the waves ran up the strand in glee though receding they sometimes left behind bones mixed with shells
__label__MELVILLE but else than these no sign of death was seen throughout the isle
__label__MELVILLE did men in odo live for aye
__label__MELVILLE was ponce de leons fountain there
__label__MELVILLE for near and far you saw no ranks and files of graves no generations harvested in winrows
__label__MELVILLE in odo no hard hearted nabob slept beneath a gentle epitaph no requiescat in pace mocked a sinner damned no memento mori admonished men to live while yet they might
__label__MELVILLE here death hid his skull and hid it in the sea the common sepulcher of odo
__label__MELVILLE not dust to dust but dust to brine not hearses but canoes
__label__MELVILLE for all who died upon that isle were carried out beyond the outer reef and there were buried with their sires sires
__label__MELVILLE hence came the thought that of gusty nights when round the isles and high toward heaven flew the white reefs rack and foam that then and there kept chattering watch and ward the myriads that were ocean tombed
__label__MELVILLE but why these watery obsequies
__label__MELVILLE odo was but a little isle and must the living make way for the dead and lifes small colony be dislodged by deaths grim hosts as the gaunt tribes of tamerlane oerspread the tented pastures of the khan
__label__MELVILLE and now what follows said these islanders why sow corruption in the soil which yields us life
__label__MELVILLE we would not pluck our grapes from over graves
__label__MELVILLE this earths an urn for flowers not for ashes
__label__MELVILLE they said that oro the supreme had made a cemetery of the sea
__label__MELVILLE and what more glorious grave
__label__MELVILLE was mausolus more sublimely urned
__label__MELVILLE or do the minster lamps that burn before the tomb of charlemagne show more of pomp than all the stars that blaze above the shipwrecked mariner
__label__MELVILLE but no more of the dead men shrug their shoulders and love not their company though full soon we shall all have them for fellows
__label__MELVILLE yillah a phantom
__label__MELVILLE for a time we were happy in odo yillah and i in our islet
__label__MELVILLE nor did the pearl on her bosom glow more rosily than the roses in her cheeks though at intervals they waned and departed and deadly pale was her glance when she murmured of the whirlpool and mosses
__label__MELVILLE as pale my soul bethinking me of aleema the priest
__label__MELVILLE but day by day did her spell weave round me its magic and all the hidden things of her being grew more lovely and strange
__label__MELVILLE did i commune with a spirit
__label__MELVILLE often i thought that paradise had overtaken me on earth and that yillah was verily an angel and hence the mysteries that hallowed her
__label__MELVILLE but how fleeting our joys
__label__MELVILLE storms follow bright dawnings long memories of short lived scenes sad thoughts of joyous hours how common are ye to all mankind
__label__MELVILLE when happy do we pause and say lo thy felicity my soul
__label__MELVILLE no happiness seldom seems happiness except when looked back upon from woes
__label__MELVILLE a flowery landscape you must come out of to behold
__label__MELVILLE sped the hours the days the one brief moment of our joys
__label__MELVILLE fairy bower in the fair lagoon scene of sylvan ease and hearts repose oh yillah yillah
__label__MELVILLE all the woods repeat the sound the wild wild woods of my wild soul
__label__MELVILLE yillah
__label__MELVILLE yillah
__label__MELVILLE cry the small strange voices in me and evermore and far and deep they echo on
__label__MELVILLE days passed
__label__MELVILLE when one morning i found the arbor vacant
__label__MELVILLE gone
__label__MELVILLE a dream
__label__MELVILLE i closed my eyes and would have dreamed her back
__label__MELVILLE in vain
__label__MELVILLE starting i called upon her name but none replied
__label__MELVILLE fleeing from the islet i gained the neighboring shore and searched among the woods and my comrades meeting besought their aid
__label__MELVILLE but idle all
__label__MELVILLE no glimpse of aught save trees and flowers
__label__MELVILLE then media was sought out the event made known and quickly bands were summoned to range the isle
__label__MELVILLE noon came but no yillah
__label__MELVILLE when media averred she was no longer in odo
__label__MELVILLE whither she was gone or how he knew not nor could any imagine
__label__MELVILLE at this juncture there chanced to arrive certain messengers from abroad who presuming that all was well with taji came with renewed invitations to visit various pleasant places round about
__label__MELVILLE among these came queen hautias heralds with their iris flag once more bringing flowers
__label__MELVILLE but they came and went unheeded
__label__MELVILLE setting out to return these envoys were accompanied by numerous followers of media dispatched to the neighboring islands to seek out the missing yillah
__label__MELVILLE but three days passed and one by one they all returned and stood before me silently
__label__MELVILLE for a time i raved
__label__MELVILLE then falling into outer repose lived for a space in moods and reveries with eyes that knew no closing one glance forever fixed
__label__MELVILLE they strove to rouse me
__label__MELVILLE girls danced and sang and tales of fairy times were told of monstrous imps and youths enchanted of groves and gardens in the sea
__label__MELVILLE yet still i moved not hearing all yet noting naught
__label__MELVILLE media cried for shame oh taji thou a god
__label__MELVILLE and placed a spear in my nerveless hand
__label__MELVILLE and jarl loud called upon me to awake
__label__MELVILLE samoa marveled
__label__MELVILLE still sped the days
__label__MELVILLE and at length my memory was restored
__label__MELVILLE the thoughts of things broke over me like returning billows on a beach long bared
__label__MELVILLE a rush a foam of recollections sweet yillah gone and i bereaved
__label__MELVILLE another interval and that mood was past
__label__MELVILLE misery became a memory
__label__MELVILLE the keen pang a deep vibration
__label__MELVILLE the remembrance seemed the thing remembered though bowed with sadness
__label__MELVILLE there are thoughts that lie and glitter deep tearful pearls beneath lifes sea that surges still and rolls sunlit whatever it may hide
__label__MELVILLE common woes like fluids mix all round
__label__MELVILLE not so with that other grief
__label__MELVILLE some mourners load the air with lamentations but the loudest notes are struck from hollows
__label__MELVILLE their tears flow fast but the deep spring only wells
__label__MELVILLE at last i turned to media saying i must hie from odo and rove throughout all mardi for yillah might yet be found
__label__MELVILLE but hereafter in words little more of the maiden till perchance her fate be learned
__label__MELVILLE taji makes three acquaintances
__label__MELVILLE down to this period i had restrained samoa from wandering to the neighboring islands though he had much desired it in compliance with the invitations continually received
__label__MELVILLE but now i informed both him and his comrade of the tour i purposed desiring their company
__label__MELVILLE upon the announcement of my intention to depart to my no small surprise media also proposed to accompany me a proposition gladly embraced
__label__MELVILLE it seems that for some reason he had not as yet extended his travels to the more distant islands
__label__MELVILLE hence the voyage in prospect was particularly agreeable to him
__label__MELVILLE nor did he forbear any pains to insure its prosperity assuring me furthermore that its object must eventually be crowned with success
__label__MELVILLE i myself am interested in this pursuit said he and trust me yillah will be found
__label__MELVILLE for the tour of the lagoon the docile chamois was proposed but media dissented saying that it befitted not the lord of odo to voyage in the equipage of his guest
__label__MELVILLE therefore three canoes were selected from his own royal fleet
__label__MELVILLE one for ourselves and a trio of companions whom he purposed introducing to my notice the rest were reserved for attendants
__label__MELVILLE thanks to medias taste and heedfulness the strangers above mentioned proved truly acceptable
__label__MELVILLE the first was mohi or braid beard so called from the manner in which he wore that appendage exceedingly long and gray
__label__MELVILLE he was a venerable teller of stories and legends one of the keepers of the chronicles of the kings of mardi
__label__MELVILLE the second was babbalanja a man of a mystical aspect habited in a voluminous robe
__label__MELVILLE he was learned in mardian lore much given to quotations from ancient and obsolete authorities the ponderings of old bardianna the pandects of alla malolla
__label__MELVILLE third and last was yoomy or the warbler
__label__MELVILLE a youthful long haired blue eyed minstrel all fits and starts at times absent of mind and wan of cheek but always very neat and pretty in his apparel wearing the most becoming of turbans a bird of paradise feather its plume and sporting the gayest of sashes
__label__MELVILLE most given was yoomy to amorous melodies and rondos and roundelays very witching to hear
__label__MELVILLE but at times disdaining the oaten reed like a clarion he burst forth with lusty lays of arms and battle or in mournful strains sounded elegies for departed bards and heroes
__label__MELVILLE thus much for yoomy as a minstrel
__label__MELVILLE in other respects it would be hard to depict him
__label__MELVILLE he was so capricious a mortal so swayed by contrary moods so lofty so humble so sad so merry so made up of a thousand contradictions that we must een let him depict himself as our story progresses
__label__MELVILLE and herein it is hoped he will succeed since no one in mardi comprehended him
__label__MELVILLE now the trio thus destined for companions on our voyage had for some time been anxious to take the tour of the archipelago
__label__MELVILLE in particular babbalanja had often expressed the most ardent desire to visit every one of the isles in quest of some object mysteriously hinted
__label__MELVILLE he murmured deep concern for my loss the sincerest sympathy and pressing my hand more than once said lowly your pursuit is mine noble taji
__label__MELVILLE whereer you search i follow
__label__MELVILLE so too yoomy addressed me but with still more feeling
__label__MELVILLE and something like this also braid beard repeated
__label__MELVILLE but to my sorrow i marked that both mohi and babbalanja especially the last seemed not so buoyant of hope concerning lost yillah as the youthful yoomy and his high spirited lord king media
__label__MELVILLE as our voyage would embrace no small period of time it behoved king media to appoint some trustworthy regent to rule during his absence
__label__MELVILLE this regent was found in almanni a stem eyed resolute warrior a kinsman of the king
__label__MELVILLE all things at last in readiness and the ensuing morning appointed for a start media on the beach at eventide when both light and water waned drew a rude map of the lagoon to compensate for the obstructions in the way of a comprehensive glance at it from odo
__label__MELVILLE and thus was sketched the plan of our voyage which islands first to visit and which to touch at when we should be homeward bound
__label__MELVILLE with a fair wind at sunrise they sail
__label__MELVILLE true each to his word up came the sun and round to my isle came media
__label__MELVILLE how glorious a morning
__label__MELVILLE the new born clouds all dappled with gold and streaked with violet the sun in high spirits and the pleasant air cooled overnight by the blending circumambient fountains forever playing all round the reef the lagoon within the coral rimmed basin into which they poured subsiding hereabouts into green tranquillity
__label__MELVILLE but what monsters of canoes
__label__MELVILLE would they devour an innocent voyager
__label__MELVILLE their great black prows curling aloft and thrown back like trunks of elephants a dark snaky length behind like the sea serpents train
__label__MELVILLE the prow of the foremost terminated in a large open sharks mouth garnished with ten rows of pearly human teeth curiously inserted into the sculptured wood
__label__MELVILLE the gunwale was ornamented with rows of rich spotted leopard and tiger shells here and there varied by others flat and round and spirally traced gay serpents petrified in coils
__label__MELVILLE these were imbedded in a grooved margin by means of a resinous compound exhaling such spices that the canoes were odoriferous as the indian chests of the maldives
__label__MELVILLE the likeness of the foremost canoe to an elephant was helped by a sort of canopied howdah in its stern of heavy russet dyed tappa tasselled at the corners with long bunches of cocoanut fibres stained red
__label__MELVILLE these swayed to and fro like the fox tails on a tuscarora robe
__label__MELVILLE but what is this in the head of the canoe just under the sharks mouth
__label__MELVILLE a grinning little imp of an image a ring in its nose cowrie shells jingling at its ears with an abominable leer like that of silenus reeling on his ass
__label__MELVILLE it was taking its ease cosily smoking a pipe its bowl a duodecimo edition of the face of the smoker
__label__MELVILLE this image looked sternward everlastingly mocking us
__label__MELVILLE of these canoes it may be well to state that although during our stay in odo so many barges and shallops had touched there nothing similar to medias had been seen
__label__MELVILLE but inquiring whence his sea equipage came we were thereupon taught to reverence the same as antiquities and heir looms claw keeled dragon prowed crafts of a bygone generation at present superseded in general use by the more swan like canoes significant of the advanced stage of marine architecture in mardi
__label__MELVILLE no sooner was this known than what had seemed almost hideous in my eyes became merely grotesque
__label__MELVILLE nor could i help being greatly delighted with the good old family pride of our host
__label__MELVILLE the upper corners of our sails displayed the family crest of media three upright boars tusks in an heraldic field argent
__label__MELVILLE a fierce device whom rends he
__label__MELVILLE all things in readiness we glided away the multitude waving adieu and our flotilla disposed in the following order
__label__MELVILLE first went the royal elephant carrying media myself jarl and samoa mohi the teller of legends babbalanja and yoomy and six vivacious paddlers their broad paddle blades carved with the royal boars tusks the same tattooed on their chests for a livery
__label__MELVILLE and thus as media had promised we voyaged in state
__label__MELVILLE to crown all seated sideways in the high open sharks mouth of our prow was a little dwarf of a boy one of medias pages a red conch shell bugle wise suspended at his side
__label__MELVILLE among various other offices it was the duty of little vee vee to announce the advent of his master upon drawing near to the islands in our route
__label__MELVILLE two short bars projecting from one side of the prow furnished him the means of ascent to his perch
__label__MELVILLE as we gained the open lagoon with bellied sails and paddles playing a sheaf of foam borne upright at our prow yoomy standing where the spicy spray flew over him stretched forth his hand and cried the dawn of day is passed and mardi lies all before us all her isles and all her lakes all her stores of good and evil
__label__MELVILLE storms may come our barks may drown
__label__MELVILLE but blow before us all ye winds give us a lively blast good clarion rally round us all our wits and be this voyage full gayly sailed for yillah will yet be found
__label__MELVILLE little king peepi
__label__MELVILLE valapee or the isle of yams being within plain sight of medias dominions we were not very long in drawing nigh to its shores
__label__MELVILLE two long parallel elevations rising some three arrow flights into the air double ridge the islands entire length lapping between a widening vale so level withal that at either extremity the green of its groves blends with the green of the lagoon and the isle seems divided by a strait
__label__MELVILLE within several paces of the beach our canoes keeled the bottom and camel like mutely hinted that we voyagers must dismount
__label__MELVILLE hereupon the assembled islanders ran into the water and with bent shoulders obsequiously desired the honor of transporting us to land
__label__MELVILLE the beach gained all present wearing robes instantly stripped them to the waist a naked chest being their salute to kings
__label__MELVILLE very convenient for the common people this their half clad forms presenting a perpetual and profound salutation
__label__MELVILLE presently peepi the ruler of valapee drew near a boy hardly ten years old striding the neck of a burly mute bearing a long spear erect before him to which was attached a canopy of five broad banana leaves new plucked
__label__MELVILLE thus shaded little peepi advanced steadying himself by the forelock of his bearer
__label__MELVILLE besides his bright red robe the young prince wore nothing but the symbol of valapeean royalty a string of small close fitting concave shells coiled and ambushed in his profuse curly hair one end falling over his ear revealing a serpents head curiously carved from a nutmeg
__label__MELVILLE quite proverbial the unembarrassed air of young slips of royalty
__label__MELVILLE but there was something so surprisingly precocious in this young peepi that at first one hardly knew what to conclude
__label__MELVILLE the first compliments over the company were invited inland to a shady retreat

__label__MELVILLE peepi it seems had been proclaimed king before he was born his sire dying some few weeks previous to that event and vacating his divan declared that he left a monarch behind
__label__MELVILLE marvels were told of peepi
__label__MELVILLE along with the royal dignity and superadded to the soul possessed in his own proper person the infant monarch was supposed to have inherited the valiant spirits of some twenty heroes sages simpletons and demi gods previously lodged in his sire
__label__MELVILLE most opulent in spiritual gifts was this lord of valapee the legatee moreover of numerous anonymous souls bequeathed to him by their late loyal proprietors

__label__MELVILLE it was to the frequent practice of this ceremony that most intelligent observers imputed the flattened noses of the elderly chiefs of the island who nevertheless much gloried therein

__label__MELVILLE but had all these and similar opposite qualities simultaneously acted as motives upon peepi certes he would have been a most pitiable mortal in a ceaseless eddy of resolves incapable of a solitary act

__label__MELVILLE many ages ago there reigned in juam a king called teei
__label__MELVILLE this teeis succession to the sovereignty was long disputed by his brother marjora who at last rallying round him an army after many vicissitudes defeated the unfortunate monarch in a stout fight of clubs on the beach
__label__MELVILLE in those days willamilla during a certain period of the year was a place set apart for royal games and diversions and was furnished with suitable accommodations for king and court
__label__MELVILLE from its peculiar position moreover it was regarded as the last stronghold of the juam monarchy in remote times having twice withstood the most desperate assaults from without
__label__MELVILLE and when roonoonoo a famous upstart sought to subdue all the isles in this part of the archipelago it was to willamilla that the banded kings had repaired to take counsel together and while there conferring were surprised at the sudden onslaught of roonoonoo in person
__label__MELVILLE but in the end the rebel was captured he and all his army and impaled on the tops of the hills

__label__MELVILLE when stripping from the body the regal girdle the victor wound it round his own loins thus proclaiming himself king over juam

__label__MELVILLE but at length a sacred oracle declared that since the conqueror had slain his brother in deep willamilla so that teei never more issued from that refuge of death therefore the same fate should be marjoras for never thenceforth from that glen should he go forth neither marjora nor any son of his girdled loins nor his sons sons nor the uttermost scion of his race
__label__MELVILLE but except this denunciation naught was denounced against the usurper who mindful of the tenure by which he reigned ruled over the island for many moons at his death bequeathing the girdle to his son

__label__MELVILLE maramma
__label__MELVILLE we were now voyaging straight for maramma where lived and reigned in mystery the high pontiff of the adjoining isles prince priest and god in his own proper person great lord paramount over many kings in mardi his hands full of scepters and crosiers
__label__MELVILLE soon rounding a lofty and insulated shore the great central peak of the island came in sight domineering over the neighboring hills the same aspiring pinnacle descried in drawing near the archipelago in the chamois
__label__MELVILLE tall peak of ofo
__label__MELVILLE cried babbalanja how comes it that thy shadow so broods over mardi flinging new shades upon spots already shaded by the hill sides shade upon shade
__label__MELVILLE yet so it is said yoomy sadly that where that shadow falls gay flowers refuse to spring and men long dwelling therein become shady of face and of soul
__label__MELVILLE hast thou come from out the shadows of ofo
__label__MELVILLE inquires the stranger of one with a clouded brow
__label__MELVILLE it was by this same peak said mohi that the nimble god roo a great sinner above came down from the skies a very long time ago
__label__MELVILLE three skips and a jump and he landed on the plain
__label__MELVILLE but alas poor roo
__label__MELVILLE though easy the descent there was no climbing back
__label__MELVILLE no wonder then said babbalanja that the peak is inaccessible to man

__label__MELVILLE ay said mohi in vain on all sides of the peak various paths are tried in vain new ones are cut through the cliffs and the brambles ofo yet remains inaccessible
__label__MELVILLE nevertheless said babbalanja by some it is believed that those who by dint of hard struggling climb so high as to become invisible from the plain that these have attained the summit though others much doubt whether their be coming invisible is not because of their having fallen and perished by the way
__label__MELVILLE and wherefore said media do you mortals undertake the ascent at all
__label__MELVILLE why not be content on the plain
__label__MELVILLE and even if attainable what would you do upon that lofty clouded summit
__label__MELVILLE or how can you hope to breathe that rarefied air unfitted for your human lungs
__label__MELVILLE true my lord said babbalanja and bardianna asserts that the plain alone was intended for man who should be content to dwell under the shade of its groves though the roots thereof descend into the darkness of the earth
__label__MELVILLE but my lord you well know that there are those in mardi who secretly regard all stories connected with this peak as inventions of the people of maramma
__label__MELVILLE they deny that any thing is to be gained by making a pilgrimage thereto

__label__MELVILLE cried mohi but alma is also quoted by others in vindication of the pilgrimages to ofo
__label__MELVILLE they declare that the prophet himself was the first pilgrim that thitherward journeyed that from thence he departed to the skies
__label__MELVILLE now excepting this same peak maramma is all rolling hill and dale like the sea after a storm which then seems not to roll but to stand still poising its mountains

__label__MELVILLE according to mohi not one solitary tree bearing fruit not one esculent root grows in all the isle the population wholly depending upon the large tribute remitted from the neighboring shores

__label__MELVILLE it is extremely fertile but the inhabitants say that it would be wrong to make a bread fruit orchard of the holy island
__label__MELVILLE and hence my lord said babbalanja while others are charged with the business of their temporal welfare these islanders take no thought of the morrow and broad maramma lies one fertile waste in the lagoon
__label__MELVILLE they land
__label__MELVILLE coming close to the island the pennons and trappings of our canoes were removed and vee vee was commanded to descend from the sharks mouth and for a time to lay aside his conch

__label__MELVILLE winding our way among jungles we came to a deep hollow planted with one gigantic palm shaft belted round by saplings springing from its roots
__label__MELVILLE but laocoon like sire and sons stood locked in the serpent folds of gnarled distorted banians and the banian bark eating into their vital wood corrupted their veins of sap till all those palm nuts were poisoned chalices
__label__MELVILLE near by stood clean limbed comely manchineels with lustrous leaves and golden fruit

__label__MELVILLE owls hooted from dead boughs or one by one sailed by on silent pinions cranes stalked abroad or brooded in the marshes adders hissed bats smote the darkness ravens croaked and vampires fixed on slumbering lizards fanned the sultry air
__label__MELVILLE hivohitee mdcccxlviii
__label__MELVILLE now those doleful woodlands passed straightway converse was renewed and much discourse took place concerning hivohitee pontiff of the isle
__label__MELVILLE for during our first friendly conversation with pani media had inquired for hivohitee and sought to know in what part of the island he abode
__label__MELVILLE whereto pani had replied that the pontiff would be invisible for several days to come being engaged with particular company
__label__MELVILLE and upon further inquiry as to who were the personages monopolizing his hospitalities media was dumb when informed that they were no other than certain incorporeal deities from above passing the capricorn solstice at maramma
__label__MELVILLE as on we journeyed much curiosity being expressed to know more of the pontiff and his guests old mohi familiar with these things was commanded to enlighten the company
__label__MELVILLE he complied and his recital was not a little significant of the occasional credulity of chroniclers
__label__MELVILLE according to his statement the deities entertained by hivohitee belonged to the third class of immortals
__label__MELVILLE these however were far elevated above the corporeal demi gods of mardi
__label__MELVILLE indeed in hivohitees eyes the greatest demi gods were as gourds
__label__MELVILLE little wonder then that their superiors were accounted the most genteel characters on his visiting list
__label__MELVILLE these immortals were wonderfully fastidious and dainty as to the atmosphere they breathed inhaling no sublunary air but that of the elevated interior where the pontiff had a rural lodge for the special accommodation of impalpable guests who were entertained at very small cost dinners being unnecessary and dormitories superfluous
__label__MELVILLE but hivohitee permitted not the presence of these celestial grandees to interfere with his own solid comfort
__label__MELVILLE passing his mornings in highly intensified chat he thrice reclined at his ease partaking of a fine plantain pudding and pouring out from a calabash of celestial old wine meanwhile carrying on the flow of soul with his guests
__label__MELVILLE and truly the sight of their entertainer thus enjoying himself in the flesh while they themselves starved on the ether must have been exceedingly provoking to these aristocratic and aerial strangers
__label__MELVILLE it was reported furthermore that hivohitee one of the haughtiest of pontiffs purposely treated his angelical guests thus cavalierly in order to convince them that though a denizen of earth a sublunarian and in respect of heaven a mere provincial he hivohitee accounted himself full as good as seraphim from the capital and that too at the capricorn solstice or any other time of the year
__label__MELVILLE strongly bent was hivohitee upon humbling their supercilious pretensions
__label__MELVILLE besides was he not accounted a great god in the land
__label__MELVILLE supreme
__label__MELVILLE having power of life and death
__label__MELVILLE essaying the deposition of kings
__label__MELVILLE and dwelling in moody state all by himself in the goodliest island of mardi
__label__MELVILLE though here be it said that his assumptions of temporal supremacy were but seldom made good by express interference with the secular concerns of the neighboring monarchs who by force of arms were too apt to argue against his claims to authority however in theory they bowed to it
__label__MELVILLE and now for the genealogy of hivohitee for eighteen hundred and forty seven hivohitees were alleged to have gone before him
__label__MELVILLE he came in a right line from the divine hivohitee i the original grantee of the empire of mens souls and the first swayer of a crosier
__label__MELVILLE the present pontiffs descent was unquestionable his dignity having been transmitted through none but heirs male the whole procession of high priests being the fruit of successive marriages between uterine brother and sister
__label__MELVILLE a conjunction deemed incestuous in some lands but here held the only fit channel for the pure transmission of elevated rank
__label__MELVILLE added to the hereditary appellation hivohitee which simply denoted the sacerdotal station of the pontiffs and was but seldom employed in current discourse they were individualized by a distinctive name bestowed upon them at birth
__label__MELVILLE and the degree of consideration in which they were held may be inferred from the fact that during the lifetime of a pontiff the leading sound in his name was banned to ordinary uses
__label__MELVILLE whence at every new accession to the archiepiscopal throne it came to pass that multitudes of words and phrases were either essentially modified or wholly dropped
__label__MELVILLE wherefore the language of maramma was incessantly fluctuating and had become so full of jargonings that the birds in the groves were greatly puzzled not knowing where lay the virtue of sounds so incoherent
__label__MELVILLE and in a good measure this held true of all tongues spoken throughout the archipelago the birds marveling at mankind and mankind at the birds wondering how they could continually sing when for all man knew to the contrary it was impossible they could be holding intelligent discourse
__label__MELVILLE and thus though for thousands of years men and birds had been dwelling together in mardi they remained wholly ignorant of each others secrets the islander regarding the fowl as a senseless songster forever in the clouds and the fowl him as a screeching crane destitute of pinions and lofty aspirations
__label__MELVILLE over and above numerous other miraculous powers imputed to the pontiffs as spiritual potentates there was ascribed to them one special privilege of a secular nature that of healing with a touch the bites of the ravenous sharks swarming throughout the lagoon
__label__MELVILLE with these they were supposed to be upon the most friendly terms according to popular accounts sociably bathing with them in the sea permitting them to rub their noses against their priestly thighs playfully mouthing their hands with all their tiers of teeth
__label__MELVILLE at the ordination of a pontiff the ceremony was not deemed complete until embarking in his barge he was saluted high priest by three sharks drawing near with teeth turned up swimming beside his canoe
__label__MELVILLE these monsters were deified in maramma had altars there it was deemed worse than homicide to kill one
__label__MELVILLE and what if they destroy human life
__label__MELVILLE say the islanders are they not sacred
__label__MELVILLE now many more wonderful things were related touching hivohitee and though one could not but doubt the validity of many prerogatives ascribed to him it was nevertheless hard to do otherwise than entertain for the pontiff that sort of profound consideration which all render to those who indisputably possess the power of quenching human life with a wish
__label__MELVILLE they visit the great morai
__label__MELVILLE as garrulous guide to the party braid beard soon brought us nigh the great morai of maramma the burial place of the pontiffs and a rural promenade for certain idols there inhabiting
__label__MELVILLE our way now led through the bed of a shallow water course mohi observing as we went that our feet were being washed at every step whereas to tread the dusty earth would be to desecrate the holy morai by transferring thereto the base soil of less sacred ground
__label__MELVILLE here and there thatched arbors were thrown over the stream for the accommodation of devotees who in these consecrated waters issuing from a spring in the morai bathed their garments that long life might ensue
__label__MELVILLE yet as braid beard assured us sometimes it happened that divers feeble old men zealously donning their raiment immediately after immersion became afflicted with rheumatics and instances were related of their falling down dead in this their pursuit of longevity
__label__MELVILLE coming to the morai we found it inclosed by a wall and while the rest were surmounting it mohi was busily engaged in the apparently childish occupation of collecting pebbles
__label__MELVILLE of these however to our no small surprise he presently made use by irreverently throwing them at all objects to which he was desirous of directing attention
__label__MELVILLE in this manner was pointed out a black boars head suspended from a bough
__label__MELVILLE full twenty of these sentries were on post in the neighboring trees
__label__MELVILLE proceeding we came to a hillock of bone dry sand resting upon the otherwise loamy soil
__label__MELVILLE possessing a secret preservative virtue this sand had ages ago been brought from a distant land to furnish a sepulcher for the pontiffs who here side by side and sire by son slumbered all peacefully in the fellowship of the grave
__label__MELVILLE mohi declared that were the sepulcher to be opened it would be the resurrection of the whole line of high priests
__label__MELVILLE but a resurrection of bones after all said babbalanja ever osseous in his allusions to the departed
__label__MELVILLE passing on we came to a number of runic looking stones all over hieroglyphical inscriptions and placed round an elliptical aperture where welled up the sacred spring of the morai clear as crystal and showing through its waters two tiers of sharp tusk like stones the mouth of oro so called and it was held that if any secular hand should be immersed in the spring straight upon it those stony jaws would close
__label__MELVILLE we next came to a large image of a dark hued stone representing a burly man with an overgrown head and abdomen hollowed out and open for inspection therein were relics of bones
__label__MELVILLE before this image we paused

__label__MELVILLE to insure his digestion all indirect routes to the interior were avoided the sacrifices being packed in the ventricle itself

__label__MELVILLE it seems there was a particular family upon the island whose members for many generations had been set apart as sacrifices for the deity called doleema

__label__MELVILLE and though when it came to the last some of these unfortunates went joyfully to their doom declaring that they gloried to die in the service of holy doleema still were there others who audaciously endeavored to shun their fate upon the approach of a festival fleeing to the innermost wilderness of the island

__label__MELVILLE now many moons ago according to braid beard the tapparians of a certain cluster of islands seeing themselves hopelessly confounded with the plebeian race of mortals such as artificers honest men bread fruit bakers and the like seeing in short that nature had denied them every inborn mark of distinction and furthermore that their external assumptions were derided by so many in mardi these selfsame tapparians poor devils resolved to secede from the rabble form themselves into a community of their own and conventionally pay that homage to each other which universal mardi could not be prevailed upon to render to them
__label__MELVILLE jointly they purchased an island called pimminee toward the extreme west of the lagoon and thither they went and framing a code of laws amazingly arbitrary considering they themselves were the framers solemnly took the oath of allegiance to the commonwealth thus established

__label__MELVILLE all girdles must be so many inches in length and with such a number of tassels in front

__label__MELVILLE in the year 1799 captain amasa delano of duxbury in massachusetts commanding a large sealer and general trader lay at anchor with a valuable cargo in the harbor of st maria a small desert uninhabited island toward the southern extremity of the long coast of chili

__label__MELVILLE on the second day not long after dawn while lying in his berth his mate came below informing him that a strange sail was coming into the bay
__label__MELVILLE ships were then not so plenty in those waters as now
__label__MELVILLE he rose dressed and went on deck
__label__MELVILLE the morning was one peculiar to that coast
__label__MELVILLE everything was mute and calm everything gray
__label__MELVILLE the sea though undulated into long roods of swells seemed fixed and was sleeked at the surface like waved lead that has cooled and set in the smelters mould
__label__MELVILLE the sky seemed a gray surtout
__label__MELVILLE flights of troubled gray fowl kith and kin with flights of troubled gray vapors among which they were mixed skimmed low and fitfully over the waters as swallows over meadows before storms
__label__MELVILLE shadows present foreshadowing deeper shadows to come

__label__MELVILLE considering the lawlessness and loneliness of the spot and the sort of stories at that day associated with those seas captain delanos surprise might have deepened into some uneasiness had he not been a person of a singularly undistrustful good nature not liable except on extraordinary and repeated incentives and hardly then to indulge in personal alarms any way involving the imputation of malign evil in man
__label__MELVILLE whether in view of what humanity is capable such a trait implies along with a benevolent heart more than ordinary quickness and accuracy of intellectual perception may be left to the wise to determine
__label__MELVILLE but whatever misgivings might have obtruded on first seeing the stranger would almost in any seamans mind have been dissipated by observing that the ship in navigating into the harbor was drawing too near the land a sunken reef making out off her bow
__label__MELVILLE this seemed to prove her a stranger indeed not only to the sealer but the island consequently she could be no wonted freebooter on that ocean
__label__MELVILLE with no small interest captain delano continued to watch her a proceeding not much facilitated by the vapors partly mantling the hull through which the far matin light from her cabin streamed equivocally enough much like the sun by this time hemisphered on the rim of the horizon and apparently in company with the strange ship entering the harbor which wimpled by the same low creeping clouds showed not unlike a lima intriguantes one sinister eye peering across the plaza from the indian loop hole of her dusk saya y manta
__label__MELVILLE it might have been but a deception of the vapors but the longer the stranger was watched the more singular appeared her manoeuvres

__label__MELVILLE the wind which had breezed up a little during the night was now extremely light and baffling which the more increased the apparent uncertainty of her movements

__label__MELVILLE the same day and month and year his honor doctor juan martinez de rozas councilor of the royal audience of this kingdom and learned in the law of this intendency ordered the captain of the ship san dominick don benito cereno to appear which he did in his litter attended by the monk infelez of whom he received the oath which he took by god our lord and a sign of the cross under which he promised to tell the truth of whatever he should know and should be asked and being interrogated agreeably to the tenor of the act commencing the process he said that on the twentieth of may last he set sail with his ship from the port of valparaiso bound to that of callao loaded with the produce of the country beside thirty cases of hardware and one hundred and sixty blacks of both sexes mostly belonging to don alexandro aranda gentleman of the city of mendoza that the crew of the ship consisted of thirty six men beside the persons who went as passengers that the negroes were in part as follows

__label__MELVILLE that all the negroes slept upon deck as is customary in this navigation and none wore fetters because the owner his friend aranda told him that they were all tractable that on the seventh day after leaving port at three oclock in the morning all the spaniards being asleep except the two officers on the watch who were the boatswain juan robles and the carpenter juan bautista gayete and the helmsman and his boy the negroes revolted suddenly wounded dangerously the boatswain and the carpenter and successively killed eighteen men of those who were sleeping upon deck some with hand spikes and hatchets and others by throwing them alive overboard after tying them that of the spaniards upon deck they left about seven as he thinks alive and tied to manoeuvre the ship and three or four more who hid themselves remained also alive
__label__MELVILLE although in the act of revolt the negroes made themselves masters of the hatchway six or seven wounded went through it to the cockpit without any hindrance on their part that during __label__MELVILLE that omitting other events which daily happened and which can only serve uselessly to recall past misfortunes and conflicts after seventy three days navigation reckoned from the time __label__MELVILLE a pisgah view from the rock

__label__MELVILLE the frigate and ship flyaway

__label__MELVILLE sketch sixth
__label__MELVILLE barrington isle and the buccaneers
__label__MELVILLE let us all servile base subjection scorn and as we be sons of the earth so wide let us our fathers heritage divide and challenge to ourselves our portions dew of all the patrimony which a few hold on hugger mugger in their hand
__label__MELVILLE lords of the world and so will wander free whereso us listeth uncontrolld of any
__label__MELVILLE how bravely now we live how jocund how near the first inheritance without fear how free from little troubles
__label__MELVILLE near two centuries ago barrington isle was the resort of that famous wing of the west indian buccaneers which upon their repulse from the cuban waters crossing the isthmus of darien ravaged the pacific side of the spanish colonies and with the regularity and timing of a modern mail waylaid the royal treasure ships plying between manilla and acapulco
__label__MELVILLE after the toils of piratic war here they came to say their prayers enjoy their free and easies count their crackers from the cask their doubloons from the keg and measure their silks of asia with long toledos for their yard sticks
__label__MELVILLE as a secure retreat an undiscoverable hiding place no spot in those days could have been better fitted
__label__MELVILLE in the centre of a vast and silent sea but very little traversed surrounded by islands whose inhospitable aspect might well drive away the chance navigator and yet within a few days sail of the opulent countries which they made their prey the unmolested buccaneers found here that tranquillity which they fiercely denied to every civilized harbor in that part of the world
__label__MELVILLE here after stress of weather or a temporary drubbing at the hands of their vindictive foes or in swift flight with golden booty those old marauders came and lay snugly out of all harms reach
__label__MELVILLE but not only was the place a harbor of safety and a bower of ease but for utility in other things it was most admirable

__label__MELVILLE tortoises good for food trees good for fuel and long grass good for bedding abound here and there are pretty natural walks and several landscapes to be seen

__label__MELVILLE one had been a long sofa with back and arms just such a sofa as the poet gray might have loved to throw himself upon his crebillon in hand

__label__MELVILLE they never were here except their ships remained and they would most likely have slept on board

__label__MELVILLE at any rate long as those ruins of seats on barrington remain the most singular monuments are furnished to the fact that all of the buccaneers were not unmitigated monsters

__label__MELVILLE not very improbable after all
__label__MELVILLE for consider the vacillations of a man
__label__MELVILLE still strange as it may seem i must also abide by the more charitable thought namely that among these adventurers were some gentlemanly companionable souls capable of genuine tranquillity and virtue

__label__MELVILLE charless isle and the dog king

__label__MELVILLE sketch ninth
__label__MELVILLE hoods isle and the hermit oberlus
__label__MELVILLE that darkesome glen they enter where they find that cursed man low sitting on the ground musing full sadly in his sullein mind his griesly lockes long gronen and unbound disordered hong about his shoulders round and hid his face through which his hollow eyne lookt deadly dull and stared as astound his raw bone cheekes through penurie and pine were shronke into the jawes as he did never dine
__label__MELVILLE his garments nought but many ragged clouts with thornes together pind and patched reads the which his naked sides he wrapt abouts
__label__MELVILLE southeast of crossmans isle lies hoods isle or mccains beclouded isle and upon its south side is a vitreous cove with a wide strand of dark pounded black lava called black beach or oberluss landing
__label__MELVILLE it might fitly have been styled charons
__label__MELVILLE it received its name from a wild white creature who spent many years here in the person of a european bringing into this savage region qualities more diabolical than are to be found among any of the surrounding cannibals
__label__MELVILLE about half a century ago oberlus deserted at the above named island then as now a solitude
__label__MELVILLE he built himself a den of lava and clinkers about a mile from the landing subsequently called after him in a vale or expanded gulch containing here and there among the rocks about two acres of soil capable of rude cultivation the only place on the isle not too blasted for that purpose
__label__MELVILLE here he succeeded in raising a sort of degenerate potatoes and pumpkins which from time to time he exchanged with needy whalemen passing for spirits or dollars
__label__MELVILLE his appearance from all accounts was that of the victim of some malignant sorceress he seemed to have drunk of circes cup beast like rags insufficient to hide his nakedness his befreckled skin blistered by continual exposure to the sun nose flat countenance contorted heavy earthy hair and beard unshorn profuse and of fiery red
__label__MELVILLE he struck strangers much as if he were a volcanic creature thrown up by the same convulsion which exploded into sight the isle
__label__MELVILLE all bepatched and coiled asleep in his lonely lava den among the mountains he looked they say as a heaped drift of withered leaves torn from autumn trees and so left in some hidden nook by the whirling halt for an instant of a fierce night wind which then ruthlessly sweeps on somewhere else to repeat the capricious act
__label__MELVILLE it is also reported to have been the strangest sight this same oberlus of a sultry cloudy morning hidden under his shocking old black tarpaulin hat hoeing potatoes among the lava
__label__MELVILLE so warped and crooked was his strange nature that the very handle of his hoe seemed gradually to have shrunk and twisted in his grasp being a wretched bent stick elbowed more like a savages war sickle than a civilized hoe handle
__label__MELVILLE it was his mysterious custom upon a first encounter with a stranger ever to present his back possibly because that was his better side since it revealed the least
__label__MELVILLE if the encounter chanced in his garden as it sometimes did the new landed strangers going from the sea side straight through the gorge to hunt up the queer green grocer reported doing business here oberlus for a time hoed on unmindful of all greeting jovial or bland as the curious stranger would turn to face him the recluse hoe in hand as diligently would avert himself bowed over and sullenly revolving round his murphy hill
__label__MELVILLE thus far for hoeing
__label__MELVILLE when planting his whole aspect and all his gestures were so malevolently and uselessly sinister and secret that he seemed rather in act of dropping poison into wells than potatoes into soil
__label__MELVILLE but among his lesser and more harmless marvels was an idea he ever had that his visitors came equally as well led by longings to behold the mighty hermit oberlus in his royal state of solitude as simply to obtain potatoes or find whatever company might be upon a barren isle
__label__MELVILLE it seems incredible that such a being should possess such vanity a misanthrope be conceited but he really had his notion and upon the strength of it often gave himself amusing airs to captains
__label__MELVILLE but after all this is somewhat of a piece with the well known eccentricity of some convicts proud of that very hatefulness which makes them notorious
__label__MELVILLE at other times another unaccountable whim would seize him and he would long dodge advancing strangers round the clinkered corners of his hut sometimes like a stealthy bear he would slink through the withered thickets up the mountains and refuse to see the human face
__label__MELVILLE except his occasional visitors from the sea for a long period the only companions of oberlus were the crawling tortoises and he seemed more than degraded to their level having no desires for a time beyond theirs unless it were for the stupor brought on by drunkenness
__label__MELVILLE but sufficiently debased as he appeared there yet lurked in him only awaiting occasion for discovery a still further proneness
__label__MELVILLE indeed the sole superiority of oberlus over the tortoises was his possession of a larger capacity of degradation and along with that something like an intelligent will to it
__label__MELVILLE moreover what is about to be revealed perhaps will show that selfish ambition or the love of rule for its own sake far from being the peculiar infirmity of noble minds is shared by beings which have no mind at all
__label__MELVILLE no creatures are so selfishly tyrannical as some brutes as any one who has observed the tenants of the pasture must occasionally have observed
__label__MELVILLE this islands mine by sycorax my mother said oberlus to himself glaring round upon his haggard solitude
__label__MELVILLE by some means barter or theft for in those days ships at intervals still kept touching at his landing he obtained an old musket with a few charges of powder and ball
__label__MELVILLE possessed of arms he was stimulated to enterprise as a tiger that first feels the coming of its claws
__label__MELVILLE the long habit of sole dominion over every object round him his almost unbroken solitude his never encountering humanity except on terms of misanthropic independence or mercantile craftiness and even such encounters being comparatively but rare all this must have gradually nourished in him a vast idea of his own importance together with a pure animal sort of scorn for all the rest of the universe
__label__MELVILLE the unfortunate creole who enjoyed his brief term of royalty at charless isle was perhaps in some degree influenced by not unworthy motives such as prompt other adventurous spirits to lead colonists into distant regions and assume political preeminence over them

__label__MELVILLE but for this king oberlus and what shortly follows no shade of palliation can be given
__label__MELVILLE he acted out of mere delight in tyranny and cruelty by virtue of a quality in him inherited from sycorax his mother
__label__MELVILLE armed now with that shocking blunderbuss strong in the thought of being master of that horrid isle he panted for a chance to prove his potency upon the first specimen of humanity which should fall unbefriended into his hands
__label__MELVILLE nor was he long without it
__label__MELVILLE one day he spied a boat upon the beach with one man a negro standing by it

__label__MELVILLE the vessel had put in for wood and the boats crew had gone into the thickets for it

__label__MELVILLE throwing these on the beach they again went into the thickets while the negro proceeded to load the boat
__label__MELVILLE oberlus now makes all haste and accosts the negro who aghast at seeing any living being inhabiting such a solitude and especially so horrific a one immediately falls into a panic not at all lessened by the ursine suavity of oberlus who begs the favor of assisting him in his labors

__label__MELVILLE he refuses
__label__MELVILLE whereupon presenting his piece oberlus snaps at him

__label__MELVILLE but while the too vindictive smugglers were busy destroying his hut and garden oberlus makes his escape into the mountains and conceals himself there in impenetrable recesses only known to himself till the ship sails when he ventures back and by means of an old file which he sticks into a tree contrives to free himself from his handcuffs
__label__MELVILLE brooding among the ruins of his hut and the desolate clinkers and extinct volcanoes of this outcast isle the insulted misanthrope now meditates a signal revenge upon humanity but conceals his purposes

__label__MELVILLE of porters voyage into the pacific where they will recognize many sentences for expeditions sake derived verbatim from thence and incorporated here the main difference save a few passing reflections between the two accounts being that the present writer has added to porters facts accessory ones picked up in the pacific from reliable sources and where facts conflict has naturally preferred his own authorities to porters

__label__MELVILLE nor does the stranger wandering among other of the enchanted isles fail to stumble upon still other solitary abodes long abandoned to the tortoise and the lizard
__label__MELVILLE probably few parts of earth have in modern times sheltered so many solitaries
__label__MELVILLE the reason is that these isles are situated in a distant sea and the vessels which occasionally visit them are mostly all whalers or ships bound on dreary and protracted voyages exempting them in a good degree from both the oversight and the memory of human law
__label__MELVILLE such is the character of some commanders and some seamen that under these untoward circumstances it is quite impossible but that scenes of unpleasantness and discord should occur between them
__label__MELVILLE a sullen hatred of the tyrannic ship will seize the sailor and he gladly exchanges it for isles which though blighted as by a continual sirocco and burning breeze still offer him in their labyrinthine interior a retreat beyond the possibility of capture
__label__MELVILLE to flee the ship in any peruvian or chilian port even the smallest and most rustical is not unattended with great risk of apprehension not to speak of jaguars
__label__MELVILLE a reward of five pesos sends fifty dastardly spaniards into the wood who with long knives scour them day and night in eager hopes of securing their prey
__label__MELVILLE neither is it in general much easier to escape pursuit at the isles of polynesia
__label__MELVILLE those of them which have felt a civilizing influence present the same difficulty to the runaway with the peruvian ports the advanced natives being quite as mercenary and keen of knife and scent as the retrograde spaniards while owing to the bad odor in which all europeans lie in the minds of aboriginal savages who have chanced to hear aught of them to desert the ship among primitive polynesians is in most cases a hope not unforlorn
__label__MELVILLE hence the enchanted isles become the voluntary tarrying places of all sorts of refugees some of whom too sadly experience the fact that flight from tyranny does not of itself insure a safe asylum far less a happy home
__label__MELVILLE moreover it has not seldom happened that hermits have been made upon the isles by the accidents incident to tortoise hunting
__label__MELVILLE the interior of most of them is tangled and difficult of passage beyond description the air is sultry and stifling an intolerable thirst is provoked for which no running stream offers its kind relief
__label__MELVILLE in a few hours under an equatorial sun reduced by these causes to entire exhaustion woe betide the straggler at the enchanted isles
__label__MELVILLE their extent is such as to forbid an adequate search unless weeks are devoted to it
__label__MELVILLE the impatient ship waits a day or two when the missing man remaining undiscovered up goes a stake on the beach with a letter of regret and a keg of crackers and another of water tied to it and away sails the craft
__label__MELVILLE nor have there been wanting instances where the inhumanity of some captains has led them to wreak a secure revenge upon seamen who have given their caprice or pride some singular offense
__label__MELVILLE thrust ashore upon the scorching marl such mariners are abandoned to perish outright unless by solitary labors they succeed in discovering some precious dribblets of moisture oozing from a rock or stagnant in a mountain pool

__label__MELVILLE a large hair seal came upon the beach

__label__MELVILLE but men not endowed with courage equal to such desperate attempts find their only resource in forthwith seeking some watering place however precarious or scanty building a hut catching tortoises and birds and in all respects preparing for a hermit life till tide or time or a passing ship arrives to float them off
__label__MELVILLE at the foot of precipices on many of the isles small rude basins in the rocks are found partly filled with rotted rubbish or vegetable decay or overgrown with thickets and sometimes a little moist which upon examination reveal plain tokens of artificial instruments employed in hollowing them out by some poor castaway or still more miserable runaway

__label__MELVILLE the bell tower

__label__MELVILLE for in obedience to the loftiest behest of his soul he had done certain vital acts which had already lost him his worldly felicity and which he felt must in the end indirectly work him some still additional and not to be thought of woe
